33:1 These are the journeys of the sons of Israel, by which they came out of the land of Egypt by their armies, under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
33:2 Moses recorded their starting places according to their journeys by the command of the , and these are their journeys according to their starting places.
33:3 Now they journeyed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the sons of Israel started out boldly in the sight of all the Egyptians,
33:4 while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn whom the had fatally struck among them. The had also executed judgments against their gods.
33:5 Then the sons of Israel journeyed from Rameses and camped in Succoth.
33:6 They journeyed from Succoth and camped in Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
33:7 Then they journeyed from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon; and they camped before Migdol.
33:8 They journeyed from Pi-hahiroth and passed through the midst of the sea to the wilderness; and they went three days journey in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
33:9 They journeyed from Marah and came to Elim; and in Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
33:10 They journeyed from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
33:11 And they journeyed from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
33:12 They journeyed from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
33:13 They journeyed from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
33:14 And they journeyed from Alush and camped at Rephidim; now it was there that the people had no water to drink.
33:15 And they journeyed from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
33:16 They journeyed from the wilderness of Sinai, and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
33:17 They journeyed from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
33:18 They journeyed from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
33:19 They journeyed from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
33:20 They journeyed from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
33:21 They journeyed from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
33:22 They journeyed from Rissah and camped in Kehelathah.
33:23 They journeyed from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
33:24 They journeyed from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
33:25 They journeyed from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
33:26 They journeyed from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
33:27 They journeyed from Tahath and camped at Terah.
33:28 They journeyed from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
33:29 They journeyed from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
33:30 They journeyed from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
33:31 They journeyed from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
33:32 They journeyed from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
33:33 They journeyed from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
33:34 They journeyed from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
33:35 They journeyed from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
33:36 They journeyed from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
33:37 They journeyed from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom.
33:38 Then Aaron the priest went up to Mount Hor at the command of the , and died there in the fortieth year after the sons of Israel had come from the land of Egypt, on the first in the fifth month.
33:39 Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
33:40 Now the Canaanite, the king of Arad who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard about the coming of the sons of Israel.
33:41 Then they journeyed from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
33:42 They journeyed from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
33:43 They journeyed from Punon and camped at Oboth.
33:44 They journeyed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, at the border of Moab.
33:45 They journeyed from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
33:46 They journeyed from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
33:47 They journeyed from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
33:48 They journeyed from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan Jericho.
33:49 They camped by the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
33:50 Then the spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan Jericho, saying,
33:51 Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
33:52 you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from you, and destroy all their sculptures, destroy all their cast metal images, and eliminate all their high places;
33:53 and you shall take possession of the land and live in it, for I have given the land to you to possess it.
33:54 You shall maintain the land as an inheritance by lot according to your families; to the larger you shall give more inheritance, and to the smaller you shall give less inheritance. Wherever the lot falls to anyone, that shall be his. You shall pass on as an inheritance according to the tribes of your fathers.
33:55 But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from you, then it will come about that those whom you let remain of them like thorns in your eyes and like pricks in your sides, and they will trouble you in the land in which you live.
33:56 And just as I plan to do to them, I will do to you.
34:1 Then the spoke to Moses, saying,
34:2 Command the sons of Israel and say to them, When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance, land of Canaan according to its borders.
34:3 Your southern region shall extend from the wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom, and your southern border shall extend from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.
34:4 Then your border shall change direction from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim and continue to Zin, and its termination shall be to the south of Kadesh-barnea; and it shall reach Hazaraddar and continue to Azmon.
34:5 Then the border shall change direction from Azmon to the brook of Egypt, and its termination shall be the sea.
34:6 As for the western border, you shall have the Great Sea, that is, coastline; this shall be your western border.
34:7 And this shall be your northern border: you shall draw your boundary from the Great Sea to Mount Hor.
34:8 You shall draw a boundary from Mount Hor to the Lebo-hamath, and the termination of the border shall be at Zedad;
34:9 and the border shall proceed to Ziphron, and its termination shall be at Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern border.
34:10 For your eastern border you shall also draw a boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham,
34:11 and the border shall go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east of Ain; and the border shall go down and reach to the slope on the east side of the Sea of Chinnereth.
34:12 And the border shall go down to the Jordan, and its termination shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land according to its borders on all sides.
34:13 So Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying, This is the land that you are to possess by lot, which the has commanded to give to the nine and a half tribes.
34:14 For the tribe of the sons of Reuben have received according to their fathers households, and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to their fathers households, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their possession.
34:15 The two and a half tribes have received their possession across the Jordan Jericho, eastward toward the sunrise.
34:16 Then the spoke to Moses, saying,
34:17 These are the names of the men who shall assign the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun.
34:18 And you shall take one leader of each tribe to assign the land as an inheritance.
34:19 These are the names of the men: of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
34:20 Of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Samuel the son of Ammihud.
34:21 Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon.
34:22 And of the tribe of the sons of Dan, a leader, Bukki the son of Jogli.
34:23 Of the sons of Joseph: of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, a leader, Hanniel the son of Ephod.
34:24 Of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, a leader, Kemuel the son of Shiphtan.
34:25 Of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, a leader, Elizaphan the son of Parnach.
34:26 Of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, a leader, Paltiel the son of Azzan.
34:27 Of the tribe of the sons of Asher, a leader, Ahihud the son of Shelomi.
34:28 Of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, a leader, Pedahel the son of Ammihud.
34:29 These are the ones whom the commanded to apportion the inheritance to the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan.
35:1 Now the spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan Jericho, saying,
35:2 Command the sons of Israel that they give to the Levites from the inheritance of their possession cities to live in; and you shall give to the Levites pasture lands around the cities.
35:3 The cities shall be theirs to live in; and their pasture lands shall be for their cattle and for their equipment and for all their animals.
35:4 The pasture lands of the cities which you are to give to the Levites from the wall of the city outward a thousand cubits around.
35:5 You shall also measure outside the city on the east side two thousand cubits, on the south side two thousand cubits, on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits, with the city in the center. This shall become theirs as pasture lands for the cities.
35:6 The cities which you shall give to the Levites the six cities of refuge, which you shall provide for the one who commits manslaughter to flee to; and in addition to them you shall give forty-two cities.
35:7 The total of the cities which you are to give to the Levites forty-eight cities, together with their pasture lands.
35:8 As for the cities which you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel, you shall take more from the larger, and you shall take fewer from the smaller; each shall give some of his cities to the Levites in proportion to his inheritance which he possesses.
35:9 Then the spoke to Moses, saying,
35:10 Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
35:11 then you shall select for yourselves cities to be your cities of refuge, so that the one who commits manslaughter killing a person unintentionally may flee there.
35:12 The cities shall serve you as a refuge from the avenger, so that the one who commits manslaughter does not die until he stands before the congregation for trial.
35:13 So the cities which you are to provide shall be six cities of refuge for you.
35:14 You shall provide three cities across the Jordan, and three cities in the land of Canaan; they are to be cities of refuge.
35:15 These six cities shall be a refuge for the sons of Israel, for the stranger, and for the foreign resident among them; so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
35:16 But if he struck him with an iron object, so that he died, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
35:17 And if he struck him with a stone in the hand, by which he would die, and he did die, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
35:18 Or he struck him with a wooden object in the hand, by which he would die, and he did die, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
35:19 The blood avenger himself shall put the murderer to death; he himself shall put him to death when he meets him.
35:20 Now if he pushed him in hatred, or he threw at him with malicious intent, and he died,
35:21 or he struck him with his hand with hostility, and he died, the one who struck him must be put to death; he is a murderer. The blood avenger shall put the murderer to death when he meets him.
35:22 But if he pushed him suddenly, without hostility, or threw any object at him without malicious intent,
35:23 or had any deadly stone, and without looking he dropped on him so that he died, while he was not his enemy nor was he seeking to harm him,
35:24 then the congregation shall judge between the one who fatally struck and the blood avenger in accordance with these ordinances.
35:25 And the congregation shall save the one who committed manslaughter from the hand of the blood avenger, and the congregation shall return him to his city of refuge to which he fled; and he shall live in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
35:26 But if at any time he goes beyond the border of his city of refuge to which he flees,
35:27 and the blood avenger finds him outside the border of his city of refuge, and the blood avenger kills him, he will not be guilty of bloodshed,
35:28 because he should have remained in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. But after the death of the high priest the one who committed manslaughter may return to the land of his property.
35:29 These things shall be a statutory ordinance for you throughout your generations in all your dwelling places.
35:30 anyone kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death on the testimony of witnesses, but no person shall be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
35:31 Moreover, you shall not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is condemned to death, but he must be put to death.
35:32 And you shall not accept a ransom for one who has fled to his city of refuge, so that he may return to live in the land before the death of the priest.
35:33 So you shall not defile the land in which you ; for blood defiles the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed on it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
35:34 So you shall not defile the land in which you live, in the midst of which I dwell; for I the am dwelling in the midst of the sons of Israel.
36:1 Now the heads of the fathers of the family of the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of the sons of Joseph, came forward and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the fathers of the sons of Israel,
36:2 and they said, The commanded my lord to give the land by lot to the sons of Israel as an inheritance, and my lord was commanded by the to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.
36:3 But they marry one of the sons of the tribes of the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be withdrawn from the inheritance of our fathers and will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they belong; so it will be withdrawn from our allotted inheritance.
36:4 And when the jubilee of the sons of Israel takes place, then their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they belong; so their inheritance will be withdrawn from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.
36:5 Then Moses commanded the sons of Israel in accordance with the word of the , saying, The tribe of the sons of Joseph is right in statements.
36:6 This is what the has commanded regarding the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry whomever they wish; only they must marry within the family of the tribe of their father.
36:7 So no inheritance of the sons of Israel will be transferred from tribe to tribe, for the sons of Israel shall each retain possession of the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.
36:8 And every daughter who comes into possession of an inheritance of tribe of the sons of Israel shall marry one of the family of the tribe of her father, so that the sons of Israel may each possess the inheritance of his fathers.
36:9 So no inheritance will be transferred from one tribe to another tribe, for the tribes of the sons of Israel shall each retain possession of its own inheritance.
36:10 Just as the had commanded Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did:
36:11 Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad married their uncles sons.
36:12 They married from the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of the family of their father.
36:13 These are the commandments and the ordinances which the commanded to the sons of Israel through Moses in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan Jericho.
DEUTERONOMY
1:1 These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
1:2 It is eleven days from Horeb by way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.
1:3 In the fortieth year, on the first of the eleventh month, Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, in accordance with everything that the had commanded him to them,
1:4 after he had defeated Sihon the king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and in Edrei.
1:5 Across the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this Law, saying,
1:6 The our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, You have stayed long enough at this mountain.
1:7 Turn and set out on your journey, and go to the hill country of the Amorites, and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Negev, by the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.
1:8 See, I have placed the land before you; go in and take possession of the land which the swore to give to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and their descendants after them.
1:9 And I spoke to you at that time, saying, I am not able to endure you alone.
1:10 The your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are this day like the stars of heaven in number.
1:11 May the , the God of your fathers increase you a thousand times more than you are, and bless you, just as He has promised you!
1:12 How can I alone endure the burden and weight of you and your strife?
1:13 Obtain for yourselves men who are wise, discerning, and informed from your tribes, and I will appoint them as your heads.
1:14 And you answered me and said, The thing which you have said to do is good.
1:15 So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and informed men, and appointed them as heads over you, commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers for your tribes.
1:16 Then I ordered your judges at that time, saying, Hear between your fellow countrymen and judge righteously between a person and his fellow countryman, or the stranger who is with him.
1:17 You are not to show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You are not to be afraid of any person, for the judgment is Gods. The case that is too difficult for you, you shall bring to me, and I will hear it.
1:18 At that time I commanded you all the things that you were to do.
1:19 Then we set out from Horeb, and went all that great and terrible wilderness that you saw on the way to the hill country of the Amorites, just as the our God had commanded us; and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
1:20 And I said to you, You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the our God is about to give us.
1:21 See, the your God has placed the land before you; go up, take possession, just as the , the God of your fathers, has spoken to you. Do not fear or be dismayed.
1:22 Then all of you approached me and said, Let us send men ahead of us, so that they may spy out the land for us, and bring back to us word of the way by which we should go up, and the cities which we should enter.
1:23 The plan pleased me, and I took twelve of your men, one man for each tribe.
1:24 Then they turned and went up into the hill country, and came to the Valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.
1:25 And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. They also brought us back a report and said, The land that the our God is about to give us is good.
1:26 Yet you were unwilling to go up; instead you rebelled against the command of the your God;
1:27 and you grumbled in your tents and said, Because the hates us, He has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us.
1:28 Where can we go up? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, The people are bigger and taller than we; the cities are large and fortified to heaven. And besides, we saw the sons of the Anakim there.
1:29 But I said to you, Do not be terrified, nor fear them.
1:30 The your God, who goes before you, will Himself fight for you, just as He did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
1:31 and in the wilderness where you saw how the your God carried you, just as a man carries his son, on all of the road which you have walked until you came to this place.
1:32 Yet in spite of all this, you did not trust the your God,
1:33 who goes before you on way, to seek out a place for you to make camp, in the fire by night to show you the way by which you should go, and in the cloud by day.
1:34 Then the heard the sound of your words, and He was angry and swore an oath, saying,
1:35 Not one of these men, this evil generation, shall see the good land which I swore to give your fathers,
1:36 except Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and to him I will give the land on which he has set foot, and to his sons, because he has followed the fully.
1:37 The was angry with me also on your account, saying, Not even you shall enter there.
1:38 Joshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, shall himself enter there; encourage him, for he will give it to Israel as an inheritance.
1:39 Moreover, your little ones who, you said, would become plunder, and your sons, who this day have no knowledge of good and evil, shall enter there, and I will give it to them and they shall take possession of it.
1:40 But as for you, turn around and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.
1:41 Then you replied to me, We have sinned against the ; we ourselves will go up and fight, just as the our God commanded us. And every man of you strapped on his weapons of war, and you viewed it as easy to go up into the hill country.
1:42 But the said to me, Say to them, Do not go up nor fight, for I am not among you; otherwise you will be defeated by your enemies.
1:43 So I spoke to you, but you would not listen. Instead, you rebelled against the command of the , and acted presumptuously and went up into the hill country.
1:44 And the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do, and they scattered you from Seir to Hormah.
1:45 Then you returned and wept before the ; but the did not listen to your voice, nor pay attention to you.
1:46 So you remained at Kadesh for many days, the days that you spent .
2:1 Then we turned and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea, as the spoke to me, and we circled Mount Seir for many days.
2:2 And the spoke to me, saying,
2:3 You have circled this mountain long enough. turn north,
2:4 and command the people, saying, You are going to pass through the territory of your brothers the sons of Esau, who live in Seir; and they will be afraid of you. So be very careful;
2:5 do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, as much as a footprint, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.
2:6 You are to buy food from them with money so that you may eat, and you shall also purchase water from them with money so that you may drink.
2:7 For the your God has blessed you in all that you have done; He has known your wandering through this great wilderness. These forty years the your God has been with you; you have not lacked anything.
2:8 So we passed beyond our brothers the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the Arabah road, away from Elath and Ezion-geber. And we turned and passed through by the way of the wilderness of Moab.
2:9 Then the said to me, Do not attack Moab, nor provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as a possession.
2:10 (The Emim lived there previously, a people as great, numerous, and tall as the Anakim.
2:11 Like the Anakim, they too are regarded as Rephaim, but the Moabites call them Emim.
2:12 The Horites previously lived in Seir, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them, and settled in their place; just as Israel did to the land of their possession which the gave them.)
2:13 Now arise and cross over the Wadi Zered yourselves. So we crossed over the Wadi Zered.
2:14 Now the time that it took for us to come from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed over the Wadi Zered was thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of war perished from within the camp, just as the had sworn to them.
2:15 Indeed, the hand of the was against them, to destroy them from within the camp until they all perished.
2:16 So it came about, when all the men of war had finally perished from among the people,
2:17 that the spoke to me, saying,
2:18 Today you shall cross over Ar, the border of Moab.
2:19 When you come opposite the sons of Ammon, do not attack them nor provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as a possession.
2:20 (It is also regarded as the land of the Rephaim, Rephaim previously lived in it, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummin,
2:21 a people as great, numerous, and tall as the Anakim; but the destroyed them before them. And they dispossessed them and settled in their place,
2:22 just as He did for the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites from before them; they dispossessed them and settled in their place, even to this day.
2:23 And the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor, destroyed them and lived in their place.)
2:24 Arise, set out, and pass through the Valley of Arnon. Look! I have handed over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; start taking possession and plunge into battle with him.
2:25 This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the faces of people everywhere, who, when they hear the news of you, will tremble and be in anguish because of you.
2:26 So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
2:27 Let me pass through your land; I will travel only on the road. I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
2:28 You will sell me food for money so that I may eat, and give me water for money so that I may drink, only let me pass through on foot,
2:29 just as the sons of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross over the Jordan into the land that the our God is giving us.
2:30 But Sihon king of Heshbon was not willing for us to pass through his land; for the your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, in order to hand him over to you, as today.
2:31 And the said to me, See, I have begun to turn Sihon and his land over to you. Begin taking possession, so that you may possess his land.
2:32 Then Sihon came out with all his people to meet us in battle at Jahaz.
2:33 And the our God turned him over to us, and we defeated him with his sons and all his people.
2:34 So we captured all his cities at that time and utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city. We left no survivor.
2:35 We took only the animals as our plunder, and the spoils of the cities which we had captured.
2:36 From Aroer which is on the edge of the Valley of Arnon and the city which is in the valley, even to Gilead, there was no city that was too high for us; the our God turned it all over to us.
2:37 Only you did not go near the land of the sons of Ammon, all along the river Jabbok and the cities of the hill country, and wherever the our God had commanded us .
3:1 Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came out with all his people to meet us in battle at Edrei.
3:2 But the said to me, Do not fear him, for I have handed him and all his people and his land over to you; and you shall do to him just as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.
3:3 So the our God also handed over to us Og, king of Bashan, with all his people, and we struck them until no survivor was left.
3:4 We captured all his cities at that time; there was not a city which we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
3:5 All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many unwalled towns.
3:6 We utterly destroyed them, as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children of every city.
3:7 But all the animals and the spoils of the cities we took as our plunder.
3:8 So at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Valley of Arnon to Mount Hermon
3:9 (Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir):
3:10 all the cities of the plateau, all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
3:11 (For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Behold, his bed was a bed of iron; it is in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon. Its length was nine cubits, and its width four cubits by the usual cubit.)
3:12 So we took possession of this land at that time. From Aroer, which is by the Valley of Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead and its cities I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
3:13 The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, all the region of Argob. (As to all Bashan, it is called the land of Rephaim.
3:14 Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, , Bashan, and named it after his own name: Havvoth-jair, to this day.)
3:15 To Machir I gave Gilead.
3:16 To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave from Gilead even as far as the Valley of Arnon, the middle of the valley as a border, and as far as the river Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon;
3:17 the Arabah also, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth even as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, at the foot of the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
3:18 Then I commanded you at that time, saying, The your God has given you this land to possess it; all you valiant men shall cross over armed ahead of your brothers, the sons of Israel.
3:19 However, your wives, your little ones, and your livestock (I know that you have much livestock) shall remain in your cities which I have given you,
3:20 until the gives rest to your fellow countrymen as to you, and they also take possession of the land which the your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then you may return, each man to his possession which I have given you.
3:21 And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Your eyes have seen everything that the your God has done to these two kings; the will do the same to all the kingdoms into which you are about to cross.
3:22 Do not fear them, for the your God is the One fighting for you.
3:23 I also pleaded with the at that time, saying,
3:24 Lord , You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand; for what god in heaven or on earth who can do such works and mighty acts as Yours?
3:25 Please let me cross over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, that good hill country, and Lebanon.
3:26 But the was angry with me on your account, and would not listen to me; instead, the said to me, Enough! Do not speak to Me any more about this matter.
3:27 Go up to the top of Pisgah and raise your eyes to the west, the north, the south, and the east, and see with your eyes; for you shall not cross over this Jordan.
3:28 But commission Joshua and encourage him and strengthen him, for he shall go across leading this people, and he will give to them, as an inheritance, the land which you will see.
3:29 So we remained in the valley opposite Beth-peor.
4:1 Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the judgments which I am teaching you to perform, so that you will live and go in and take possession of the land which the , the God of your fathers, is giving you.
4:2 You shall not add to the word which I am commanding you, nor take away from it, so that you may keep the commandments of the your God which I am commanding you.
4:3 Your eyes have seen what the has done in the case of Baal-peor, for all the men who followed Baal-peor, the your God has destroyed them from among you.
4:4 But you who clung to the your God are alive today, every one of you.
4:5 See, I have taught you statutes and judgments just as the my God commanded me, that you are to do these things in the land where you are entering to take possession of it.
4:6 So keep and do , for that is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples who will hear all these statutes and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.
4:7 For what great nation that has a god so near to it as is the our God whenever we call on Him?
4:8 Or what great nation that has statutes and judgments as righteous as this whole Law which I am setting before you today?
4:9 Only be careful for yourself and watch over your soul diligently, so that you do not forget the things which your eyes have seen and they do not depart from your heart all the days of your life; but make them known to your sons and your grandsons.
4:10 the day you stood before the your God at Horeb, when the said to me, Assemble the people to Me, that I may have them hear My words so that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live on the earth, and that they may teach their children.
4:11 You came forward and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire to the heart of the heavens: darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
4:12 Then the spoke to you from the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, but you saw no form— only a voice.
4:13 So He declared to you His covenant which He commanded you to perform, , the Ten Commandments; and He wrote them on two tablets of stone.
4:14 The commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and judgments, so that you would perform them in the land where you are going over to take possession of it.
4:15 So be very careful yourselves, since you did not see any form on the day the spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire,
4:16 so that you do not act corruptly and make a carved image for yourselves in the form of any figure, a representation of male or female,
4:17 a representation of any animal that is on the earth, a representation of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
4:18 a representation of anything that crawls on the ground, a representation of any fish that is in the water below the earth.
4:19 And not to raise your eyes to heaven and look at the sun, the moon, and the stars, all the heavenly lights, and to be drawn away and worship them and serve them, which the your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole heaven.
4:20 But the has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, from Egypt, to be a people of His own possession, as today.
4:21 Now the was angry with me on your account, and He swore that I would not cross the Jordan, and that I would not enter the good land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance.
4:22 For I am going to die in this land; I am not crossing the Jordan, but you are going to cross, and you will take possession of this good land.
4:23 So be careful yourselves, that you do not forget the covenant of the your God which He made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image in the form of anything which the your God has commanded you.
4:24 For the your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
4:25 When you father children and grandchildren, and you grow old in the land, and you act corruptly, and make an idol in the form of anything, and do what is evil in the sight of the your God to provoke Him to anger,
4:26 I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today, that you will certainly perish quickly from the land where you are going over the Jordan to take possession of it. You will not live long on it, but will be utterly destroyed.
4:27 The will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the drives you.
4:28 There you will serve gods, the work of human hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear, nor eat nor smell .
4:29 But from there you will seek the your God, and you will find if you search for Him with all your heart and all your soul.
4:30 When you are in distress and all these things happen to you, in the latter days you will return to the your God and listen to His voice.
4:31 For the your God is a compassionate God; He will not abandon you nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant with your fathers which He swore to them.
4:32 Indeed, ask now about the earlier days that were before your time, since the day that God created mankind on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other. Has been done like this great thing, or has been heard like it?
4:33 Has people heard the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you have heard , and survived?
4:34 Or has a god ventured to go to take for himself a nation from within nation by trials, by signs and wonders, by war, by a mighty hand, by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, just as the your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
4:35 You were shown so that you might know that the , He is God; there is no other besides Him.
4:36 Out of the heavens He let you hear His voice to discipline you; and on earth He let you see His great fire, and you heard His words from the midst of the fire.
4:37 Because He loved your fathers, He chose their descendants after them. And He personally brought you from Egypt by His great power,
4:38 driving out from before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in to give you their land as an inheritance, as today.
4:39 Therefore know today, and take it to your heart, that the , He is God in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other.
4:40 So you shall keep His statutes and His commandments which I am giving you today, so that it may go well for you and for your children after you, and that you may live long on the land which the your God is giving you for all time.
4:41 Then Moses set apart three cities across the Jordan to the east,
4:42 for one to flee there who unintentionally killed his neighbor, without having hatred for him in time past; and by fleeing to one of these cities he might live:
4:43 Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
4:44 Now this is the Law which Moses set before the sons of Israel;
4:45 these are the testimonies and the statutes, and the ordinances which Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, when they came out of Egypt,
4:46 across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel defeated when they came out of Egypt.
4:47 And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites, who across the Jordan to the east,
4:48 from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Valley of Arnon, even as far as Mount Sion (that is, Hermon),
4:49 with all the Arabah across the Jordan to the east, even as far as the sea of the Arabah, at the foot of the slopes of Pisgah.
5:1 Now Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: Listen, Israel, to the statutes and ordinances which I am speaking today for you to hear, so that you may learn them and be careful to do them.
5:2 The our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
5:3 The did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, all of us who are alive here today.
5:4 The spoke with you face to face at the mountain from the midst of the fire,
5:5 I was standing between the and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the ; for you were afraid because of the fire, and you did not go up on the mountain. He said,
5:6 I am the your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
5:7 You shall have no other gods besides Me.
5:8 You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any likeness what is in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the water under the earth.
5:9 You shall not worship them nor serve them; for I, the your God, am a jealous God, inflicting the punishment of the fathers on the children, even on the third and fourth of those who hate Me,
5:10 but showing favor to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
5:11 You shall not take the name of the your God in vain, for the will not leave unpunished the one who takes His name in vain.
5:12 Keep the Sabbath day to treat it as holy, as the your God commanded you.
5:13 For six days you shall labor and do all your work,
5:14 but the seventh day is a Sabbath of the your God; you shall not do any work , you or your son or your daughter, or your male slave or your female slave, or your ox, your donkey, or any of your cattle, or your resident who stays with you, so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as well as you.
5:15 And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the your God brought you out of there by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm; therefore the your God commanded you to celebrate the Sabbath day.
5:16 Honor your father and your mother, just as the your God has commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged and that it may go well for you on the land which the your God is giving you.
5:17 You shall not murder.
5:18 You shall not commit adultery.
5:19 You shall not steal.
5:20 You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
5:21 You shall not covet your neighbors wife, nor desire your neighbors house, his field, his male slave or his female slave, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
5:22 These words the spoke to your whole assembly at the mountain from the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a great voice, and He added nothing more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
5:23 And when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you approached me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.
5:24 You said, Behold, the our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the midst of the fire; we have seen today that God speaks with mankind, yet he lives.
5:25 Now then, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us; if we hear the voice of the our God any longer, then we will die!
5:26 For who of humanity who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as we , and lived?
5:27 Go near and listen to everything that the our God says; then speak to us everything that the our God speaks to you, and we will listen and do .
5:28 Now the heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the said to me, I have heard the sound of the words of this people which they have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.
5:29 If only they had such a heart in them, to fear Me and keep all My commandments always, so that it would go well with them and with their sons forever!
5:30 Go, say to them, Return to your tents.
5:31 But as for you, stand here by Me, that I may speak to you all the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments which you shall teach them, so that they may follow in the land which I am giving them to possess.
5:32 So you shall be careful to do just as the your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.
5:33 You shall walk entirely in the way which the your God has commanded you, so that you may live and that it may be well for you, and that you may prolong days in the land which you will possess.
6:1 Now this is the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments which the your God has commanded to teach you, so that you may do in the land where you are going over to take possession of it,
6:2 so that you, your son, and your grandson will fear the your God, to keep all His statutes and His commandments which I command you, all the days of your life, and that your days may be prolonged.
6:3 Now Israel, you shall listen and be careful to do , so that it may go well for you and that you may increase greatly, just as the , the God of your fathers, has promised you, a land flowing with milk and honey.
6:4 Hear, Israel! The is our God, the is one!
6:5 And you shall love the your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
6:6 These words, which I am commanding you today, shall be on your heart.
6:7 And you shall repeat them diligently to your sons and speak of them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
6:8 You shall also tie them as a sign to your hand, and they shall be as frontlets on your forehead.
6:9 You shall also write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
6:10 Then it shall come about when the your God brings you into the land that He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you, great and splendid cities which you did not build,
6:11 and houses full of all good things which you did not fill, and carved cisterns which you did not carve out, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, and you eat and are satisfied,
6:12 be careful that you do not forget the who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
6:13 You shall fear the your God; and you shall worship Him and swear by His name.
6:14 You shall not follow other gods, any of the gods of the peoples who surround you,
6:15 for the your God in the midst of you is a jealous God; , or else the anger of the your God will be kindled against you, and He will wipe you off the face of the earth.
6:16 You shall not put the your God to the test, as you tested at Massah.
6:17 You shall diligently keep the commandments of the your God, and His provisions and His statutes which He has commanded you.
6:18 You shall do what is right and good in the sight of the , so that it may go well for you and that you may go in and take possession of the good land which the swore to your fathers,
6:19 by driving out all your enemies from you, as the has spoken.
6:20 When your son asks you in time to come, saying, What the provisions and the statutes and the judgments which the our God commanded you?
6:21 then you shall say to your son, We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
6:22 Moreover, the provided great and terrible signs and wonders before our eyes against Egypt, Pharaoh, and all his household;
6:23 He brought us out of there in order to bring us in, to give us the land which He had sworn to our fathers.
6:24 So the commanded us to follow all these statutes, to fear the our God for our good always and for our survival, as today.
6:25 And it will be righteousness for us if we are careful to follow all this commandment before the our God, just as He commanded us.
7:1 When the your God brings you into the land where you are entering to take possession of it, and He drives away many nations from before you, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than you,
7:2 and when the your God turns them over to you and you defeat them, you shall utterly destroy them. You shall not make a covenant with them nor be gracious to them.
7:3 Furthermore, you shall not intermarry with them: you shall not give your daughters to their sons, nor shall you take their daughters for your sons.
7:4 For they will turn your sons away from following Me, and they will serve other gods; then the anger of the will be kindled against you and He will quickly destroy you.
7:5 But this is what you shall do to them: you shall tear down their altars, smash their memorial stones, cut their Asherim to pieces, and burn their carved images in the fire.
7:6 For you are a holy people to the your God; the your God has chosen you to be a people for His personal possession out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
7:7 The did not make you His beloved nor choose you because you were greater in number than any of the peoples, since you were the fewest of all peoples,
7:8 but because the loved you and kept the oath which He swore to your forefathers, the brought you out by a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
7:9 Know therefore that the your God, He is God, the faithful God, who keeps His covenant and His faithfulness to a thousand generations for those who love Him and keep His commandments;
7:10 but He repays those who hate Him to their faces, to eliminate them; He will not hesitate toward him who hates Him, He will repay him to his face.
7:11 Therefore, you shall keep the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments which I am commanding you today, to do them.
7:12 Then it shall come about, because you listen to these judgments and keep and do them, that the your God will keep His covenant with you and His faithfulness which He swore to your forefathers.
7:13 And He will love you, bless you, and make you numerous; He will also bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain, your new wine, and your oil, the newborn of your cattle and the offspring of your flock, in the land which He swore to your forefathers to give you.
7:14 You shall be blessed above all peoples; there will be no sterile male or infertile female among you or among your cattle.
7:15 And the will remove from you all sickness; and He will not inflict upon you any of the harmful diseases of Egypt which you have known, but He will give them to all who hate you.
7:16 You shall consume all the peoples whom the your God will turn over to you; your eye shall not pity them, nor shall you serve their gods, for that a snare to you.
7:17 If you say in your heart, These nations are greater than I; how can I dispossess them?
7:18 you are not to be afraid of them; you shall remember well what the your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:
7:19 the great trials which your eyes saw and the signs and the wonders, and the mighty hand and the outstretched arm by which the your God brought you out. The your God will do the same to all the peoples of whom you are afraid.
7:20 Indeed, the your God will send the hornet against them, until those who are left and hide themselves from you perish.
7:21 You are not to be terrified of them, because the your God is in your midst, a great and awesome God.
7:22 And the your God will drive away these nations from you little by little; you will not be able to put an end to them quickly, otherwise the wild animals would become too numerous for you.
7:23 But the your God will turn them over to you, and will throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
7:24 And He will hand over their kings to you, so that you will eliminate their name from under heaven; no one will be able to stand against you until you have destroyed them.
7:25 The carved images of their gods you are to burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it for yourselves, or you will be trapped by it; for it is an abomination to the your God.
7:26 And you shall not bring an abomination into your house and become designated for destruction, like it; you are to utterly detest it, and you are to utterly loathe it, for it is something designated for destruction.
8:1 All the commandments that I am commanding you today you shall be careful to do, so that you may live and increase, and go in and take possession of the land which the swore to your forefathers.
8:2 And you shall remember all the way which the your God has led you in the wilderness these forty years, in order to humble you, putting you to the test, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep His commandments or not.
8:3 And He humbled you and let you go hungry, and fed you with the manna which you did not know, nor did your fathers know, in order to make you understand that man shall not live on bread alone, but man shall live on everything that comes out of the mouth of the .
8:4 Your clothing did not wear out on you, nor did your foot swell these forty years.
8:5 So you are to know in your heart that the your God was disciplining you just as a man disciplines his son.
8:6 Therefore, you shall keep the commandments of the your God, to walk in His ways and to fear Him.
8:7 For the your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of fountains and springs, flowing out in valleys and hills;
8:8 a land of wheat and barley, of vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey;
8:9 a land where you will eat food without shortage, in which you will not lack anything; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you can dig copper.
8:10 When you have eaten and are satisfied, you shall bless the your God for the good land which He has given you.
8:11 Be careful that you do not forget the your God by failing to keep His commandments, His ordinances, and His statutes which I am commanding you today;
8:12 otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, and you build good houses and live ,
8:13 and when your herds and your flocks increase, and your silver and gold increase, and everything that you have increases,
8:14 then your heart will become proud and you will forget the your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery;
8:15 He who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, fiery serpents and scorpions, and thirsty ground where there was no water; He who brought water for you out of the rock of flint.
8:16 In the wilderness He who fed you manna which your fathers did not know, in order to humble you and in order to put you to the test, to do good for you in the end.
8:17 Otherwise, you may say in your heart, My power and the strength of my hand made me this wealth.
8:18 But you are to remember the your God, for it is He who is giving you power to make wealth, in order to confirm His covenant which He swore to your fathers, as this day.
8:19 And it shall come about, if you ever forget the your God and follow other gods and serve and worship them, I testify against you today that you will certainly perish.
8:20 Like the nations that the eliminates from you, so you shall perish, because you would not listen to the voice of the your God.
9:1 Hear, Israel! You are crossing the Jordan today, to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified to heaven,
9:2 a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, whom you know and of whom you have heard , Who can stand against the sons of Anak?
9:3 So be aware today that it is the your God who is crossing over ahead of you a consuming fire. He will destroy them and He will subdue them before you, so that you may drive them out and eliminate them quickly, just as the has spoken to you.
9:4 Do not say in your heart when the your God has driven them away from you, Because of my righteousness the has brought me in to take possession of this land. Rather, because of the wickedness of these nations the is dispossessing them before you.
9:5 not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart you are going in to take possession of their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations the your God is driving them out from before you, and in order to confirm the oath which the swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
9:6 Know, then, that not because of your righteousness the your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stubborn people.
9:7 Remember, do not forget how you provoked the your God to anger in the wilderness; from the day that you left the land of Egypt until you arrived at this place, you have been rebellious against the .
9:8 Even at Horeb you provoked the to anger, and the was so angry with you that He would have destroyed you.
9:9 When I went up to the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which the made with you, then I remained on the mountain for forty days and nights; I neither ate bread nor drank water.
9:10 The gave me the two tablets of stone written by the finger of God; and on them all the words which the had spoken with you at the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.
9:11 It came about at the end of forty days and nights that the gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.
9:12 Then the said to me, Arise, go down from here quickly, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have behaved corruptly. They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them; they have made a cast metal image for themselves.
9:13 The also said to me, I have seen this people, and indeed, it is a stubborn people.
9:14 Leave Me alone, that I may destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven; and I will make of you a nation mightier and greater than they.
9:15 So I turned and came down from the mountain while the mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
9:16 And I saw that you had indeed sinned against the your God. You had made for yourselves a cast metal image of a calf; you had quickly turned aside from the way that the had commanded you.
9:17 So I took hold of the two tablets and threw them from my two hands, and smashed them to pieces before your eyes!
9:18 Then I fell down before the like the first , for forty days and nights; I neither ate bread nor drank water, because of all your sin which you had committed by doing what was evil in the sight of the , to provoke Him to anger.
9:19 For I was afraid of the anger and the rage with which the was angry with you so as to destroy you; but the listened to me that time as well.
9:20 The was also angry enough with Aaron to destroy him; so I also prayed for Aaron at the same time.
9:21 And I took your sinful which you had made, the calf, and burned it in the fire and crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust; and I threw its dust into the stream that came down from the mountain.
9:22 Then at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah you kept provoking the to anger.
9:23 And when the sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, Go up and take possession of the land which I have given you, you rebelled against the command of the your God; you neither trusted Him nor listened to His voice.
9:24 You have been rebellious toward the since the day I knew you.
9:25 So I fell down before the for the forty days and nights, which I did because the said He would destroy you.
9:26 And I prayed to the and said, Lord , do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance, whom You have redeemed through Your greatness, whom You have brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand!
9:27 Remember Your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not turn Your attention to the stubbornness of this people, or to their wickedness, or their sin.
9:28 Otherwise, the land from which You brought us will say, Since the was not able to bring them into the land which He had promised them, and since He hated them, He has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness!
9:29 Yet they are Your people, and Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power and Your outstretched arm.

10:5 Then I turned and came down from the mountain, and I put the tablets in the ark which I had made; and they are there, just as the commanded me.
10:6 (Now the sons of Israel set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and there he was buried, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.

10:13 to keep the commandments and His statutes which I am commanding you today for your good?
10:14 Behold, to the your God belong heaven and the highest heavens, the earth and all that is in it.
10:15 Yet the set His affection on your fathers, to love them, and He chose their descendants after them, you over all the peoples, as this day.
10:16 So circumcise your heart, and do not stiffen your neck any longer.
10:17 For the your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who does not show partiality, nor take a bribe.
10:18 He executes justice for the orphan and the widow, and shows His love for the stranger by giving him food and clothing.
10:19 So show your love for the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
10:20 You shall fear the your God; you shall serve Him, and cling to Him, and you shall swear by His name.
10:21 He is your glory and He is your God, who has done these great and awesome things for you which your eyes have seen.

11:7 but your own eyes have seen all the great work of the which He did.
11:8 You shall therefore keep every commandment which I am commanding you today, so that you may be strong and go in and take possession of the land into which you are about to cross to possess it;
11:9 and so that you may prolong days on the land which the swore to your fathers to give to them and to their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
11:10 For the land, into which you are entering to possess it, is not like the land of Egypt from which you came, where you used to sow your seed and water it by your foot like a vegetable garden.
11:11 But the land into which you are about to cross to possess it, a land of hills and valleys, drinks water from the rain of heaven,
11:12 a land for which the your God cares; the eyes of the your God are continually on it, from the beginning even to the end of the year.
11:13 And it shall come about, if you listen obediently to my commandments which I am commanding you today, to love the your God and to serve Him with all your heart and all your soul,
11:14 that He will provide rain for your land in its season, the early and late rain, so that you may gather your grain, your new wine, and your oil.
11:15 He will also provide grass in your field for your cattle, and you will eat and be satisfied.
11:16 Beware that your hearts are not easily deceived, and that you do not turn away and serve other gods, and worship them.
11:17 Otherwise, the anger of the will be kindled against you, and He will shut up the sky so that there will be no rain, and the ground will not yield its produce; then you will quickly perish from the good land which the is giving you.
11:18 You shall therefore take these words of mine to heart and to soul; and you shall tie them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets on your forehead.
11:19 You shall also teach them to your sons, speaking of them when you sit in your house, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
11:20 And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
11:21 so that your days and the days of your sons may be increased on the land which the swore to your fathers to give them, as long as the heavens are above the earth.
11:22 For if you are careful to keep all of this commandment which I am commanding you to do, to love the your God, to walk in all His ways and cling to Him,
11:23 then the will dispossess all these nations from you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.
11:24 Every place on which the sole of your foot steps shall be yours; your border will be from the wilderness to Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, as far as the western sea.
11:25 No one will stand against you; the your God will instill the dread of you and the fear of you in all the land on which you set foot, just as He has spoken to you.
11:26 See, I am placing before you today a blessing and a curse:
11:27 the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the your God, which I am commanding you today;
11:28 and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the your God, but turn aside from the way which I am commanding you today, by following other gods which you have not known.
11:29 And it shall come about, when the your God brings you into the land where you are entering to possess it, that you shall place the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
11:30 Are they not across the Jordan, west of the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
11:31 For you are about to cross the Jordan to go in to take possession of the land which the your God is giving you, and you shall possess it and live in it,
11:32 and you shall be careful to do all the statutes and the judgments which I am placing before you today.
12:1 These are the statutes and the judgments which you shall carefully follow in the land which the , the God of your fathers, has given you to possess as long as you live on the earth.
12:2 You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations whom you are going to dispossess serve their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
12:3 And you shall tear down their altars and smash their memorial stones to pieces, and burn their Asherim in the fire, and cut to pieces the carved images of their gods; and you shall eliminate their name from that place.
12:4 You shall not act this way toward the your God.
12:5 But you shall seek at the place which the your God will choose from all your tribes, to establish His name there for His dwelling, and you shall come there.
12:6 You shall bring there your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the contribution of your hand, your vowed offerings, your voluntary offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.
12:7 There you and your households shall eat before the your God, and rejoice in all your undertakings in which the your God has blessed you.
12:8 You shall not do at all what we are doing here today, everyone whatever is right in his eyes;
12:9 for you have not as yet come to the resting place and the inheritance which the your God is giving you.
12:10 When you cross the Jordan and live in the land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance, and He gives you rest from all your enemies around so that you live in security,
12:11 then it shall come about that the place in which the your God will choose for His name to dwell, there you shall bring everything that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and all your choice vowed offerings which you will vow to the .
12:12 And you shall rejoice before the your God, you and your sons and daughters, your male and female slaves, and the Levite who is within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance with you.
12:13 Be careful that you do not offer your burnt offerings in any place that you see,
12:14 but in the place which the chooses in one of your tribes: there you shall offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do everything that I command you.
12:15 However, you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates, whatever you desire, according to the blessing of the your God which He has given you; the unclean and the clean may eat it, as the gazelle and the deer.
12:16 Only you shall not eat the blood; you are to pour it out on the ground like water.
12:17 You are not allowed to eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, new wine, or oil, or the firstborn of your herd or flock, or any of your vowed offerings which you vow, or your voluntary offerings, or the contribution of your hand.
12:18 But you shall eat them before the your God in the place which the your God will choose, you and your son and daughter, and your male and female slaves, and the Levite who is within your gates; and you shall rejoice before the your God in all your undertakings.
12:19 Be careful that you do not abandon the Levite as long as you live in your land.
12:20 When the your God extends your border as He has promised you, and you say, I will eat meat, because you desire to eat meat, you may eat meat, whatever you desire.
12:21 If the place where the your God chooses to put His name is too far from you, then you may slaughter from your herd and flock which the has given you, as I have commanded you; and you may eat within your gates whatever you desire.
12:22 Just as a gazelle or a deer is eaten, so you may eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it.
12:23 Only be sure not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the flesh.
12:24 You shall not eat it; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
12:25 You shall not eat it, so that it may go well for you and your sons after you, since you will be doing what is right in the sight of the .
12:26 Only your holy things which you may have and your vowed offerings, you shall take and go to the place which the chooses.
12:27 And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, on the altar of the your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the your God, and you shall eat the flesh.
12:28 Be careful and listen to all these words which I am commanding you, so that it may go well for you and your sons after you forever, for you will be doing what is good and right in the sight of the your God.
12:29 When the your God cuts off from you the nations which you are going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,
12:30 be careful that you are not ensnared to follow them, after they are destroyed from your presence, and that you do not inquire about their gods, saying, How do these nations serve their gods, that I also may do likewise?
12:31 You shall not behave this way toward the your God, because every abominable act which the hates, they have done for their gods; for they even burn their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
12:32 Whatever I command you, you shall be careful to do; you shall not add to nor take away from it.
13:1 If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
13:2 and the sign or the wonder comes , of which he spoke to you, saying, Lets follow other gods (whom you have not known) and lets serve them,
13:3 you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer of dreams; for the your God is testing you to find out whether you love the your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
13:4 You shall follow the your God and fear Him; and you shall keep His commandments, listen to His voice, serve Him, and cling to Him.
13:5 But that prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he has spoken falsely against the your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to drive you from the way in which the your God commanded you to walk. So you shall eliminate the evil from among you.
13:6 If your brother, your mothers son, or your son or daughter, or the wife you cherish, or your friend who is like your own soul, entices you secretly, saying, Lets go and serve other gods (whom neither you nor your fathers have known,
13:7 of the gods of the peoples who are around you, near you, or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other end),
13:8 you shall not consent to him or listen to him; and your eye shall not pity him, nor shall you spare or conceal him.
13:9 Instead, you shall most certainly kill him; your hand shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.
13:10 So you shall stone him to death, because he has attempted to drive you away from the your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
13:11 Then all Israel will hear and be afraid, and will not do such a wicked thing among you again.
13:12 If you hear in one of your cities, which the your God is giving you to live in, saying
13:13 some worthless men have gone out from among you and have seduced the inhabitants of their city, saying, Lets go and serve other gods (whom you have not known),
13:14 then you shall investigate, search out, and inquire thoroughly. And if it is true the matter is certain that this abomination has been committed among you,
13:15 you shall most certainly strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword. Utterly destroy it and all who are in it and its cattle, with the edge of the sword.
13:16 Then you shall gather all its plunder into the middle of its public square, and burn the city and all its plunder with fire as a whole burnt offering to the your God; and it shall be a ruin forever. It shall never be rebuilt.
13:17 Nothing at all from what is designated for destruction is to cling to your hand, in order that the may turn from His burning anger and show mercy to you, and have compassion on you and make you increase, just as He has sworn to your fathers,
13:18 if you will listen to the voice of the your God, keeping all His commandments which I am commanding you today, and doing what is right in the sight of the your God.
14:1 You are sons of the your God; you shall not cut yourselves nor shave a bald spot above your forehead for the dead.
14:2 For you are a holy people to the your God, and the has chosen you to be a people for His personal possession out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
14:3 You shall not eat any detestable thing.
14:4 These are the animals that you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
14:5 the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
14:6 And any animal that has a divided hoof and has hoofs split in two, chews the cud, among the animals, that animal you may eat.
14:7 However, you are not to eat these among the ones that chew the cud, or among those that have the hoof divided in two: the camel, the rabbit, and the rock hyrax, for though they chew the cud, they do not have a divided hoof; they are unclean to you.
14:8 And the pig, because it has a divided hoof but not the cud, it is unclean for you. You shall not eat any of their flesh, nor touch their carcasses.
14:9 These you may eat of everything that is in the water: anything that has fins and scales you may eat,
14:10 but anything that does not have fins and scales, you shall not eat; it is unclean for you.
14:11 You may eat any clean bird.
14:12 But these are the ones that you shall not eat: the eagle and the vulture and the buzzard,
14:13 and the red kite, the falcon, and the kite in their kinds,
14:14 and every raven in its kind,
14:15 and the ostrich, the owl, the seagull, and the hawk in their kinds,
14:16 the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
14:17 the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
14:18 the stork, and the heron in their kinds, and the hoopoe and the bat.
14:19 And all the swarming insects with wings are unclean to you; they shall not be eaten.
14:20 You may eat any clean bird.
14:21 You shall not eat anything which dies . You may give it to the stranger who is in your town, so that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a stranger; for you are a holy people to the your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mothers milk.
14:22 You shall certainly tithe all the produce from what you sow, which comes from the field every year.
14:23 You shall eat in the presence of the your God, at the place where He chooses to establish His name, the tithe of your grain, your new wine, your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and your flock, so that you may learn to fear the your God always.
14:24 But if the distance is so great for you that you are not able to bring , since the place where the your God chooses to set His name is too far away from you when the your God blesses you,
14:25 then you shall exchange for money, and bind the money in your hand and go to the place which the your God chooses.
14:26 And you may spend the money on whatever your heart desires: on oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink, or whatever your heart desires; and there you shall eat in the presence of the your God and rejoice, you and your household.
14:27 Also you shall not neglect the Levite who is in your town, for he has no portion or inheritance among you.
14:28 At the end of every third year you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year, and you shall deposit in your town.
14:29 And the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance among you, and the stranger, the orphan, and the widow who are in your town, shall come and eat and be satisfied, in order that the your God may bless you in all the work of your hand which you do.
15:1 At the end of seven years you shall grant a release of debts.
15:2 And this is the regulation for the release of debts: every creditor is to forgive what he has loaned to his neighbor; he shall not require it of his neighbor and his brother, because the release has been proclaimed.
15:3 From a foreigner you may require , but your hand shall forgive whatever of yours is with your brother.
15:4 However, there will be no poor among you, since the will certainly bless you in the land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,
15:5 if only you listen obediently to the voice of the your God, to follow carefully all this commandment which I am commanding you today.
15:6 For the your God will have blessed you just as He has promised you, and you will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow; and you will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
15:7 If there is a poor person among you, one of your brothers, in any of your towns in your land which the your God is giving you, you shall not harden your heart, nor close your hand from your poor brother;
15:8 but you shall fully open your hand to him, and generously lend him enough for his need whatever he lacks.
15:9 Be careful that there is no mean-spirited thought in your heart, such as, The seventh year, the year of release of debts, is near, and your eye is malicious toward your poor brother, and you give him nothing; then he may cry out to the against you, and it will be a sin in you.
15:10 You shall generously give to him, and your heart shall not be grudging when you give to him, because for this thing the your God will bless you in all your work, and in all your undertakings.
15:11 For the poor will not cease to exist in the land; therefore I am commanding you, saying, You shall fully open your hand to your brother, to your needy and poor in your land.
15:12 If your fellow countryman, a Hebrew man or woman, is sold to you, then he shall serve you for six years, but in the seventh year you shall set him free.
15:13 And when you set him free, you shall not send him away empty-handed.
15:14 You shall give generously to him from your flock, your threshing floor, and from your wine vat; you shall give to him as the your God has blessed you.
15:15 And you are to remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the your God redeemed you; therefore I am commanding this of you today.
15:16 But it shall come about, if he says to you, I will not leave you, because he loves you and your household, since he is doing well with you,
15:17 then you shall take an awl and pierce it through his ear into the door, and he shall be your servant permanently. You shall also do the same to your female slave.
15:18 It shall not seem difficult for you when you set him free, because he has given you six years double the service of a hired worker; so the your God will bless you in whatever you do.
15:19 You shall consecrate to the your God all the firstborn males that are born in your herd and in your flock; you shall not work with the firstborn of your herd, nor shear the firstborn of your flock.
