15:20 You and your household shall eat it every year before the your God in the place which the chooses.
15:21 But if it has any impairment, a limp, or blindness, any serious impairment, you shall not sacrifice it to the your God.
15:22 You shall eat it within your gates; the unclean and the clean alike , as a gazelle or a deer.
15:23 Only you shall not eat its blood; you are to pour it out on the ground like water.
16:1 Observe the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to the your God, for in the month of Abib the your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
16:2 You shall sacrifice the Passover to the your God the flock and the herd, in the place where the chooses to establish His name.
16:3 You shall not eat leavened bread with it; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction (for you came out of the land of Egypt in a hurry), so that you will remember the day when you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
16:4 For seven days no leaven shall be seen with you in your entire territory, and none of the meat which you sacrifice on the evening of the first day shall be left overnight until the morning.
16:5 You are not allowed to sacrifice the Passover in any of your towns which the your God is giving you;
16:6 but at the place where the your God chooses to establish His name, you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening at sunset, at the time that you came out of Egypt.
16:7 You shall cook and eat in the place which the your God chooses. In the morning you are to return to your tents.
16:8 For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a festive assembly to the your God; you shall do no work .
16:9 You shall count seven weeks for yourself; you shall begin to count seven weeks from you begin the sickle to the standing grain.
16:10 Then you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks to the your God with a voluntary offering of your hand in a proportional amount, which you shall give just as the your God blesses you;
16:11 and you shall rejoice before the your God, you, your son and your daughter, and your male and female slaves, and the Levite who is in your town, and the stranger, the orphan, and the widow who are in your midst, at the place where the your God chooses to establish His name.
16:12 You shall also remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall be careful and comply with these statutes.
16:13 You shall celebrate the Feast of Booths for seven days when you have gathered in from your threshing floor and your wine vat;
16:14 and you shall rejoice in your feast, you, your son and your daughter, and your male and female slaves, and the Levite, the stranger, the orphan, and the widow who are in your towns.
16:15 For seven days you shall celebrate a feast to the your God in the place which the chooses, because the your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, so that you will be altogether joyful.
16:16 Three times a year all your males shall appear before the your God at the place which He chooses: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Booths; and they are not to appear before the empty-handed.
16:17 Everyone shall give as he is able, in accordance with the blessing of the your God which He has given you.
16:18 You shall appoint for yourself judges and officers in all your towns which the your God is giving you, according to your tribes, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
16:19 You shall not distort justice, you shall not show partiality; and you shall not accept a bribe, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and distorts the words of the righteous.
16:20 Justice, justice, you shall pursue, so that you may live and possess the land which the your God is giving you.
16:21 You shall not plant for yourself an Asherah of any kind of tree beside the altar of the your God, which you shall make for yourself.
16:22 And you shall not set up for yourself a memorial stone, which the your God hates.
17:1 You shall not sacrifice to the your God an ox or a sheep which has a blemish any defect, for that is a detestable thing to the your God.
17:2 If there is found in your midst, in any of your towns which the your God is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the sight of the your God, by violating His covenant,
17:3 and has gone and served other gods and worshiped them, or the sun, the moon, or any of the heavenly lights, which I have commanded not to do,
17:4 and if it is reported to you and you have heard , then you shall investigate thoroughly. And if it is true and the report is trustworthy that this detestable thing has been done in Israel,
17:5 then you are to bring out to your gates that man or woman who has done this evil deed, , the man or the woman, and you shall stone them to death.
17:6 On the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses, the condemned shall be put to death; he shall not be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
17:7 The hands of the witnesses shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So you shall eliminate the evil from your midst.
17:8 If a case is too difficult for you to decide, between one kind of homicide or another, between one kind of lawsuit or another, and between one kind of assault or another, cases of dispute in your courts, then you shall arise and go up to the place which the your God chooses.
17:9 So you shall come to the Levitical priests or the judge who is in those days, and you shall inquire and they will declare to you the verdict.
17:10 Then you shall act in accordance with the terms of the verdict which they declare to you from that place which the chooses; and you shall be careful to act in accordance with everything that they instruct you .
17:11 In accordance with the terms of the law about which they instruct you, and in accordance with the verdict which they tell you, you shall act; you shall not turn aside from the word which they declare to you, to the right or the left.
17:12 But the person who acts insolently by not listening to the priest who stands there to serve the your God, nor to the judge, that person shall die; so you shall eliminate the evil from Israel.
17:13 Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and will not act insolently again.
17:14 When you enter the land which the your God is giving you, and you take possession of it and live in it, and you say, I will appoint a king over me like all the nations who are around me,
17:15 you shall in fact appoint a king over you whom the your God chooses. from among your countrymen you shall appoint as king over yourselves; you may not put a foreigner over yourselves, who is not your countryman.
17:16 In any case, he is not to acquire many horses for himself, nor shall he make the people return to Egypt in order to acquire many horses, since the has said to you, You shall never again return that way.
17:17 And he shall not acquire many wives for himself, so that his heart does not turn away; nor shall he greatly increase silver and gold for himself.
17:18 Now it shall come about, when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write for himself a copy of this Law on a scroll in the presence of the Levitical priests.
17:19 And it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he will learn to fear the his God, by carefully following all the words of this Law and these statutes,
17:20 so that his heart will not be haughty toward his countrymen, and that he will not turn away from the commandment to the right or the left, so that he and his sons may live long in his kingdom in the midst of Israel.
18:1 The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, shall not have a portion or inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings by fire and His property.
18:2 They shall not have an inheritance among their countrymen; the is their inheritance, as He promised them.
18:3 Now this shall be the priests portion from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, either an ox or a sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
18:4 You shall give him the first fruits of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first fleece of your sheep.
18:5 For the your God has chosen him and his sons from all your tribes, to stand to serve in the name of the always.
18:6 Now if a Levite comes from any of your towns throughout Israel where he resides, and he comes whenever he desires to the place which the chooses,
18:7 then he shall serve in the name of the his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the .
18:8 They shall eat equal portions, except for from the sale of their fathers .
18:9 When you enter the land which the your God is giving you, you shall not learn to imitate the detestable things of those nations.
18:10 There shall not be found among you who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, one who uses divination, a soothsayer, one who interprets omens, or a sorcerer,
18:11 or one who casts a spell, or a medium, or a spiritist, or one who consults the dead.
18:12 For whoever does these things is detestable to the ; and because of these detestable things the your God is going to drive them out before you.
18:13 You are to be blameless before the your God.
18:14 For these nations, which you are going to dispossess, listen to soothsayers and diviners, but as for you, the your God has not allowed you so.
18:15 The your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your countrymen; to him you shall listen.
18:16 in accordance with everything that you asked of the your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, Do not let me hear the voice of the my God again, and do not let me see this great fire anymore, or I will die!
18:17 And the said to me, They have spoken well.
18:18 I will raise up for them a prophet from among their countrymen like you, and I will put My words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them everything that I command him.
18:19 And it shall come about that whoever does not listen to My words which he speaks in My name, I Myself will require of him.
18:20 But the prophet who speaks a word presumptuously in My name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or which he speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
18:21 And if you say in your heart, How will we recognize the word which the has not spoken?
18:22 When the prophet speaks in the name of the , and the thing does not happen or come , that is the thing which the has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously; you are not to be afraid of him.
19:1 When the your God cuts off the nations whose land the your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and settle in their cities and in their houses,
19:2 you shall set aside for yourself three cities in the midst of your land which the your God is giving you to possess.
19:3 You shall prepare the roads for yourself, and divide into three regions the territory of your land which the your God will give you as an inheritance, so that anyone who commits manslaughter may flee there.
19:4 Now this is the case of the one who commits manslaughter, who may flee there and live: when he kills his friend unintentionally, not hating him previously—
19:5 as when goes into the forest with his friend to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to cut down the tree, and the iron slips off the handle and strikes his friend so that he dies—he may flee to one of these cities and live.
19:6 Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue him in the heat of his anger, and overtake him because the way is long, and take his life, though he was not sentenced to death since he had not hated him previously.
19:7 Therefore I command you, saying, You shall set aside for yourself three cities.
19:8 And if the your God enlarges your territory, just as He has sworn to your fathers, and gives you all the land that He promised to give your fathers—
19:9 if you carefully follow all of this commandment which I am commanding you today, to love the your God, and to walk in His ways always—then you shall add three more cities for yourself, besides these three.
19:10 So innocent blood will not be shed in the midst of your land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance, and guilt for bloodshed will be on you.
19:11 But if there is a person who hates his neighbor, and waits in ambush for him and rises up against him and strikes him so that he dies, and he flees to one of these cities,
19:12 then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there, and hand him over to the avenger of blood, so that he may die.
19:13 You shall not pity him, but you shall eliminate the guilt for the bloodshed of the innocent from Israel, so that it may go well for you.
19:14 You shall not displace your neighbors boundary marker, which the ancestors have set, in your inheritance which you will inherit in the land that the your God is giving you to possess.
19:15 A single witness shall not rise up against a person regarding any wrongdoing or any sin that he commits; on the testimony of two or three witnesses a matter shall be confirmed.
19:16 If a malicious witness rises up against a person to testify against him of wrongdoing,
19:17 then both people who have the dispute shall stand before the , before the priests and the judges who will be in those days.
19:18 And the judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness is a false witness he has testified against his brother falsely,
19:19 then you shall do to him just as he had planned to do to his brother. So you shall eliminate the evil from among you.
19:20 And the rest will hear and be afraid, and will never again do such an evil thing among you.
19:21 So you shall not show pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
20:1 When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses, chariots, people more numerous than you, do not be afraid of them; for the your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt, is with you.
20:2 When you are approaching the battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people.
20:3 He shall say to them, Hear, Israel, you are approaching the battle against your enemies today. Do not be fainthearted. Do not be afraid, or panic, or be terrified by them,
20:4 for the your God is the One who is going with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.
20:5 The officers also shall speak to the people, saying, Who is the man that has built a new house but has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, otherwise he might die in the battle and another man would dedicate it.
20:6 And who is the man that has planted a vineyard but has not put it to use? Let him go and return to his house, otherwise he might die in the battle and another man would put it to use.
20:7 And who is the man that is betrothed to a woman and has not married her? Let him go and return to his house, otherwise he might die in the battle and another man would marry her.
20:8 Then the officers shall speak further to the people and say, Who is the man that is afraid and fainthearted? Let him go and return to his house, so that he does not make his brothers hearts melt like his heart!
20:9 And when the officers have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of armies at the head of the people.
20:10 When you approach a city to fight against it, you shall offer it terms of peace.
20:11 And if it agrees to make peace with you and opens to you, then all the people who are found in it shall become your forced labor and serve you.
20:12 However, if it does not make peace with you, but makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.
20:13 When the your God gives it into your hand, you shall strike all the men in it with the edge of the sword.
20:14 However, the women, the children, the animals, and everything that is in the city, all of its spoils, you shall take as plunder for yourself; and you shall use the spoils of your enemies which the your God has given you.
20:15 This is what you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations nearby.
20:16 Only in the cities of these peoples that the your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall not leave anything that breathes alive.
20:17 Instead, you shall utterly destroy them, the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, just as the your God has commanded you,
20:18 so that they will not teach you to do all the same detestable practices of theirs which they have done for their gods, by which you would sin against the your God.
20:19 When you besiege a city for a long time, to make war against it in order to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them; for you may eat from them, so you shall not cut them down. For is the tree of the field a human, that it should be besieged by you?
20:20 Only the trees that you know are not fruit trees you shall destroy and cut down, so that you may construct siegeworks against the city that is making war against you until it falls.
21:1 If a person who has been killed is found lying in the open country in the land which the your God is giving you to possess, it is not known who struck him,
21:2 then your elders and your judges shall go out and measure to the cities which are around the one who was killed.
21:3 And it shall be that the city which is nearest to the person killed, that is, that the elders of that city shall take a heifer of the herd that has not been worked and has not pulled in a yoke;
21:4 and the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a valley with running water, which has not been plowed or sown, and they shall break the heifers neck there in the valley.
21:5 Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, because the your God has chosen them to serve Him and to bless in the name of the ; and every dispute and violent crime shall be settled by them.
21:6 And all the elders of that city which is nearest to the person killed shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley;
21:7 and they shall respond and say, Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see .
21:8 Forgive Your people Israel whom You have redeemed, , and do not place the guilt for innocent blood in the midst of Your people Israel. And the guilt for bloodshed shall be forgiven them.
21:9 So you shall remove the guilt for innocent blood from your midst, when you do what is right in the eyes of the .
21:10 When you go out to battle against your enemies, and the your God hands them over to you and you take them away captive,
21:11 and you see among the captives a beautiful woman, and are strongly attracted to her and would take her as a wife for yourself,
21:12 then you shall bring her into your home, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails.
21:13 She shall also remove the clothes of her captivity and shall remain in your house, and weep for her father and mother a full month; and after that you may have relations with her and become her husband and she shall be your wife.
21:14 But it shall be, if you are not pleased with her, then you shall let her go wherever she wishes; and you certainly shall not sell her for money, you shall not treat her as merchandise, since you have humiliated her.
21:15 If a man has two wives, the one loved and the other unloved, and the loved and the unloved have borne him sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the unloved,
21:16 then it shall be on the day that he wills what he owns as an inheritance to his sons, he is not allowed to treat the son of the loved as the firstborn, at the expense of the son of the unloved, the firstborn .
21:17 On the contrary, he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the unloved , by giving him a double portion of everything that he owns, for he the beginning of his strength; to him belongs the right of the firstborn.
21:18 If any person has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey his father or his mother, and when they discipline him, he does not listen to them,
21:19 then his father and mother shall seize him, and bring him out to the elders of his city at the gateway of his hometown.
21:20 And they shall say to the elders of his city, This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he does not obey us, he is thoughtless and given to drinking.
21:21 Then all the men of his city shall stone him to death; so you shall eliminate the evil from your midst, and all Israel will hear and fear.
21:22 Now if a person has committed a sin a sentence of death and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,
21:23 his body is not to be left overnight on the tree, but you shall certainly bury him on the same day (for he who is hanged is cursed of God), so that you do not defile your land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance.
22:1 You shall not see your countrymans ox or his sheep straying away, and avoid them; you shall certainly bring them back to your countryman.
22:2 And if your countryman is not near you, or if you do not know him, then you shall bring it to your house, and it shall remain with you until your countryman looks for it; then you shall restore it to him.
22:3 You shall also do this with his donkey, and you shall do the same with his garment, and you shall do likewise with any lost property of your countryman, which has been lost by him and you have found. You are not allowed to avoid .
22:4 You shall not see your countrymans donkey or his ox fallen down on the road, and avoid them; you shall certainly help him raise up.
22:5 A woman shall not wear a mans clothing, nor shall a man put on a womans clothing; for whoever does these things is an abomination to the your God.
22:6 If you happen to come upon a birds nest along the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs , and the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young;
22:7 you shall certainly let the mother go, but the young you may take for yourself, in order that it may go well for you and that you may prolong your days.
22:8 When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you will not bring guilt for bloodshed on your house if anyone falls from it.
22:9 You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, otherwise all the produce of the seed which you have sown and the yield of the vineyard will be forfeited to the sanctuary.
22:10 You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
22:11 You shall not wear a material of wool and linen combined together.
22:12 You shall make yourself tassels on the four corners of your garment with which you cover yourself.
22:13 If any man takes a wife and goes in to her and turns against her,
22:14 and he charges her with shameful behavior and publicly defames her, and says, I took this woman, when I came near her, I did not find her to have evidence of virginity,
22:15 then the girls father and her mother shall take and bring out the evidence of the girls virginity to the elders of the city at the gate.
22:16 And the girls father shall say to the elders, I gave my daughter to this man as a wife, but he turned against her;
22:17 and behold, he has charged her with shameful behavior, saying, I did not find your daughter to have evidence of virginity. But this is the evidence of my daughters virginity. And they shall spread out the garment before the elders of the city.
22:18 Then the elders of that city shall take the man and rebuke him,
22:19 and they shall fine him a hundred of silver and give it to the girls father, because he publicly defamed a virgin of Israel. And she shall remain his wife; he is not allowed to divorce her all his days.
22:20 But if this charge is true, they did not find the girl to have evidence of virginity,
22:21 then they shall bring the girl out to the doorway of her fathers house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death, because she has committed a disgraceful sin in Israel by playing the prostitute in her fathers house; so you shall eliminate the evil from among you.
22:22 If a man is found sleeping with a married woman, then both of them shall die, the man who slept with the woman, and the woman; so you shall eliminate the evil from Israel.
22:23 If there is a girl who is a virgin betrothed to a man, and man finds her in the city and sleeps with her,
22:24 then you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city and you shall stone them to death: the girl, because she did not cry out for help in the city, and the man, because he has violated his neighbors wife. So you shall eliminate the evil from among you.
22:25 But if the man finds the girl who is betrothed in the field, and the man seizes her and rapes her, then only the man who raped her shall die.
22:26 And you are not to do anything to the girl; there is no sin in the girl death, for just as a man rises against his neighbor and murders him, so is this case.
22:27 When he found her in the field, the betrothed girl cried out, but there was no one to save her.
22:28 If a man finds a girl who is a virgin, who is not betrothed, and he seizes her and has sexual relations with her, and they are discovered,
22:29 then the man who had sexual relations with her shall give the girls father fifty of silver, and she shall become his wife, because he has violated her; he is not allowed to divorce her all his days.
22:30 A man shall not take his fathers wife , so that he does not uncover his fathers garment.
23:1 No one who is emasculated or has his male organ cut off may enter the assembly of the .
23:2 No one of illegitimate birth may enter the assembly of the ; none of his , even to the tenth generation, may enter the assembly of the .
23:3 No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the ; none of their , even to the tenth generation, may ever enter the assembly of the ,
23:4 because they did not meet you with food and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you.
23:5 Nevertheless, the your God was unwilling to listen to Balaam, but the your God turned the curse into a blessing for you because the your God loves you.
23:6 You shall never seek their peace or their prosperity all your days.
23:7 You shall not loathe an Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not loathe an Egyptian, because you were a stranger in his land.
23:8 The sons of the third generation who are born to them may enter the assembly of the .
23:9 When you go out as an army against your enemies, you shall be on guard against every evil thing.
23:10 If there is among you any man who is unclean because of a nocturnal emission, then he must go outside the camp; he may not reenter the camp.
23:11 But when evening approaches, he shall bathe himself with water, and at sundown he may reenter the camp.
23:12 You shall also have a place outside the camp, so that you may go out there ,
23:13 and you shall have a spade among your tools, and it shall be when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and shall turn and cover up your excrement.
23:14 Since the your God walks in the midst of your camp to save you and to defeat your enemies before you, your camp must be holy; so He must not see anything indecent among you or He will turn away from you.
23:15 You shall not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped from his master to you.
23:16 He shall live with you in your midst, in the place that he chooses in one of your towns where it pleases him; you shall not mistreat him.
23:17 None of the daughters of Israel shall be a cult prostitute, nor shall any of the sons of Israel be a cult prostitute.
23:18 You shall not bring the earnings of a prostitute or the money for a dog into the house of the your God for any vowed offering, because both of these are an abomination to the your God.
23:19 You are not to charge interest to your countrymen: interest on money, food, anything that may be loaned on interest.
23:20 You may charge interest to a foreigner, but to your countrymen you shall not charge interest, so that the your God may bless you in all that you undertake in the land which you are about to enter to possess.
23:21 When you make a vow to the your God, you shall not delay to pay it, for the your God will certainly require it of you, and it will be a sin for you.
23:22 However, if you refrain from making vows, it will not be a sin for you.
23:23 You shall be careful and perform what goes out of your lips, since in fact you have vowed a voluntary offering to the your God, whatever you have promised.
23:24 When you enter your neighbors vineyard, you may eat grapes until you are satisfied; but you are not to put in your basket.
23:25 When you enter your neighbors standing grain, you may pluck the heads of grain with your hand, but you are not to use a sickle on your neighbors standing grain.
24:1 When a man takes a wife and marries her, and it happens, if she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found some indecency in her, that he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts in her hand, and sends her away from his house,
24:2 and she leaves his house and goes and becomes another mans ,
24:3 and the latter husband turns against her, writes her a certificate of divorce and puts in her hand, and sends her away from his house, or if the latter husband who took her to be his wife dies,
24:4 her former husband who sent her away is not allowed to take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled; for that is an abomination before the , and you shall not bring sin on the land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance.
24:5 When a man takes a new wife, he is not to go out with the army, nor be assigned any duty; he shall be free at home for one year and shall make his wife whom he has taken happy.
24:6 No one shall seize a handmill or an upper millstone as a pledge , since he would be seizing means of life as a pledge.
24:7 If someone is caught kidnapping any of his countrymen of the sons of Israel, and he treats him as merchandise and sells him, then that thief shall die; so you shall eliminate the evil from among you.
24:8 Be careful about an infestation of leprosy, that you are very attentive and act in accordance with everything that the Levitical priests teach you; just as I have commanded them, you shall be careful to act.
24:9 Remember what the your God did to Miriam on the way as you came out of Egypt.
24:10 When you make your neighbor a loan of any kind, you shall not enter his house to take his pledge.
24:11 You shall stand outside, and the person to whom you are making the loan shall bring the pledge outside to you.
24:12 And if he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge.
24:13 When the sun goes down you shall certainly return the pledge to him, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you; and it will be righteousness for you before the your God.
24:14 You shall not exploit a hired worker poor and needy, whether one of your countrymen or one of your strangers who are in your land in your towns.
24:15 You shall give him his wages on his day before the sun sets—for he is poor and sets his heart on it—so that he does not cry out against you to the , and it becomes a sin in you.
24:16 Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, nor shall sons be put to death for fathers; everyone shall be put to death for his own sin .
24:17 You shall not pervert the justice due a stranger an orphan, nor seize a widows garment as a pledge.
24:18 But you are to remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and that the your God redeemed you from there; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.
24:19 When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you are not to go back to get it; it shall belong to the stranger, the orphan, and to the widow, in order that the your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
24:20 When you beat off your olive tree, you are not to search through the branches again; shall be for the stranger, the orphan, and for the widow.
24:21 When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you are not to go over it again; shall be for the stranger, the orphan, and the widow.
24:22 And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.
25:1 If there is a dispute between people and they go to court, and the judges decide their case, and they declare the righteous innocent and pronounce the wicked guilty,
25:2 then it shall be if the wicked person deserves to be beaten, the judge shall then make him lie down and have him beaten in his presence with the number according to his wrongful act.
25:3 He may have him beaten forty times, not more, so that he does not have him beaten with many more lashes than these, and that your brother does not become contemptible in your eyes.
25:4 You shall not muzzle the ox while it is threshing.
25:5 When brothers live together, and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the deceased shall not be outside to a strange man. Her husbands brother shall have relations with her and take her to himself as wife, and perform the duty of a husbands brother to her.
25:6 It shall then be that the firstborn to whom she gives birth shall assume the name of his deceased brother, so that his name will not be wiped out from Israel.
25:7 But if the man does not desire to take his brothers widow, then his brothers widow shall go up to the gate to the elders, and say, My husbands brother refuses to establish a name for his brother in Israel; he is not willing to perform the duty of a husbands brother to me.
25:8 Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak to him. And he persists and says, I do not desire to take her,
25:9 then his brothers widow shall come up to him in the sight of the elders, and pull his sandal off his foot and spit in his face; and she shall declare, This is what is done to the man who does not build up his brothers house!
25:10 And in Israel his family shall be called by the name, The house of him whose sandal was removed.
25:11 If men, a man and his countryman, have a fight with each other, and the wife of one comes up to save her husband from the hand of the one who is hitting him, and she reaches out with her hand and grasps that mans genitals,
25:12 then you shall cut off her hand; you shall not show pity.
25:13 You shall not have in your bag differing weights, a large and a small.
25:14 You shall not have in your house differing measures, a large and a small.
25:15 You shall have a correct and honest weight; you shall have a correct and honest measure, so that your days may be prolonged in the land which the your God is giving you.
25:16 For everyone who does these things, everyone who acts unjustly is an abomination to the your God.
25:17 Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt,
25:18 how he confronted you on the way and attacked among you all the stragglers at your rear when you were tired and weary; and he did not fear God.
25:19 So it shall come about, when the your God has given you rest from all your surrounding enemies in the land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, that you shall wipe out the mention of Amalek from under heaven; you must not forget.
26:1 Then it shall be, when you enter the land which the your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and live in it,
26:2 that you shall take some of the first of all the produce of the ground which you bring in from your land that the your God gives you, and you shall put in a basket and go to the place where the your God chooses to establish His name.
26:3 And you shall go to the priest who is at that time and say to him, I declare today to the my God that I have entered the land which the swore to our fathers to give us.
26:4 Then the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it before the altar of the your God.
26:5 And you shall respond and say before the your God, My father was a wandering Aramean, and he went down to Egypt and resided there, few in number; but there he became a great, mighty, and populous nation.
26:6 And the Egyptians treated us badly and oppressed us, and imposed hard labor on us.
26:7 Then we cried out to the , the God of our fathers, and the heard our voice and saw our wretched condition, our trouble, and our oppression;
26:8 and the brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and with great terror, and with signs and wonders;
26:9 and He has brought us to this place, and has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
26:10 And now behold, I have brought the first of the produce of the ground which You, have given me. Then you shall set it before the your God, and worship before the your God;
26:11 and you, the Levite, and the stranger who is among you shall rejoice in all the good which the your God has given you and your household.
26:12 When you have finished paying all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, then you shall give it to the Levite, to the stranger, to the orphan, and to the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied.
26:13 And you shall say before the your God, I have removed the sacred from house, and have also given it to the Levite, the stranger, the orphan, and the widow, in accordance with all Your commandments which You have commanded me; I have not violated or forgotten any of Your commandments.
26:14 I have not eaten of it while mourning, nor have I removed any of it while I was unclean, nor offered any of it to the dead. I have listened to the voice of the my God; I have acted in accordance with everything that You have commanded me.
26:15 Look down from Your holy dwelling place, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel, and the ground which You have given us, a land flowing with milk and honey just as You swore to our fathers.
26:16 This day the your God commands you to perform these statutes and ordinances. Therefore you shall be careful to perform them with all your heart and with all your soul.
26:17 Today you have declared the to be your God, and that you will walk in His ways and keep His statutes, His commandments, and His ordinances, and listen to His voice.
26:18 And the has today declared you to be His people, personal possession, just as He promised you, and that you are to keep all His commandments;
26:19 and that He will put you high above all the nations which He has made, for glory, fame, and honor; and that you shall be a consecrated people to the your God, just as He has spoken.
27:1 Then Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, Keep all the commandments which I am commanding you today.
27:2 So it shall be on the day when you cross the Jordan to the land which the your God is giving you, that you shall set up for yourself large stones and coat them with lime
27:3 and write on them all the words of this Law, when you cross over, so that you may enter the land which the your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the , the God of your fathers, promised you.
27:4 So it shall be when you cross the Jordan, you shall set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am commanding you today, and you shall coat them with lime.
27:5 Moreover, you shall build there an altar to the your God, an altar of stones; you shall not wield an iron on them.
27:6 You shall build the altar of the your God of uncut stones, and you shall offer on it burnt offerings to the your God;
27:7 and you shall sacrifice peace offerings and eat there, and rejoice before the your God.
27:8 You shall write on the stones all the words of this Law very clearly.
27:9 Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, Be silent and listen, Israel! This day you have become a people for the your God.
27:10 So you shall obey the your God, and do His commandments and His statutes which I am commanding you today.
27:11 Moses also commanded the people on that day, saying,
27:12 When you cross the Jordan, these shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
27:13 For the curse, these shall stand on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
27:14 The Levites shall then respond and say to all the people of Israel with a loud voice,
27:15 Cursed is the person who makes a carved image or cast metal image, an abomination to the , the work of the hands of a craftsman, and sets up in secret. And all the people shall reply and say, Amen.
27:16 Cursed is one who treats his father or mother contemptuously. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:17 Cursed is one who displaces his neighbors boundary marker. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:18 Cursed is one who misleads a person who is blind on the road. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:19 Cursed is one who distorts the justice a stranger, an orphan, or a widow. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:20 Cursed is he who sleeps with his fathers wife, because he has uncovered his fathers garment. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:21 Cursed is one who has sexual intercourse with any animal. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:22 Cursed is he who sleeps with his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:23 Cursed is he who sleeps with his mother-in-law. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:24 Cursed is he who attacks his neighbor in secret. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:25 Cursed is he who accepts a bribe to attack an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.
27:26 Cursed is who does not fulfill the words of this Law by doing them. And all the people shall say, Amen.
28:1 Now it shall be, if you diligently obey the your God, being careful to do all His commandments which I am commanding you today, that the your God will put you high above all the nations of the earth.
28:2 And all these blessings will come to you and reach you if you obey the your God:
28:3 Blessed you in the city, and blessed you in the country.
28:4 Blessed the children of your womb, the produce of your ground, and the offspring of your animals: the newborn of your herd and the young of your flock.
28:5 Blessed your basket and your kneading bowl.
28:6 Blessed you when you come in, and blessed you when you go out.
28:7 The will cause your enemies who rise up against you to be defeated by you; they will go out against you one way and will flee at your presence seven ways.
28:8 The will command the blessing for you in your barns and in everything that you put your hand to, and He will bless you in the land that the your God is giving you.
28:9 The will establish you as a holy people to Himself, as He swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the your God and walk in His ways.
28:10 So all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the , and they will be afraid of you.
28:11 And the will give you more than enough prosperity, in the children of your womb, in the offspring of your livestock, and in the produce of your ground, in the land which the swore to your fathers to give you.
28:12 The will open for you His good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain to your land in its season and to bless every work of your hand; and you will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.
28:13 And the will make you the head and not the tail, and you will only be above, and not be underneath, if you listen to the commandments of the your God which I am commanding you today, to follow carefully,
28:14 and do not turn aside from any of the words which I am commanding you today, to the right or the left, to pursue other gods to serve them.
28:15 But it shall come about, if you do not obey the your God, to be careful to follow all His commandments and His statutes which I am commanding you today, that all these curses will come upon you and overtake you:
28:16 Cursed you in the city, and cursed you in the country.
28:17 Cursed your basket and your kneading bowl.
28:18 Cursed the children of your womb, the produce of your ground, the newborn of your herd, and the offspring of your flock.
28:19 Cursed you when you come in, and cursed you when you go out.
28:20 The will send against you curses, panic, and rebuke, in everything you undertake to do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, on account of the evil of your deeds, because you have abandoned Me.
28:21 The will make the plague cling to you until He has eliminated you from the land where you are entering to take possession of it.
28:22 The will strike you with consumption, inflammation, fever, feverish heat, and with the sword, with blight, and with mildew, and they will pursue you until you perish.
28:23 The heaven which is over your head shall be bronze, and the earth which is under you, iron.
28:24 The will make the rain of your land powder and dust; from heaven it shall come down on you until you are destroyed.
28:25 The will cause you to be defeated by your enemies; you will go out one way against them, but you will flee seven ways from their presence, and you will be terror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
28:26 Your dead bodies will serve as food for all birds of the sky and for the animals of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten .
28:27 The will strike you with the boils of Egypt and with tumors, the festering rash, and with scabies, from which you cannot be healed.
28:28 The will strike you with insanity, blindness, and with confusion of mind;
28:29 and you will be groping about at noon, just as a person who is blind gropes in the darkness, and you will not be successful in your ways; but you will only be oppressed and robbed all the time, with no one to save you.
28:30 You will betroth a woman, but another man will violate her; you will build a house, but you will not live in it; you will plant a vineyard, but you will not make use of its fruit.
28:31 Your ox slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat of it; your donkey snatched away from you, and will not be restored to you; your sheep given to your enemies, and you will have no one to save you.
28:32 Your sons and your daughters given to another people, while your eyes look on and long for them constantly; but there will be nothing you can do.
28:33 A people whom you do not know will eat the produce of your ground and every product of your labor, and you will never be anything but oppressed and mistreated continually.
28:34 You will also be driven insane by the sight of what you see.
28:35 The will strike you on the knees and thighs with severe boils from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.
28:36 The will bring you and your king, whom you appoint over you, to a nation that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone.
28:37 And you will become an horror, a song of mockery, and an object of taunting among all the peoples where the drives you.
28:38 You will bring out a great amount of seed to the field, but you will gather in little, because the locust will devour it.
28:39 You will plant and cultivate vineyards, but you will neither drink of the wine nor bring in , because the worm will eat it.
28:40 You will have olive trees throughout your territory but you will not anoint yourself with the oil, because your olives will drop off .
28:41 You will father sons and daughters but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity.
28:42 The cricket will take possession of all your trees and the produce of your ground.
28:43 The stranger who is among you will rise above you higher and higher, and you will go down lower and lower.
28:44 He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him; he will be the head, and you will be the tail.
28:45 So all these curses shall come upon you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you would not obey the your God by keeping His commandments and His statutes which He commanded you.
28:46 And they will become a sign and a wonder against you and your descendants forever.
28:47 Since you did not serve the your God with joy and a cheerful heart, for the abundance of all ,
28:48 you will serve your enemies whom the will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and devoid of all ; and He will put an iron yoke on your neck until He has destroyed you.
28:49 The will bring a nation against you from far away, from the end of the earth, as the eagle swoops down; a nation whose language you will not understand,
28:50 a nation with a defiant attitude, who will have no respect for the old, nor show favor to the young.
28:51 Furthermore, it will eat the offspring of your herd and the produce of your ground until you are destroyed; that will leave you no grain, new wine, or oil, nor the newborn of your cattle or the young of your flock, until they have eliminated you.
28:52 And it will besiege you in all your towns until your high and fortified walls in which you trusted come down throughout your land, and it will besiege you in all your towns throughout your land which the your God has given you.
28:53 Then you will eat the offspring of your own body, the flesh of your sons and of your daughters whom the your God has given you, during the siege and the hardship by which your enemy will oppress you.
28:54 The man who is refined and very delicate among you will be hostile toward his brother, toward the wife he cherishes, and toward the rest of his children who are left,
28:55 so that he will not give one of them any of the flesh of his children which he will eat, since he has nothing left, during the siege and the hardship by which your enemy will oppress you in all your towns.
28:56 The refined and delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicateness and tenderness, will be hostile toward the husband she cherishes and toward her son and daughter,
28:57 and toward her afterbirth that comes from between her legs, and toward her children to whom she gives birth, because she will eat them secretly for lack of anything , during the siege and the hardship with which your enemy will oppress you in your towns.
28:58 If you are not careful to follow all the words of this Law that are written in this book, to fear this honored and awesome name, the your God,
28:59 then the will bring extraordinary plagues on you and your descendants, severe and lasting plagues, and miserable and chronic sicknesses.
28:60 And He will bring back on you every disease of Egypt of which you were afraid, and they will cling to you.
28:61 Also every sickness and every plague, which are not written in the book of this Law, the will bring on you until you are destroyed.
28:62 Then you will be left few in number, whereas you were as numerous as the stars of heaven, because you did not obey the your God.
28:63 And it will come about that, just as the rejoiced over you to be good to you, and make you numerous, so will the rejoice over you to wipe you out and destroy you; and you will be torn away from the land which you are entering to possess.
28:64 Furthermore, the will scatter you among all the peoples, from end of the earth to the other; and there you will serve other gods, wood and stone, which you and your fathers have not known.
28:65 Among those nations you will find no peace, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot; but there the will give you a trembling heart, failing of eyes, and despair of soul.
28:66 So your lives will be hanging in doubt before you; and you will be terrified night and day, and have no assurance of your life.
28:67 In the morning you will say, If only it were evening! And at evening you will say, If only it were morning! because of the terror of your heart which you fear, and the sight of your eyes which you will see.
28:68 And the will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way about which I said to you, You will never see it again! And there you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but there will be no buyer.
29:1 These are the words of the covenant which the commanded Moses to make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which He had made with them at Horeb.
29:2 And Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, You have seen all that the did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and all his servants, and to all his land;
29:3 the great trials which your eyes have seen, those great signs and wonders.
29:4 Yet to this day the has not given you a heart to know, nor eyes to see, nor ears to hear.
29:5 And I have led you in the wilderness for forty years; your clothes have not worn out on you, and your sandal has not worn out on your foot.
29:6 You have not eaten bread, nor have you drunk wine or strong drink, in order that you might know that I am the your God.
29:7 When you reached this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon and Og the king of Bashan came out to meet us for battle, but we defeated them;
29:8 and we took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites.
29:9 So you will keep the words of this covenant and do them, in order that you may be successful in everything that you do.
29:10 You stand today, all of you, before the your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders and your officers, , all the men of Israel,
29:11 your little ones, your wives, and the stranger who is within your camps, from the one who gathers your firewood to the one who draws your water,
29:12 so that you may enter into the covenant with the your God, and into His oath which the your God is making with you today,
29:13 in order that He may establish you today as His people, and that He may be your God, just as He spoke to you and as He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
29:14 Now not with you alone I am making this covenant and this oath,
29:15 but with those who stand here with us today in the presence of the our God, and with those who are not with us here today
29:16 (for you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed;
29:17 moreover, you have seen their abominations and their idols wood and stone, silver and gold, which with them);
29:18 so that there will not be among you a man or woman, or family or tribe, whose heart turns away today from the our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations; that there will not be among you a root bearing poisonous fruit and wormwood.
29:19 And it shall be when he hears the words of this curse, that he will consider himself fortunate in his heart, saying, I will do well though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart in order to destroy the watered along with the dry.
29:20 The will not be willing to forgive him, but rather the anger of the and His wrath will burn against that person, and every curse that is written in this book will lie upon him, and the will wipe out his name from under heaven.
29:21 Then the will single him out for disaster from all the tribes of Israel, in accordance with all the curses of the covenant which is written in this Book of the Law.
29:22 Now the future generation, your sons who rise up after you and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases with which the has afflicted it, will say,
29:23 All its land is brimstone and salt, burned debris, unsown and unproductive, and no grass grows on it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the overthrew in His anger and in His wrath.
29:24 All the nations will say, Why has the done this to this land? Why this great outburst of anger?
29:25 Then will say, because they abandoned the covenant of the , the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.
29:26 And they went and served other gods and worshiped them, gods that they have not known and whom He had not assigned to them.
29:27 Therefore, the anger of the burned against that land, to bring upon it every curse which is written in this book;
29:28 and the uprooted them from their land in anger, fury, and in great wrath, and hurled them into another land, as this day.
29:29 The secret things belong to the our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our sons forever, so that we may follow all the words of this Law.
30:1 So it will be when all of these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have placed before you, and you call to mind in all the nations where the your God has scattered you,
30:2 and you return to the your God and obey Him with all your heart and soul in accordance with everything that I am commanding you today, you and your sons,
30:3 then the your God will restore you from captivity, and have compassion on you, and will gather you again from all the peoples where the your God has scattered you.
30:4 If any of your scattered are at the ends of the earth, from there the your God will gather you, and from there He will bring you back.
30:5 The your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it; and He will be good to you and make you more numerous than your fathers.
30:6 Moreover, the your God will circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants, to love the your God with all your heart and all your soul, so that you may live.
30:7 And the your God will inflict all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.
30:8 And you will again obey the , and follow all His commandments which I am commanding you today.
30:9 Then the your God will prosper you abundantly in every work of your hand, in the children of your womb, the offspring of your cattle, and in the produce of your ground, for the will again rejoice over you for good, just as He rejoiced over your fathers;
30:10 if you obey the your God, to keep His commandments and His statutes which are written in this Book of the Law, if you turn to the your God with all your heart and soul.
30:11 For this commandment which I am commanding you today is not too difficult for you, nor is it far away.
30:12 It is not in heaven, that you could say, Who will go up to heaven for us and get it for us, and proclaim it to us, so that we may follow it?
30:13 Nor is it beyond the sea, that you could say, Who will cross the sea for us and get it for us and proclaim it to us, so that we may follow it?
30:14 On the contrary, the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may follow it.
30:15 See, I have placed before you today life and happiness, and death and adversity,
30:16 in that I am commanding you today to love the your God, to walk in His ways and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His judgments, so that you may live and become numerous, and that the your God may bless you in the land where you are entering to take possession of it.
30:17 But if your heart turns away and you will not obey, but allow yourself to be led astray and you worship other gods and serve them,
30:18 I declare to you today that you will certainly perish. You will not prolong days in the land where you are crossing the Jordan to enter and take possession of it.
30:19 I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have placed before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. So choose life in order that you may live, you and your descendants,
30:20 by loving the your God, by obeying His voice, and by holding close to Him; for this is your life and the length of your days, so that you may live in the land which the swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give them.
31:1 So Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
31:2 And he said to them, I am 120 years old today; I am no longer able to go out and come in, and the has told me, You shall not cross this Jordan.
31:3 It is the your God who is going to cross ahead of you; He Himself will destroy these nations before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua is the one who is going to cross ahead of you, just as the has spoken.
31:4 And the will do to them just as He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when He destroyed them.
31:5 The will turn them over to you, and you will do to them in accordance with all the commandments which I have commanded you.
31:6 Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid or in dread of them, for the your God is the One who is going with you. He will not desert you or abandon you.
31:7 Then Moses called to Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land which the has sworn to their fathers to give them, and you will give it to them as an inheritance.

31:13 And their children, who have not known, will hear and learn to fear the your God, as long as you live on the land which you are about to cross the Jordan to possess.
31:14 Then the said to Moses, Behold, the time for you to die is near; call Joshua and present yourselves at the tent of meeting, and I will commission him. So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the tent of meeting.
31:15 And the appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.
31:16 The said to Moses, Behold, you are about to lie down with your fathers; and this people will arise and play the prostitute with the foreign gods of the land into the midst of which they are going, and they will abandon Me and break My covenant which I have made with them.
31:17 Then My anger will be kindled against them on that day, and I will abandon them and hide My face from them, and they will be consumed, and many evils and troubles will find them; so they will say on that day, Is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us?
31:18 But I will assuredly hide My face on that day because of all the evil that they will have done, for they will have turned away to other gods.
31:19 Now then, write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the sons of Israel; put it on their lips, so that this song may be a witness for Me against the sons of Israel.
31:20 For when I bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey, which I swore to their fathers, and they eat and are satisfied and become prosperous, then they will turn to other gods and serve them, and spurn Me and break My covenant.
31:21 Then it will come about, when many evils and troubles find them, that this song will testify before them as a witness (for it shall not be forgotten from the mouth of their descendants); for I know their inclination which they are developing today, before I bring them into the land which I swore.
31:22 So Moses wrote down this song on the same day, and taught it to the sons of Israel.
31:23 Then He commissioned Joshua the son of Nun, and said, Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the sons of Israel into the land which I swore to them, and I will be with you.
31:24 It came about, when Moses finished writing the words of this Law in a book until they were complete,

31:26 Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the your God, so that it may remain there as a witness against you.

31:28 Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, that I may speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against them.
31:29 For I know that after my death you will behave very corruptly and turn from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will confront you in the latter days, because you will do that which is evil in the sight of the , provoking Him to anger with the work of your hands.

32:2 May my teaching drip as the rain, My speech trickle as the dew, As droplets on the fresh grass, And as the showers on the vegetation.
32:3 For I proclaim the name of the ; Ascribe greatness to our God!
32:4 The Rock! His work is perfect, For all His ways are just; A God of faithfulness and without injustice, Righteous and just is He.
32:5 They have acted corruptly against Him, not His children, their defect; a perverse and crooked generation.
32:6 this you do to the , You foolish and unwise people? Is He not your Father purchased you? He has made you and established you.

32:8 When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, When He separated the sons of mankind, He set the boundaries of the peoples According to the number of the sons of Israel.
32:9 For the portion is His people; Jacob is the allotment of His inheritance.
32:10 He found him in a desert land, And in the howling wasteland of a wilderness; He encircled him, He cared for him, He guarded him as the apple of His eye.
32:11 As an eagle stirs up its nest, hovers over its young, He spread His wings, He caught them, He carried them on His pinions.
32:12 The alone guided him, And there was no foreign god with him.
32:13 He had him ride on the high places of the earth, And he ate the produce of the field; And He had him suck honey from the rock, And oil from the flinty rock,

32:16 They made Him jealous with strange ; With abominations they provoked Him to anger.

32:22 For a fire has flared in My anger, And it burns to the lowest part of Sheol, And devours the earth with its yield, And sets on fire the foundations of the mountains.
32:23 I will add misfortunes to them; I will use up My arrows on them.
32:24 wasted by famine, and emaciated by plague And a bitter epidemic; And the teeth of beasts I will send against them, With the venom of crawling things of the dust.

32:26 I would have said, I will wipe them out, I will remove the mention of their name from humanity,
32:27 Had I not feared the provocation by the enemy, That their adversaries would misjudge, That they would say, Our hand is triumphant, And the has not performed all this.
32:28 For they are a nation destitute of counsel, And there is no understanding in them.
32:29 If only they were wise they understood this; they would discern their future!
32:30 How could one chase a thousand, And two put ten thousand to flight, Unless their Rock had sold them, And the had given them up?
32:31 Indeed, their rock is not like our Rock; Even our enemies themselves judge this.
32:32 For their vine is from the vine of Sodom, And from the fields of Gomorrah; Their grapes are grapes of poison, Their clusters, bitter.
32:33 Their wine is the venom of serpents, And the deadly poison of vipers.
32:34 Is it not stored up with Me, Sealed up in My treasuries?
32:35 Vengeance is Mine, and retribution; In time their foot will slip. For the day of their disaster is near, And the impending things are hurrying to them.
32:36 For the will vindicate His people, And will have compassion on His servants, When He sees that strength is gone, And there is none , bond or free.

32:38 Those who ate the fat of their sacrifices, drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and help you, Let them be your protection!
32:39 See now that I, I am He, And there is no god besides Me; I put to death and give life. I have wounded and I heal, And there is no one who can save from My hand.
32:40 Indeed, I raise My hand to heaven, And say, as I live forever,
32:41 If I have sharpened My flashing sword, And My hand has taken hold of justice, I will return vengeance on My adversaries, And I will repay those who hate Me.
32:42 I will make My arrows drunk with blood, And My sword will devour flesh, With the blood of the slain and the captives, From the long-haired leaders of the enemy.
32:43 Rejoice, you nations, His people; For He will avenge the blood of His servants, And will return vengeance on His adversaries, And will atone for His land His people.

32:52 For you will see the land at a distance but you will not go there, into the land which I am giving the sons of Israel.
