10:1 Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon to the name of the , she came to test him with riddles.
10:2 So she came to Jerusalem with a very large entourage, with camels carrying balsam oil and a very large gold and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she spoke to him about everything that was in her heart.
10:3 And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was concealed from the king which he did not explain to her.
10:4 When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,
10:5 and the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the service of his waiters and their attire, his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings which he offered at the house of the , she was breathless.
10:6 Then she said to the king, It was a true story that I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom.
10:7 But I did not believe the stories until I came and my eyes saw . And behold, the half was not reported to me. You have exceeded wisdom and prosperity the report which I heard.
10:8 Blessed are your men, blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you continually hear your wisdom!
10:9 Blessed be the your God who delighted in you to put you on the throne of Israel; because the loves Israel forever, He made you king, to do justice and righteousness.
10:10 Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, and a very large of balsam oil and precious stones. Never again did such a large quantity of balsam oil come in as that which the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
10:11 And the ships of Hiram as well, which brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir a very great almug trees and precious stones.
10:12 The king made from the almug trees supports for the house of the and for the kings house, and lyres and harps for the singers; such almug trees have not come in , nor have they been seen to this day.
10:13 And King Solomon granted the queen of Sheba everything she desired, whatever she requested, besides what he gave her in proportion to his royal bounty. Then she departed and went to her own land together with her servants.
10:14 Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents of gold,
10:15 besides from the traders, and the wares of the merchants and all the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the country.
10:16 King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold, using six hundred gold on each large shield.
10:17 And three hundred shields of beaten gold, using three minas of gold on each shield; and the king put them in the house of the timber of Lebanon.
10:18 Moreover, the king made a large throne of ivory and overlaid it with fine gold.
10:19 six steps to the throne and a round top to the throne at its back, and armrests on each side of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
10:20 Twelve lions were standing there on the six steps on the one side and on the other; nothing like was made for any other kingdom.
10:21 Now all King Solomons drinking utensils of gold, and all the utensils of the house of the timber of Lebanon of pure gold. None was of silver; it was not considered anything in the days of Solomon.
10:22 For the king had the ships of Tarshish at sea with Hirams ships; once every three years the ships of Tarshish would come carrying gold and silver, ivory, monkeys, and peacocks.
10:23 So King Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.
10:24 And all the earth was seeking the attention of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
10:25 And they were bringing, everyone, a gift: articles of silver and gold, garments, weapons, balsam oil, horses, and mules, so much year by year.
10:26 Now Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen; and he had 1,400 chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
10:27 And the king made silver as stones in Jerusalem, and he made cedars as plentiful as sycamore trees that are in the lowland.
10:28 Also Solomons import of horses was from Egypt and Kue, the kings merchants acquired from Kue for a price.
10:29 A chariot was imported from Egypt for six hundred of silver, and a horse for 150; and by the same means they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of the Arameans.

11:5 For Solomon became a follower of Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and of Milcom the abhorrent idol of the Ammonites.

11:13 Yet I will not tear away all the kingdom, I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David, and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.
11:14 Then the raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite; he was of the royal line in Edom.

11:19 Now Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him in marriage the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.

11:22 However, Pharaoh said to him, But what have you lacked with me that you are here, requesting to go to your own country? And he answered, Nothing; nevertheless you must let me go.

11:27 Now this was the reason why he rebelled against the king: Solomon built the Millo, closed up the breach of the city of his father David.
11:28 Now the man Jeroboam was a valiant warrior, and when Solomon saw that the young man was industrious, he appointed him over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
11:29 And it came about at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Now Ahijah had clothed himself with a new cloak; and both of them were alone in the field.

12:6 And King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was still alive, saying, How do you advise to answer this people?
12:7 Then they spoke to him, saying, If you will be a servant to this people today, and will serve them and grant them their request, and speak pleasant words to them, then they will be your servants always.
12:8 But he ignored the advice of the elders which they had given him, and consulted with the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
12:9 He said to them, What advice do you give, so that we may answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, Lighten the yoke which your father put on us?
12:10 And the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, This is what you should say to this people who spoke to you, saying: Your father made our yoke heavy, now you make it lighter for us! You should speak this way to them: My little finger is thicker than my fathers waist!
12:11 Now then, my father loaded you with a heavy yoke; yet I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions!
12:12 Then Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had directed, saying, Return to me on the third day.
12:13 And the king answered the people harshly, for he ignored the advice of the elders which they had given him,
12:14 and he spoke to them according to the advice of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions!
12:15 So the king did not listen to the people; because it was a turn of events from the , in order to establish His word which the spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

13:1 Now behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of the , while Jeroboam was standing at the altar to burn incense.
13:2 And he cried out against the altar by the word of the and said, Altar, altar, this is what the says: Behold, a son shall be born to the house of David, Josiah by name; and on you he shall sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones shall burn on you.
13:3 Then he gave a sign on the same day, saying, This is the sign which the has spoken: Behold, the altar shall be torn to pieces and the ashes which are on it shall be poured out.
13:4 Now when the king heard the statement of the man of God which he cried out against the altar in Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, Seize him! But his hand which he had stretched out toward him dried up, and he could not draw it back to himself.
13:5 The altar also was torn to pieces and the ashes were poured out from the altar, in accordance with the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the .
13:6 And the king responded and said to the man of God, Please appease the your God and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored to me. So the man of God appeased the , and the kings hand was restored to him, and it became as it was before.
13:7 Then the king said to the man of God, Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a gift.
13:8 But the man of God said to the king, If you were to give me half your house, I would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place.
13:9 For so it was commanded me by the word of the , saying, You shall not eat bread nor drink water, nor return by the way that you came.
13:10 So he went another way and did not return by the way that he had come to Bethel.
13:11 Now an old prophet was living in Bethel; and his sons came and told him all the deeds which the man of God had done that day in Bethel; the words which he had spoken to the king, these also they reported to their father.
13:12 And their father said to them, Which way did he go? Now his sons had seen the way that the man of God who came from Judah had gone.
13:13 Then he said to his sons, Saddle the donkey for me. So they saddled the donkey for him and he rode on it.
13:14 So he went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak; and he said to him, Are you the man of God who came from Judah? And he said, I am.
13:15 Then he said to him, Come home with me and eat bread.
13:16 But he said, I cannot return with you, nor come with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
13:17 For a command to me by the word of the : You shall not eat bread, nor drink water there; do not return by going the way that you came.
13:18 Then he said to him, I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the , saying, Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water. he lied to him.
13:19 So he went back with him, and ate bread in his house and drank water.
13:20 Now it came about, as they were sitting down at the table, that the word of the came to the prophet who had brought him back;
13:21 and he cried out to the man of God who came from Judah, saying, This is what the says: Because you have disobeyed the command of the , and have not kept the commandment which the your God commanded you,
13:22 but have returned and eaten bread and drunk water in the place of which He said to you, You are not to eat bread nor drink water; your dead body will not come to the grave of your fathers.
13:23 It came about after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
13:24 Now when he had gone, a lion met him on the way and killed him, and his body was thrown on the road, with the donkey standing beside it; the lion also was standing beside the body.
13:25 And behold, men passed by and saw the body thrown on the road, and the lion standing beside the body; so they came and told in the city where the old prophet had lived.
13:26 Now when the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard , he said, It is the man of God, who disobeyed the command of the ; therefore the has given him to the lion, which has torn him and killed him, in accordance with the word of the which He spoke to him.
13:27 Then he spoke to his sons, saying, Saddle the donkey for me. And they saddled .
13:28 Then he went and found his body thrown on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside the body; the lion had not eaten the body nor harmed the donkey.
13:29 So the prophet picked up the body of the man of God and laid it on the donkey and brought it back; and he came to the city of the old prophet to mourn and to bury him.
13:30 He laid his body in his own grave, and they mourned over him, , Oh, my brother!
13:31 And after he had buried him, he talked to his sons, saying, When I die, bury me in the grave in which the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
13:32 For the thing will certainly come to pass which he cried out by the word of the against the altar that is in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria.
13:33 After this event, Jeroboam did not abandon his evil way, but he again appointed priests of the high places from all the people; anyone who wanted, he ordained, and he became priests of the high places.
13:34 This event also became a sin of the house of Jeroboam, even to wipe out and eliminate from the face of the earth.
14:1 At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam became sick.

14:4 And Jeroboams wife did so, and set out and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see because his eyes were glossy from his old age.

14:21 Now Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. And his mothers name was Naamah the Ammonitess.

15:1 Now in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, Abijam became king over Judah.
15:2 He reigned for three years in Jerusalem; and his mothers name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
15:3 He walked in all the sins of his father which he had committed before him; and his heart was not wholly devoted to the his God, like the heart of his father David.
15:4 But for Davids sake the his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, to raise up his son after him and to establish Jerusalem,

15:6 And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
15:7 Now the rest of the acts of Abijam and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
15:8 And Abijam lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and his son Asa became king in his place.
15:9 So in the twentieth year of Jeroboam the king of Israel, Asa began to reign as king of Judah.
15:10 He reigned for forty-one years in Jerusalem; and his mothers name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
15:11 Now Asa did what was right in the sight of the , like his father David.
15:12 He also removed the male cult prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols which his fathers had made.
15:13 And even his mother Maacah, he also removed her from queen mother, because she had made an abominable image as an Asherah; and Asa cut down her abominable image and burned at the brook Kidron.
15:14 But the high places were not eliminated; nevertheless Asas heart was wholly devoted to the all his days.
15:15 And he brought into the house of the the holy gifts of his father and his own holy gifts: silver, gold, and utensils.
15:16 Now there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
15:17 Baasha king of Israel marched against Judah and fortified Ramah in order to prevent from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.
15:18 Then Asa took all the silver and the gold that was left in the treasuries of the house of the and the treasuries of the kings house, and handed it over to his servants. And King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,
15:19 a treaty between you and me, between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you a gift of silver and gold; go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel so that he will withdraw from me.
15:20 So Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinneroth, besides all the land of Naphtali.
15:21 When Baasha heard , he stopped fortifying Ramah and remained in Tirzah.

15:23 Now the rest of all the acts of Asa and all his might, and all that he did and the cities which he built, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
15:24 And Asa lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David; and his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place.
15:25 Now Nadab the son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel for two years.
15:26 He did evil in the sight of the , and walked in the way of his father and in his sin into which he misled Israel.
15:27 Then Baasha the son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar conspired against him, and Baasha struck and killed him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were laying siege to Gibbethon.
15:28 So Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.

16:4 Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone belonging to him who dies in the field, the birds of the sky will eat.

16:10 Then Zimri came in and struck him and put him to death in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and he became king in his place.
16:11 And when he became king, as soon as he sat on his throne, he killed all the household of Baasha; he did not leave a single male alive, either of his relatives or of his friends.

16:13 for all the sins of Baasha and the sins of his son Elah, which they committed and into which they misled Israel, provoking the God of Israel to anger with their idols.
16:14 Now the rest of the acts of Elah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
16:15 In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned for seven days in Tirzah. Now the people were camped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
16:16 And the people who were camped heard it being said, Zimri has conspired and has also struck and killed the king! Therefore all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp.
16:17 Then Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
16:18 When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the citadel of the kings house and burned the kings house over himself with fire, and died,

16:21 Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; the half followed Omri.
16:22 But the people who followed Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni the son of Ginath. And Tibni died and Omri became king.
16:23 In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel for twelve years; he reigned for six years at Tirzah.
16:24 And he purchased the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built on the hill, and named the city which he built Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.
16:25 Now Omri did evil in the sight of the , and acted more wickedly than all who before him.
16:26 For he walked entirely in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and in his sins into which he misled Israel, provoking the God of Israel to anger with their idols.
16:27 Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he did and his might which he displayed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
16:28 And Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria; and his son Ahab became king in his place.
16:29 Now Ahab the son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and Ahab the son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-two years.

16:32 So he erected an altar for Baal at the house of Baal, which he built in Samaria.

17:1 Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, As the , the God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall certainly be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word.
17:2 Then the word of the came to him, saying,
17:3 Go from here and turn eastward, and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
17:4 And it shall be that you will drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to provide food for you there.
17:5 So he went and did according to the word of the , for he went and lived by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
17:6 And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and he would drink from the brook.
17:7 But it happened after a while that the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
17:8 Then the word of the came to him, saying,
17:9 Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there; behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide food for you.
17:10 So he arose and went to Zarephath, and when he came to the entrance of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks; and he called to her and said, Please get me a little water in a cup, so that I may drink.
17:11 As she was going to get , he called to her and said, Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand.
17:12 But she said, As the your God lives, I have no food, only a handful of flour in the bowl and a little oil in the jar; and behold, I am gathering a few sticks so that I may go in and prepare it for me and my son, so that we may eat it and die.
17:13 However, Elijah said to her, Do not fear; go, do as you have said. Just make me a little bread loaf from it first and bring out to me, and afterward you may make for yourself and for your son.
17:14 For this is what the , the God of Israel says: The bowl of flour shall not be used up, nor shall the jar of oil become empty, until the day that the provides rain on the face of the earth.
17:15 So she went and did in accordance with the word of Elijah, and she and he and her household ate for days.
17:16 The bowl of flour was not used up, nor did the jar of oil become empty, in accordance with the word of the which He spoke through Elijah.
17:17 Now it happened after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick; and his condition became very grave, until he was no longer breathing.
17:18 So she said to Elijah, Why is my yours, you man of God? you have come to me to bring my wrongdoing to remembrance, and to put my son to death!
17:19 But he said to her, Give me your son. Then he took him from her arms and carried him up to the upstairs room where he was living, and laid him on his own bed.
17:20 And he called to the and said, , my God, have You also brought catastrophe upon the widow with whom I am staying, by causing her son to die?
17:21 Then he stretched himself out over the boy three times, and called to the and said, , my God, please, let this boys life return to him.
17:22 And the listened to the voice of Elijah, and the life of the boy returned to him and he revived.
17:23 Elijah then took the boy and brought him down from the upstairs room into the house and gave him to his mother; and Elijah said, See, your son is alive.
17:24 Then the woman said to Elijah, Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the in your mouth is truth.

18:2 So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. Now the famine severe in Samaria.
18:3 Ahab summoned Obadiah, who in charge of the household. (Now Obadiah feared the greatly;
18:4 for when Jezebel killed the prophets of the , Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them by fifties in a cave, and provided them with bread and water.)
18:5 Then Ahab said to Obadiah, Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the river valleys; perhaps we will find grass and keep the horses and mules alive, and not kill some of the cattle.

18:14 Yet now you are saying, Go, say to your master, Behold, Elijah ; he will then kill me!
18:15 Then Elijah said, As the of armies lives, before whom I stand, I will certainly present myself to him today.

18:18 He said, I have not brought disaster to Israel, but you and your fathers house , because you have abandoned the commandments of the and you have followed the Baals.
18:19 Now then, send gather to me all Israel at Mount Carmel, with 450 prophets of Baal and four hundred prophets of the Asherah, who eat at Jezebels table.
18:20 So Ahab sent among all the sons of Israel and brought the prophets together at Mount Carmel.
18:21 Then Elijah approached all the people and said, How long are you going to struggle with the two choices? If the is God, follow Him; but if Baal, follow him. But the people did not answer him a word.
18:22 Then Elijah said to the people, I alone am left as a prophet of the , while Baals prophets are 450 men.
18:23 Now have them give us two oxen; and have them choose the one ox for themselves and cut it up, and place it on the wood, but put no fire ; and I will prepare the other ox and lay it on the wood, and I will not put a fire .
18:24 Then you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the ; and the God who answers by fire, He is God. And all the people replied, That is a good idea.
18:25 So Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, Choose the one ox for yourselves and prepare it first, since many you, and call on the name of your god, but put no fire .
18:26 Then they took the ox which was given them and they prepared it, and they called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, O Baal, answer us! But there was no voice and no one answered. And they limped about the altar which they had made.
18:27 And at noon Elijah ridiculed them and said, Call out with a loud voice, since he is a god; undoubtedly he is attending to business, or is on the way, or is on a journey. Perhaps he is asleep, and will awaken.
18:28 So they cried out with a loud voice, and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and lances until blood gushed out on them.
18:29 When midday was past, they raved until the time of the offering of the sacrifice; but there was no voice, no one answered, and no one paid attention.
18:30 Then Elijah said to all the people, Come forward to me. So all the people came forward to him. And he repaired the altar of the which had been torn down.
18:31 Then Elijah took twelve stones, corresponding to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the had come, saying, Israel shall be your name.
18:32 And with the stones he built an altar in the name of the ; and he made a trench around the altar, large enough to hold two measures of seed.
18:33 Then he laid out the wood, and he cut the ox in pieces and placed on the wood.
18:34 And he said, Fill four large jars with water and pour on the burnt offering and on the wood. And he said, Do it a second time, so they did it a second time. Then he said, Do it a third time, so they did it a third time.
18:35 The water flowed around the altar, and he also filled the trench with water.
18:36 Then at the time of the offering of the sacrifice, Elijah the prophet approached and said, , God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, today let it be known that You are God in Israel and that I am Your servant, and I have done all these things at Your word.
18:37 Answer me, , answer me, so that this people may know that You, , are God, and You have turned their heart back.
18:38 Then the fire of the fell and consumed the burnt offering and the wood, and the stones and the dust; and it licked up the water that was in the trench.
18:39 When all the people saw , they fell on their faces; and they said, The , He is God; the , He is God!
18:40 Then Elijah said to them, Seize the prophets of Baal; do not let one of them escape. So they seized them; and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slaughtered them there.
18:41 Now Elijah said to Ahab, Go up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of the roar of a shower.
18:42 So Ahab went up to eat and drink. But Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he bent down to the earth and put his face between his knees.
18:43 And he said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. So he went up and looked, but he said, There is nothing. Yet said, Go back seven times.
18:44 And the seventh , he said, Behold, a cloud as small as a persons hand is coming up from the sea. And said, Go up, say to Ahab, Harness and go down, so that the shower does not stop you.
18:45 Meanwhile the sky became dark with clouds and wind , and there was a heavy shower. And Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.
18:46 Then the hand of the was on Elijah, and he belted around his waist and outran Ahab to Jezreel.
19:1 Now Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
19:2 Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, So may the gods do to me and more so, if about this time tomorrow I do not make your life like the life of one of them.
19:3 And he was afraid, and got up and ran for his life and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah; and he left his servant there.
19:4 But he himself went a days journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a broom tree; and he asked for himself to die, and said, Enough! Now, , take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.
19:5 Then he lay down and fell asleep under a broom tree; but behold, there was an angel touching him, and he said to him, Arise, eat!
19:6 And he looked, and behold, there was at his head a round loaf of bread hot coals, and a pitcher of water. So he ate and drank, and lay down again.

20:1 Now Ben-hadad, king of Aram, gathered all his army, and thirty-two kings with him, and horses and chariots. And he went up and besieged Samaria, and fought against it.
20:2 Then he sent messengers to the city to Ahab, king of Israel, and said to him, This is what Ben-hadad says:
20:3 Your silver and your gold are mine; your most beautiful wives and children are also mine.
20:4 And the king of Israel replied, As you say, my lord, O king; I am yours, as well as all that I have.
20:5 Then the messengers returned and said, Ben-hadad says this: I did indeed send to you, saying, You shall give me your silver, your gold, your wives, and your children;
20:6 but about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants; and they will take in their hands everything that is pleasing to your eyes, and take away.

21:4 So Ahab entered his house sullen and furious because of the answer that Naboth the Jezreelite had given to him, since he said, I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers. And he lay down on his bed and turned his face away, and ate no food.
21:5 But Jezebel his wife came to him and said to him, How is it that your spirit is so sullen that you are not eating food?
21:6 So he said to her, because I was speaking to Naboth the Jezreelite and saying to him, Give me your vineyard for money; or else, if it pleases you, I will give you a vineyard in place of it. But he said, I will not give you my vineyard.

21:12 They proclaimed a fast, and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
21:13 Then the two worthless men came in and sat opposite him; and the worthless men testified against him, against Naboth, before the people, saying, Naboth cursed God and the king. So they took him outside the city and stoned him to death with stones.

3:1 Now Jehoram the son of Ahab became king over Israel at Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned for twelve years.
3:2 He did evil in the sight of the , though not like his father and his mother; for he removed the memorial stone of Baal which his father had made.
3:3 Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel; he did not abandon them.
3:4 Now Mesha the king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to make payments to the king of Israel of a hundred thousand lambs, and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
3:5 However, when Ahab died, the king of Moab broke with the king of Israel.
3:6 So King Jehoram left Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.
3:7 Then he went and sent to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, saying, The king of Moab has broken away from me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab? And he said, I will go up. Consider me yours, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.
3:8 Then he said, Which way shall we go up? And he answered, The way of the wilderness of Edom.
3:9 So the king of Israel went with the king of Judah and the king of Edom, and they made a circuit of seven days journey. But there was no water for the army or for the cattle that followed them.
3:10 Then the king of Israel said, It is hopeless! For the has called these three kings to hand them over to Moab!
3:11 But Jehoshaphat said, Is there no prophet of the here, that we may inquire of the by him? And one of the king of Israels servants answered and said, Elisha the son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water on the hands of Elijah.
3:12 And Jehoshaphat said, The word of the is with him. So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.
3:13 Now Elisha said to the king of Israel, What business do you have with me? Go to your fathers prophets and your mothers prophets. But the king of Israel said to him, No, for the has called these three kings to hand them over to Moab.
3:14 Elisha said, As the of armies lives, before whom I stand, if I did not respect Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look at you nor see you.
3:15 But now bring me a musician. And it came about, when the musician played, that the hand of the came upon him.
3:16 And he said, This is what the says: Make this valley full of trenches.
3:17 For the says this: You will not see wind, nor will you see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, so that you will drink, you, your livestock, and your animals.
3:18 And this is an insignificant thing in the sight of the ; He will also give the Moabites into your hand.
3:19 Then you shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and cut down every good tree and stop up all the springs of water, and spoil every good plot of land with stones.
3:20 And it happened in the morning about offering the sacrifice, that behold, water came from the direction of Edom, and the country was filled with water.
3:21 Now all the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. And all who were able to put on armor and older were summoned and they took their positions on the border.
3:22 Then they got up early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and the Moabites saw the water opposite as red as blood.
3:23 So they said, This is blood; the kings must have fought each other, and they have killed one another. Now then, Moab, to the spoils!
3:24 But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck the Moabites, so that they fled from them; and invaded the land, killing the Moabites.
3:25 So they destroyed the cities; and each one threw a stone on every plot of good land and filled it. So they stopped up every spring of water and cut down every good tree, until in Kir-hareseth they left its stones; however, the rock slingers surrounded and struck it.
3:26 When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew swords, to break through to the king of Edom; but they could not.
3:27 Then took his oldest son who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. And great anger came upon Israel, and they departed from him and returned to their own land.
4:1 Now a woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the ; and the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves.
4:2 So Elisha said to her, What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house? And she said, Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.
4:3 Then he said, Go, borrow containers elsewhere for yourself, empty containers from all your neighbors—do not get few.
4:4 Then you shall come in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all these containers; and you shall set aside what is full.
4:5 So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons; they bringing to her, and she poured .
4:6 When the containers were full, she said to her son, Bring me another container. But he said to her, There are no more containers. Then the oil stopped.
4:7 So she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you your sons can live on the rest.
4:8 Now a day came when Elisha went over to Shunem, where there was a prominent woman, and she urged him to eat food. And so it was, as often as he passed by, he turned in there to eat food.
4:9 And she said to her husband, Behold now, I am aware that this is a holy man of God passing by us repeatedly.
4:10 Please, lets make a little walled upper room, and lets set up a bed for him there, and a table, a chair, and a lampstand; then it shall be, when he comes to us, he can turn in there.
4:11 Now one day he came there, and turned in to the upper room and rested.
4:12 Then he said to his servant Gehazi, Call this Shunammite. And when he had called her, she stood before him.
4:13 And he said to him, Say now to her, Behold, you have taken trouble for us with all this care; what can I do for you? Would you like me to speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army? But she answered, I live among my own people.
4:14 So he said, What then is to be done for her? And Gehazi answered, It is a fact that she has no son, and her husband is old.
4:15 He then said, Call her. When he had called her, she stood in the doorway.
4:16 Then he said, At this season next year, you are going to embrace a son. And she said, No, my lord, you man of God, do not lie to your servant.
4:17 Now the woman conceived and gave birth to a son at that season the next year, as Elisha had told her.
4:18 When the child was grown, the day came that he went out to his father, to the reapers.
4:19 And he said to his father, My head, my head! And said to his servant, Carry him to his mother.
4:20 When he had carried him and brought him to his mother, he sat on her lap until noon, and he died.
4:21 And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut behind him and left.
4:22 Then she called to her husband and said, Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I may run to the man of God and return.
4:23 But he said, Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath. So she said, fine.
4:24 Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, Drive and go on; do not slow down the pace for me unless I tell you.
4:25 So she went on and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her at a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, Behold, that person there is the Shunammite.
4:26 Please run now to meet her and say to her, Is it well for you? Is it well for your husband? Is it well for the child? Then she answered, It is well.
4:27 But she came to the man of God at the hill and took hold of his feet. And Gehazi came up to push her away, but the man of God said, Leave her alone, for her soul is troubled within her; and the has concealed from me and has not informed me.
4:28 Then she said, Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say, Do not give me false hope?
4:29 Then he said to Gehazi, Get ready and take my staff in your hand, and go; if you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not reply to him. And lay my staff on the boys face.
4:30 The mother of the boy said, As the lives and you yourself live, I will not leave you. So he got up and followed her.
4:31 Then Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boys face, but there was no sound or response. So he returned to meet him and informed him, saying, The boy has not awakened.
4:32 When Elisha entered the house, behold the boy was dead, laid on his bed.
4:33 So he entered and shut the door behind them both, and he prayed to the .
4:34 Then he got up and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, his hands on his hands, and he bent down on him; and the flesh of the child became warm.
4:35 Then he returned and walked in the house back and forth once, and went up and bent down on him; and the boy sneezed seven times, then the boy opened his eyes.
4:36 And he called Gehazi and said, Call this Shunammite. So he called her. And when she came to him, he said, Pick up your son.
4:37 Then she came in and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground, and she picked up her son and left.
4:38 When Elisha returned to Gilgal, a famine in the land. As the sons of the prophets were sitting in front of him, he said to his servant, Put on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.
4:39 Then one went out into the field to gather mallow, and found a wild vine and gathered from it his lap full of wild gourds; and he came and sliced them into the pot of stew, because they did not know .
4:40 So they poured out for the men to eat. But as they were eating the stew, they cried out and said, You man of God, there is death in the pot! And they were unable to eat.
4:41 Then he said, Bring flour. And he threw it into the pot, and said, Pour out for the people that they may eat. Then there was nothing harmful in the pot.
4:42 Now a man came from Baal-shalishah, and brought the man of God bread of the first fruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh grain in his sack. And said, Give to the people that they may eat.
4:43 But his attendant said, How am I to serve this to a hundred men? Nevertheless he said, Give to the people that they may eat, for this is what the says: They shall eat and have left over.
4:44 So he served to them, and they ate and had left over, in accordance with the word of the .
5:1 Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in the view of his master, and eminent, because by him the had given victory to Aram. The man was also a valiant warrior, afflicted with leprosy.
5:2 Now the Arameans had gone out in bands and had taken captive a little girl from the land of Israel; and she waited on Naamans wife.
5:3 And she said to her mistress, If only my master were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his leprosy.
5:4 And Naaman went in and told his master, saying, The girl who is from the land of Israel spoke such and such.
5:5 Then the king of Aram said, Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel. So he departed and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand of gold, and ten changes of clothes.
5:6 And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, which said, And now as this letter comes to you, behold, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy.
5:7 But when the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, Am I God, to kill and to keep alive, that this man is sending to me to cure a man of his leprosy? But consider now, and see how he is seeking a quarrel against me.
5:8 Now it happened, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Why did you tear your clothes? Just have him come to me, and he shall learn that there is a prophet in Israel.
5:9 So Naaman came with his horses and his chariots, and stood at the doorway of Elishas house.
5:10 And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh will be restored to you and be clean.
5:11 But Naaman was furious and went away, and he said, Behold, I thought, He will certainly come out to me, and stand and call on the name of the his God, and wave his hand over the site and cure the leprosy.
5:12 Are Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, not better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.
5:13 Then his servants approached and spoke to him, saying, My father, had the prophet told you great thing, would you not have done ? How much more , when he says to you, Wash, and be clean?
5:14 So he went down and dipped in the Jordan seven times, in accordance with the word of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
5:15 Then he returned to the man of God with all his company, and came and stood before him. And he said, Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, except in Israel; so please accept a gift from your servant now.
5:16 But he said, As the lives, before whom I stand, I will accept nothing. And he urged him to accept , but he refused.
5:17 Then Naaman said, If not, please let your servant be given two mules load of earth; for your servant will no longer offer a burnt offering nor a sacrifice to other gods, but to the .
5:18 Regarding this matter may the forgive your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my hand and I bow down in the house of Rimmon, when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the please forgive your servant in this matter.
5:19 He said to him, Go in peace. So he went some distance from him.

5:21 So Gehazi pursued Naaman. When Naaman saw running after him, he came down from the chariot to meet him and said, well?
5:22 And he said, well. My master has sent me, saying, Behold, just now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.
5:23 Naaman said, Be sure to take two talents. And he urged him, and tied up two talents of silver in two bags with two changes of clothes, and gave to two of his servants; and they carried before him.

9:1 Now Elisha the prophet summoned one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, Get ready and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
9:2 When you arrive there, then look there for Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in and have him get up from among his brothers, and bring him to an inner room.
9:3 Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head, and say, This is what the says: I have anointed you king over Israel. Then open the door and flee, and do not wait.
9:4 So the young man, the servant of the prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
9:5 When he arrived, behold, the commanders of the army were sitting, and he said, I have a word for you, commander. And Jehu said, For which of us? And he said, For you, commander.
9:6 He then got up and went into the house, and poured the oil on his head and said to him, This is what the , the God of Israel says: I have anointed you king over the people of the , over Israel.
9:7 And you shall strike the house of Ahab your master, so that I may avenge the blood of My servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the , at the hand of Jezebel.
9:8 For the entire house of Ahab shall perish, and I will eliminate from Ahab every male person both slave and free in Israel.
9:9 I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.
9:10 The dogs will eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and no one will bury . Then he opened the door and fled.
9:11 Now Jehu went out to the servants of his master, and one said to him, Is everything well? Why did this crazy fellow come to you? And he said to them, You know the man and his talk.
9:12 And they said, It is a lie; tell us now. And he said, Such and such he said to me, saying, This is what the says: I have anointed you king over Israel.
9:13 Then they hurried, and each man took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps, and blew the trumpet, saying, Jehu is king!
9:14 So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram with all Israel was defending Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram,
9:15 but King Joram had returned to Jezreel to have himself healed of the wounds which the Arameans had inflicted on him when he fought Hazael king of Aram. So Jehu said , If is your intent, let no one escape from the city to go tell in Jezreel.
9:16 Then Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel, since Joram was lying there . And Ahaziah the king of Judah had come down to see Joram.
9:17 Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel and he saw the company of Jehu as he came, and he said, I see a company. And Joram said, Take a horseman and send him to meet them and have him ask, Is peace?
9:18 So a horseman went to meet him and said, This is what the king says: Is peace? But Jehu said, How is peace any business of yours? Turn follow me. And the watchman reported, The messenger came to them, but he did not return.
9:19 Then he sent a second horseman, and he came to them and said, This is what the king says: Is peace? And Jehu answered, How is peace any business of yours? Turn follow me.
9:20 And the watchman reported, He came up to them, but he did not return; and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously.
9:21 Then Joram said, Get ready. And they made his chariot ready. Then Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu and found him on the property of Naboth the Jezreelite.
9:22 When Joram saw Jehu, he said, Is peace, Jehu? And he answered, What peace, so long as your mother Jezebels acts of prostitution and witchcraft are so many?
9:23 So Joram turned back and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, treachery, Ahaziah!
9:24 Then Jehu drew his bow with his full strength and shot Joram between his arms; and the arrow went through his heart, and he sank in his chariot.
9:25 And said to Bidkar his officer, Pick up and throw him on the property of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember, you and I were riding together after his father Ahab, that the brought this pronouncement against him:
9:26 I have certainly seen yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, declares the , and I will repay you on this property, declares the . Now then, pick him up and throw him on the property, in accordance with the word of the .
9:27 When Ahaziah the king of Judah saw , he fled by way of the garden house. But Jehu pursued him and said, Shoot him too, in the chariot. at the ascent of Gur, which is at Ibleam. But he fled to Megiddo and died there.
9:28 Then his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his grave with his fathers in the city of David.
9:29 Now in the eleventh year of Joram, the son of Ahab, Ahaziah became king over Judah.
9:30 When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard , and she put makeup on her eyes and adorned her head, and looked down through the window.
9:31 As Jehu entered the gate, she said, Is peace, Zimri, his masters murderer?
9:32 Then he raised his face toward the window and said, Who is with me, who? And two three officials looked down at him.
9:33 Then he said, Throw her down. So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her underfoot.
9:34 When he came in, he ate and drank; and he said, See now to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a kings daughter.
9:35 So they went to bury her, but they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.
9:36 Therefore they returned and informed him. And he said, This is the word of the , which He spoke by His servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, On the property of Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel;
9:37 and the corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the face of the field in the property of Jezreel, so they cannot say, This is Jezebel.
10:1 Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,
10:2 And now, when this letter comes to you, since your masters sons are with you, as well as the chariots and horses, and a fortified city and the weapons,
10:3 select the best and most capable of your masters sons and seat on his fathers throne, and fight for your masters house.
10:4 But they feared greatly and said, Behold, the two kings did not stand before him; how then can we stand?
10:5 And the one who in charge of the household, and the one who in charge of the city, and the elders, and the guardians of , sent to Jehu, saying, We are your servants, and everything that you tell us we will do. We will not appoint any man king; do what is good in your sight.
10:6 Then he wrote them a letter a second time, saying, If you are on my side, and will listen to my voice, take the heads of the men, your masters sons, and come to me at Jezreel about this time tomorrow. Now the kings sons, seventy men, with the great people of the city, were raising them.
10:7 When the letter came to them, they took the kings sons and slaughtered , seventy men, and put their heads in baskets, and sent to him at Jezreel.
10:8 When the messenger came and informed him, saying, They have brought the heads of the kings sons, he said, Put them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning.
10:9 Now in the morning he went out and stood and said to all the people, You are innocent; behold, I conspired against my master and killed him, but who killed all these?
10:10 Know then that nothing of the word of the , which the spoke concerning the house of Ahab, shall fall to the earth, for the has done what He spoke through His servant Elijah.
10:11 So Jehu killed all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, his acquaintances, and his priests, until he left him without a survivor.
10:12 Then he set out and went to Samaria. On the way while he was at Beth-eked of the shepherds,
10:13 Jehu encountered the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said, Who are you? And they answered, We are the relatives of Ahaziah; and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother.
10:14 Then he said, Take them alive. So they took them alive, and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men; and he left none of them.
10:15 Now when he had gone from there, he encountered Jehonadab the son of Rechab to meet him; and he greeted him and said to him, Is your heart right, just as my heart with your heart? And Jehonadab answered, It is. , If it is, give your hand. And he gave his hand, and he pulled him up to him into the chariot.
10:16 Then he said, Come with me and see my zeal for the . So he had him ride in his chariot.
10:17 When he came to Samaria, he killed all who remained to Ahab in Samaria, until he had eliminated them, in accordance with the word of the which He spoke to Elijah.
10:18 Then Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.
10:19 Now, summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers and all his priests; let no one go missing, because I have a great sacrifice for Baal; whoever is missing shall not live. But Jehu did it in deception, in order to eliminate the worshipers of Baal.
10:20 And Jehu said, Proclaim a holy assembly for Baal. And they proclaimed .
10:21 Then Jehu sent throughout Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal came, so that there was not a person left who did not come. And when they entered the house of Baal, the house of Baal was filled from one end to the other.
10:22 And he said to the one who in charge of the wardrobe, Bring out garments for all the worshipers of Baal. So he brought out the garments for them.
10:23 Then Jehu entered the house of Baal with Jehonadab the son of Rechab; and he said to the worshipers of Baal, Search carefully and see to it that there is here with you none of the servants of the , but only the worshipers of Baal.
10:24 Then they entered to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed for himself eighty men outside, and he had said, The one who allows any of the men whom I bring into your hands to escape shall give up his life in exchange.
10:25 Then it came about, as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the guard and to the royal officers, Go in, kill them; let none come out. So they killed them with the edge of the sword; and the guard and the royal officers threw out, and went to the sanctuary of the house of Baal.
10:26 They brought out the memorial stones of the house of Baal and burned them.
10:27 They also tore down the memorial stone of Baal and tore down the house of Baal, and made it a latrine to this day.
10:28 So Jehu eradicated Baal from Israel.
10:29 However, the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel, from these Jehu did not desist, the golden calves that at Bethel and at Dan.
10:30 Yet the said to Jehu, Because you have done well in performing what is right in My eyes, have done to the house of Ahab in accordance with everything that in My heart, your sons to the fourth shall sit on the throne of Israel.
10:31 But Jehu was not careful to walk in the Law of the , the God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not desist from the sins of Jeroboam, into which he misled Israel.
10:32 In those days the began to cut off from Israel; and Hazael defeated throughout the territory of Israel:
10:33 from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites; from Aroer, which is by the Valley of the Arnon, that is, Gilead and Bashan.
10:34 Now the rest of the acts of Jehu and everything that he did and all his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
10:35 And Jehu lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. And his son Jehoahaz became king in his place.
10:36 So the time which Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-eight years.
11:1 When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and eliminated all the royal children.
11:2 But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and abducted him from among the kings sons who were being put to death, him and his nurse in the bedroom. So they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
11:3 So he was kept hidden with her in the house of the for six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.
11:4 Now in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and brought the captains of hundreds of the Carites and of the guards, and brought them to himself at the house of the . Then he made a covenant with them and put them under oath at the house of the , and showed them the kings son.
11:5 And he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that you shall do: a third of you, who come in on the Sabbath and keep watch over the kings house
11:6 (a third also at the gate Sur, and a third at the gate behind the guards), shall keep watch over the house for defense.
11:7 And two parts of you, all who go out on the Sabbath, shall also keep watch over the house of the for the king.
11:8 Then you shall surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand; and whoever comes within the ranks shall be put to death. And you are to be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.
11:9 So the captains of hundreds acted in accordance with everything that Jehoiada the priest commanded. And each one of them took his men who were to come in on the Sabbath, along with those who were to go out on the Sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
11:10 Then the priest gave the captains of hundreds the spears and shields that King Davids, which in the house of the .
11:11 The guards stood, each with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, around the king.
11:12 Then he brought the kings son out, and put the crown on him and the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, live the king!
11:13 When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards the people, she came to the people at the house of the .
11:14 And she looked, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom, with the captains and the trumpeters beside the king; and all the people of the land were joyful and were blowing trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, Conspiracy! Conspiracy!
11:15 And Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds who were appointed over the army and said to them, Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her, put to death with the sword! For the priest said, She is not to be put to death at the house of the .
11:16 So they seized her, and when they brought her to the horses entrance of the kings house, she was put to death there.
11:17 Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the , the king, and the people, that they would be the people, and between the king and the people.
11:18 And all the people of the land came to the house of Baal and tore it down; they thoroughly smashed his altars and his images in pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. Then the priest appointed sentries over the house of the .
11:19 And he took the captains of hundreds and the Carites, and the guards and all the people of the land; and they brought the king down from the house of the , and came by way of the gate of the guards to the kings house. And he sat on the throne of the kings.
11:20 So all the people of the land rejoiced and the city was peaceful. For they had put Athaliah to death with the sword at the kings house.
11:21 Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
12:1 In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem; and his mothers name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
12:2 Jehoash did what was right in the sight of the all his days that Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
12:3 Only the high places did not end; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
12:4 Then Jehoash said to the priests, All the money of the sacred offerings which is brought into the house of the , in current money, the money of each mans assessment all the money which anyones heart prompts him to bring into the house of the ,
12:5 the priests are to take it for themselves, each from his acquaintance; and they shall repair damage to the house wherever any damage is found.
12:6 But it came about that in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had not repaired damage to the house.
12:7 So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest, and the priests, and said to them, Why do you not repair damage to the house? Now then, you are not to take money from your acquaintances, but give it up for the damage to the house.
12:8 The priests then agreed that they would not take money from the people, nor would they repair damage to the house.
12:9 Instead, Jehoiada the priest took a chest and drilled a hole in its lid and put it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into the house of the ; and the priests who guarded the threshold put in it all the money that was brought into the house of the .
12:10 When they saw that there was a great money in the chest, the kings scribe and the high priest went up and tied up in bags, and counted the money that was found in the house of the .
12:11 And they handed the money which was assessed over to those who did the work, who had the oversight of the house of the ; and they paid it out to the carpenters and the builders who worked on the house of the ;
12:12 and to the masons and the stonecutters, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the damage to the house of the , and for everything that was laid out for the house to repair it.
12:13 However there were not made for the house of the silver cups, shears, bowls, trumpets, any receptacles of gold, or receptacles of silver from the money which was brought into the house of the ;
12:14 for they gave that to those who did the work, and with it they repaired the house of the .
12:15 Moreover, they did not require an accounting from the men into whose hands they gave the money to pay to those who did the work, because they acted faithfully.
12:16 The money from the guilt offerings and the money from the sin offerings was not brought into the house of the ; it belonged to the priests.
12:17 Then Hazael the king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it, and Hazael was intent on going up against Jerusalem.
12:18 So Jehoash king of Judah took all the sacred offerings that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own sacred offerings, and all the gold that was found among the treasuries of the house of the and of the kings house, and sent to Hazael king of Aram. Then he withdrew from Jerusalem.
12:19 Now the rest of the acts of Joash and everything that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
12:20 And his servants rose up and formed a conspiracy; and they struck and killed Joash at the house of Millo going down to Silla.
12:21 For Jozacar the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, struck and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Amaziah became king in his place.
13:1 In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu became king over Israel at Samaria, for seventeen years.
13:2 He did evil in the sight of the , and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel; he did not turn from them.
13:3 So the anger of the was kindled against Israel, and He continually handed them over to Hazael king of Aram, and to Ben-hadad, the son of Hazael.
13:4 Then Jehoahaz appeased the , and the listened to him; for He saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Aram oppressed them.
13:5 And the gave Israel a savior, so that they escaped from under the hand of the Arameans; and the sons of Israel lived in their tents as previously.
13:6 Nevertheless they did not abandon the sins of the house of Jeroboam, into which he misled Israel; , they walked in them; and the Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.
13:7 For he left to Jehoahaz no more of the army than fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand infantry, because the king of Aram had eliminated them and made them like the dust at threshing.
13:8 Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did and his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
13:9 And Jehoahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and his son Joash became king in his place.
13:10 In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, for sixteen years.
13:11 He did evil in the sight of the ; he did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel; , he walked in them.
13:12 Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
13:13 So Joash lay down with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
13:14 When Elisha became sick with the illness of which he was to die, Joash the king of Israel came down to him, and wept over him and said, My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!
13:15 And Elisha said to him, Take a bow and arrows. So he took a bow and arrows.
13:16 Then said to the king of Israel, Lay your hand on the bow. And he laid his hand , then Elisha put his hands on the kings hands.
13:17 And he said, Open the window toward the east, and he opened . Then Elisha said, Shoot! So he shot. And he said, The arrow of victory, and the arrow of victory over Aram; for you will defeat the Arameans at Aphek until you have put an end .
13:18 Then he said, Take the arrows, and he took . And he said to the king of Israel, Strike the ground, and he struck three times and stopped.
13:19 Then the man of God became angry at him and said, You should have struck five or six times, then you would have struck Aram until you put an end . But now you shall strike Aram three times.
13:20 And Elisha died, and they buried him. Now the marauding bands of the Moabites would invade the land in the spring of the year.
13:21 And as they were burying a man, behold, they saw a marauding band; and they threw the man into the grave of Elisha. And when the man touched the bones of Elisha he revived and stood up on his feet.
13:22 Now Hazael king of Aram had oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
13:23 But the was gracious to them and had compassion on them and turned to them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and He was unwilling to eliminate them or cast them away from His presence until now.
13:24 When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.
13:25 Then Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz again took from the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael the cities which he had taken in war from the hand of his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash defeated him and recovered the cities of Israel.
14:1 In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz king of Israel, Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah became king.
14:2 He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And his mothers name was Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.
14:3 He did what was right in the sight of the , yet not like his father David; he acted in accordance with everything that his father Joash had done.
14:4 Only the high places were not eliminated; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
14:5 Now it came about, as soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, that he killed his servants who had killed the king, his father.
14:6 But he did not put the sons of the murderers to death, in obedience to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, as the commanded, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the sons, nor the sons be put to death for the fathers; but each shall be put to death for his own sin.
14:7 He killed ten thousand the Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and took Sela by war, and named it Joktheel, to this day.
14:8 Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, lets face each other .
14:9 But Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thorn bush that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son in marriage. But a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thorn bush.
14:10 You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart is elated. Enjoy the glory and stay home; for why should you get involved in trouble so that you would fall, you and Judah with you?
14:11 But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up; and they faced each other, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
14:12 And Judah was defeated by Israel, and they fled, every man to his tent.
14:13 Then Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and came to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
14:14 And he took all the gold and silver and all the utensils which were found in the house of the , and in the treasuries of the kings house, the hostages as well, and returned to Samaria.
14:15 Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash that he did, and his might and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
14:16 So Jehoash lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and his son Jeroboam became king in his place.
14:17 Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
14:18 Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
14:19 They formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent to Lachish after him and they killed him there.
14:20 Then they carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
14:21 And all the people of Judah took Azariah, who sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
14:22 He built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king lay down with his fathers.
14:23 In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria, for forty-one years.
14:24 He did evil in the sight of the ; he did not abandon all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel.
14:25 He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah, in accordance with the word of the , the God of Israel, which He spoke through His servant Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher.
14:26 For the saw the misery of Israel, very bitter; for there was neither bond nor free , nor was there any helper for Israel.
14:27 Yet the did not say that He would wipe out the name of Israel from under heaven, but He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.
14:28 Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did and his might, how he fought and how he recovered for Israel Damascus and Hamath, to Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
14:29 And Jeroboam lay down with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and his son Zechariah became king in his place.
15:1 In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
15:2 He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mothers name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
15:3 He did what was right in the sight of the , in accordance with everything that his father Amaziah had done.
15:4 Only the high places were not eliminated; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
15:5 And the afflicted the king, so that he had leprosy to the day of his death. And he lived in a separate house, while Jotham the kings son was in charge of the household, judging the people of the land.
15:6 Now the rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
15:7 And Azariah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Jotham became king in his place.
15:8 In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria for six months.
15:9 He did evil in the sight of the , just as his fathers had done; he did not desist from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel.
15:10 Then Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him in the presence of the people and killed him, and reigned in his place.
15:11 Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, behold they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
15:12 This is the word of the which He spoke to Jehu, saying, Your sons the fourth shall sit on the throne of Israel. And so it was.
15:13 Shallum the son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned for one month in Samaria.
15:14 Then Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and struck Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, and killed him and became king in his place.
15:15 Now the rest of the acts of Shallum and his conspiracy which he formed, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
