29:7 When I went out to the gate of the city, When I took my seat in the public square,
29:8 The young men saw me and hid themselves, And the old men arose stood.
29:9 The leaders stopped talking And put hands on their mouths;
29:10 The voices of the prominent people were hushed, And their tongues stuck to their palates.
29:11 For an ear heard, it called me blessed, And when an eye saw, it testified in support of me,
29:12 Because I saved the poor who cried for help, And the orphan who had no helper.
29:13 The blessing of the one who was about to perish came upon me, And I made the widows heart sing for joy.
29:14 I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; My justice was like a robe and a headband.
29:15 I was eyes to those who were blind, And feet to those who could not walk.
29:16 I was a father to the poor, And I investigated the case which I did not know.
29:17 I broke the jaws of the wicked And rescued the prey from his teeth.
29:18 Then I thought, I will die with my family, And I will multiply days as the sand.
29:19 My root is spread out to the waters, And dew lies on my branch all night.
29:20 My glory is new with me, And my bow is renewed in my hand.
29:21 To me they listened and waited, And they kept silent for my advice.
29:22 After my words they did not again, And my speech dropped on them.
29:23 They waited for me as for the rain, And opened their mouths as for the late rain.
29:24 I smiled at them they did not believe, And they did not look at my kindness ungraciously.
29:25 I chose a way for them and sat as chief, And lived as a king among the troops, As one who comforted the mourners.
30:1 But now those who are younger than I mock me, Whose fathers I refused to put with the dogs of my flock.
30:2 Indeed, what the strength of their hands to me? Vigor had perished from them.
30:3 From poverty and famine they are gaunt, They who gnaw at the dry ground by night in waste and desolation,
30:4 Who pluck saltweed by the bushes, And whose food is the root of the broom shrub.
30:5 They are driven from the community; They shout against them as a thief,
30:6 So that they live on the slopes of ravines, holes the ground and the rocks.
30:7 Among the bushes they cry out; Under the weeds they are gathered together.
30:8 Worthless fellows, even those without a name, They were cast out from the land.
30:9 And now I have become their taunt, And I have become a byword to them.
30:10 They loathe me stand aloof from me, And they do not refrain from spitting in my face.
30:11 Because He has undone my bowstring and afflicted me, They have cast off the bridle before me.
30:12 On the right hand their mob arises; They push aside my feet and pile up their ways of destruction against me.
30:13 They break up my path, They promote my destruction; No one restrains them.
30:14 As a wide gap they come, Amid the storm they roll on.
30:15 Sudden terrors are turned upon me; They chase my dignity like the wind, And my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
30:16 And now my soul is poured out within me; Days of misery have seized me.
30:17 At night it pierces my bones within me, And my gnawing do not rest.
30:18 By a great force my garment is distorted; It ties me up like the collar of my coat.
30:19 He has thrown me into the mire, And I have become like dust and ashes.
30:20 I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer me; I stand up, and You turn Your attention against me.
30:21 You have become cruel to me; With the strength of Your hand You persecute me.
30:22 You lift me up to the wind make me ride ; And You dissolve me in a storm.
30:23 For I know that You will bring me to death, And to the house of meeting for all living.
30:24 Yet does one in a heap of ruins not reach out hand, Or in his disaster does he not cry out for help?
30:25 Have I not wept for the one whose life is hard? Was my soul not grieved for the needy?
30:26 When I expected good, evil came; When I waited for light, darkness came.
30:27 I am seething within and cannot rest; Days of misery confront me.
30:28 I go about mourning without comfort; I stand up in the assembly cry out for help.
30:29 I have become a brother to jackals, And a companion of ostriches.
30:30 My skin turns black on me, And my bones burn with fever.
30:31 Therefore my harp is turned to mourning, And my flute to the sound of those who weep.
31:1 I have made a covenant with my eyes; How then could I look at a virgin?
31:2 And what is the portion of God from above, Or the inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
31:3 Is it not disaster to the criminal, And misfortune to those who practice injustice?
31:4 Does He not see my ways, And count all my steps?
31:5 If I have walked with deception, And my foot has hurried after deceit,
31:6 Let Him weigh me with accurate scales, And let God know my integrity.
31:7 If my step has turned from the way, Or my heart followed my eyes, Or spot has stuck to my hands,
31:8 Let me sow and another eat, And let my crops be uprooted.
31:9 If my heart has been enticed by a woman, Or I have lurked at my neighbors doorway,
31:10 May my wife grind for another, And let others kneel down over her.
31:11 For that would be a lustful crime; Moreover, it would be wrongdoing judges.
31:12 For it would be fire that consumes to Abaddon, And would uproot all my increase.
31:13 If I have rejected the claim of my male or female slaves When they filed a complaint against me,
31:14 What then could I do when God arises? And when He calls me to account, how am I to answer Him?
31:15 Did He who made me in the womb not make him, And the same one create us in the womb?
31:16 If I have kept the poor from desire, Or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
31:17 Or have eaten my morsel alone, And the orphan has not shared it
31:18 (But from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, And from my infancy I guided her),
31:19 If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, Or that the needy had no covering,
31:20 If his waist has not thanked me, And if he has not been warmed with the fleece of my sheep,
31:21 If I have lifted up my hand against the orphan, Because I saw I had support in the gate,
31:22 May my shoulder fall from socket, And my arm be broken off at the elbow.
31:23 For disaster from God is a terror to me, And because of His majesty I can do nothing.
31:24 If I have put my confidence gold, And called fine gold my trust,
31:25 If I have gloated because my wealth was great, And because my hand had obtained much;
31:26 If I have looked at the sun when it shone, Or the moon going in splendor,
31:27 And my heart was secretly enticed, And my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
31:28 That too would have been a guilty deed judgment, For I would have denied God above.
31:29 Have I rejoiced at the misfortune of my enemy, Or become excited when evil found him?
31:30 No, I have not allowed my mouth to sin By asking for his life in a curse.
31:31 Have the people of my tent not said, Who can find one who has not been satisfied with his meat?
31:32 The stranger has not spent the night outside, I have opened my doors to the traveler.
31:33 Have I covered my wrongdoings like a man, By hiding my guilt in my shirt pocket,
31:34 Because I feared the great multitude And the contempt of families terrified me, And I kept silent and did not go out of doors?
31:35 Oh that I had one to hear me! Here is my signature; Let the Almighty answer me! And the indictment which my adversary has written,
31:36 I would certainly carry it on my shoulder, I would tie it to myself a garland.
31:37 I would declare to Him the number of my steps; Like a prince, I would approach Him.
31:38 If my land cries out against me, And its furrows weep together;
31:39 If I have eaten its fruit without money, Or have caused its owners to lose their lives,
31:40 May the thorn-bush grow instead of wheat, And stinkweed instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
32:1 Then these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
32:2 But the anger of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned against Job; his anger burned because he justified himself before God.
32:3 And his anger burned against his three friends because they had found no answer, yet they had condemned Job.
32:4 Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were years older than he.
32:5 But when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, his anger burned.
32:6 So Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite spoke out and said, I am young in years and you are old; Therefore I was shy and afraid to tell you what I think.
32:7 I thought age should speak, And increased years should teach wisdom.
32:8 But it is a spirit in mankind, And the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
32:9 The abundant may not be wise, Nor may elders understand justice.
32:10 So I say, Listen to me, I too will tell what I think.
32:11 Behold, I waited for your words, I listened to your skillful speech, While you pondered what to say.
32:12 I also paid close attention to you; But indeed, there was no one who refuted Job, Not one of you who answered his words.
32:13 So do not say, We have found wisdom: God will defeat him, not man.
32:14 But he has not presented words against me, Nor will I reply to him with your arguments.
32:15 They are dismayed, they no longer answer; Words have failed them.
32:16 Should I wait, because they are not speaking, Because they have stopped no longer answer?
32:17 I too will give my share of answers; I also will tell my opinion.
32:18 For I am full of words; The spirit within me compels me.
32:19 Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; Like new wineskins, it is about to burst.
32:20 Let me speak so that I may get relief; Let me open my lips and answer.
32:21 Let me be partial to no one, Nor flatter man.
32:22 For I do not know how to flatter, my Maker would quickly take me away.
33:1 However, please hear my speech, Job, And listen to all my words.
33:2 Behold now, I open my mouth, My tongue in my mouth speaks.
33:3 My words are the integrity of my heart, And my lips speak knowledge sincerely.
33:4 The Spirit of God has made me, And the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
33:5 Refute me if you can; Line up against me, take your stand.
33:6 Behold, I belong to God, like you; I too have been formed out of the clay.
33:7 Behold, no fear of me should terrify you, Nor should my pressure weigh heavily on you.
33:8 You have in fact spoken while I listened, And I heard the sound of words:
33:9 I am pure, without wrongdoing; I am innocent and there is no guilt in me.
33:10 Behold, He invents criticisms against me; He counts me as His enemy.
33:11 He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches all my paths.
33:12 Behold, let me respond to you, you are not right in this, For God is greater than mankind.
33:13 Why do you complain to Him That He does not give an account of all His doings?
33:14 Indeed God speaks once, Or twice, no one notices it.
33:15 In a dream, a vision of the night, When deep sleep falls on people, While they slumber in their beds,
33:16 Then He opens the ears of people, And horrifies them with warnings,
33:17 So that He may turn a person away conduct, And keep a man from pride;
33:18 He keeps his soul back from the pit, And his life from perishing by the spear.
33:19 is also rebuked by pain in his bed, And with constant complaint in his bones,
33:20 So that his life loathes bread, And his soul, food that he should crave.
33:21 His flesh wastes away from sight, And his bones, were not seen, stick out.
33:22 Then his soul comes near to the pit, And his life to those who bring death.
33:23 If there is an interceding angel for him, One out of a thousand, To remind a person of what is right for him,
33:24 And he is gracious to him, and says, Free him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom;
33:25 Let his flesh become fresher than in youth, Let him return to the days of his youthful vigor;
33:26 he will pray to God, and He will accept him, So that he may see His face with joy, And He will restore His righteousness to person.
33:27 He will sing to people and say, I have sinned and perverted what is right, And it is not proper for me.
33:28 He has redeemed my soul from going to the pit, And my life will see the light.
33:29 Behold, God does all these for a man two or three times,
33:30 To bring back his soul from the pit, So that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
33:31 Pay attention, Job, listen to me; Keep silent, and let me speak.
33:32 if you have anything to say, answer me; Speak, for I would take pleasure in justifying you.
33:33 If not, listen to me; Keep silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
34:1 Then Elihu continued and said,
34:2 Hear my words, you wise men, And listen to me, you who understand.
34:3 For the ear tests words As the palate tastes food.
34:4 Let us choose for ourselves what is right; Let us understand among ourselves what is good.
34:5 For Job has said, I am righteous, But God has taken away my right;
34:6 Should I lie about my right? My wound is incurable, without wrongdoing.
34:7 What man is like Job, Who drinks up derision like water,
34:8 Who goes in company with the workers of injustice, And walks with wicked people?
34:9 For he has said, It is of no use to a man When he becomes friends with God.
34:10 Therefore, listen to me, you men of understanding. Far be it from God to do evil, And from the Almighty to do wrong.
34:11 For He repays a person for his work, And lets happen in correspondence to a mans behavior.
34:12 God certainly will not act wickedly, And the Almighty will not pervert justice.
34:13 Who gave Him authority over the earth? And who has placed the whole world ?
34:14 If He were to determine to do so, If He were to gather His spirit and His breath to Himself,
34:15 Humanity would perish together, And mankind would return to dust.
34:16 But if understanding, hear this; Listen to the sound of my words.
34:17 Shall one who hates justice rule? And will you condemn the righteous mighty One,
34:18 Who says to a king, You worthless one, To nobles, You wicked one;
34:19 Who shows no partiality to the prominent, Nor regards the rich as above the poor, Since they are all the work of His hands?
34:20 In a moment they die, and at midnight People are shaken and pass away, And the powerful are taken away without a hand.
34:21 For His eyes are upon the ways of a person, And He sees all his steps.
34:22 There is no darkness or deep shadow Where the workers of injustice can hide themselves.
34:23 For He does not consider a person further, That he should go before God in judgment.
34:24 He breaks in pieces the mighty without investigation, And sets others in their place.
34:25 Therefore He knows their deeds, And He overthrows in the night, And they are crushed.
34:26 He strikes them like the wicked In a public place,
34:27 Because they turned aside from following Him, And had no regard for any of His ways,
34:28 So that they caused the cry of the poor to come to Him, And that He would hear the cry of the afflicted—
34:29 When He keeps quiet, who can condemn? And when He hides His face, who then can look at Him, That is, regarding both nation and a person?—
34:30 So that godless people would not rule, Nor be snares for the people.
34:31 For has anyone said to God, I have endured ; I will not offend ;
34:32 Teach me what I do not see; If I have done wrong, I will not do it again?
34:33 Shall repay on your terms, because you have rejected ? For you must choose, and not I; Therefore declare what you know.
34:34 Men of understanding will say to me, And a wise man who hears me,
34:35 Job speaks without knowledge, And his words are without wisdom.
34:36 Oh that Job were tested to the limit, Because he answers like sinners.
34:37 For he adds rebellion to his sin; He claps his hands among us, And multiplies his words against God.
35:1 Then Elihu continued and said,
35:2 Do you think this is in accordance with justice? Do you say, My righteousness is more than Gods?
35:3 For you say, What advantage will it be to You? What benefit will I have, more than I had sinned?
35:4 I will answer you, And your friends with you.
35:5 Look at the heavens and see; And look at the clouds—they are higher than you.
35:6 If you have sinned, what do you accomplish against Him? And if your wrongdoings are many, what do you do to Him?
35:7 If you are righteous, what do you give to Him, Or what does He receive from your hand?
35:8 Your wickedness is for a man like yourself, And your righteousness is for a son of man.
35:9 Because of the multitude of oppressions they cry out; They cry for help because of the arm of the mighty.
35:10 But no one says, Where is God my Maker, Who gives songs in the night,
35:11 Who teaches us more than the animals of the earth And makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?
35:12 There they cry out, but He does not answer Because of the pride of evil people.
35:13 God certainly will not listen to an empty , Nor will the Almighty regard it.
35:14 How much less when you say you do not look at Him, The case is before Him, and you must wait for Him!
35:15 And now, because He has not avenged His anger, Nor has He acknowledged wrongdoing well,
35:16 So Job opens his mouth empty ; He multiplies words without knowledge.
36:1 Then Elihu continued and said,
36:2 Wait for me a little, and I will show you That there is still more to be said on Gods behalf.
36:3 I will bring my knowledge from afar, And ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
36:4 For truly my words are not false; One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.
36:5 Behold, God is mighty but does not reject ; mighty in strength of understanding.
36:6 He does not keep the wicked alive, But gives justice to the afflicted.
36:7 He does not withdraw His eyes from the righteous, But with kings on the throne He has seated them forever, and they are exalted.
36:8 And if they are bound in shackles, And are caught in the snares of misery,
36:9 Then He declares to them their work And their wrongdoings, that they have been arrogant.
36:10 He opens their ears to instruction, And commands that they return from injustice.
36:11 If they listen and serve , They will end their days in prosperity, And their years in happiness.
36:12 But if they do not listen, they will perish by the sword, And die without knowledge.
36:13 But the godless in heart nurture anger; They do not call for help when He binds them.
36:14 They die in youth, And their life among the cult prostitutes.
36:15 He rescues the afflicted in their misery, And opens their ears in oppression.
36:16 Then indeed, He induced you away from the mouth of distress, instead of it, a broad place with no constraint; And your table was full of rich food.
36:17 But you were full of judgment on the wicked; Judgment and justice take hold .
36:18 that wrath does not entice you to mockery; And do not let the greatness of the ransom turn you aside.
36:19 Will your cry for help keep you from distress, Or all the exertions of strength?
36:20 Do not long for the night, When people vanish in their places.
36:21 Be careful, do not turn to evil, For you preferred this to misery.
36:22 Behold, God is exalted in His power; Who is a teacher like Him?
36:23 Who has appointed Him His way, And who has said, You have done wrong?
36:24 Remember that you are to exalt His work, Of which people have sung.
36:25 All people have seen it; Mankind looks at it from afar.
36:26 Behold, God is exalted, and we do not know ; The number of His years is unsearchable.
36:27 For He draws up the drops of water; They distill rain from its celestial stream,
36:28 Which clouds pour down; They drip upon mankind abundantly.
36:29 Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, The thundering of His pavilion?
36:30 Behold, He spreads His lightning about Him, And He covers the depths of the sea.
36:31 For by them He judges peoples; He gives food in abundance.
36:32 He covers hands with the lightning, And commands it to strike the target.
36:33 Its thundering voice declares His presence; The livestock also, concerning what is coming up.
37:1 At this also my heart trembles, And leaps from its place.
37:2 Listen closely to the thunder of His voice, And the rumbling that goes out from His mouth.
37:3 Under the whole heaven He lets it loose, And His lightning to the ends of the earth.
37:4 After it, a voice roars; He thunders with His majestic voice, And He does not restrain the lightning when His voice is heard.
37:5 God thunders wondrously with His voice, Doing great things which we do not comprehend.
37:6 For to the snow He says, Fall on the earth, And to the downpour and the rain, Be strong.
37:7 He seals the hand of every person, So that all people may know His work.
37:8 Then the animal goes into its lair And remains in its den.
37:9 From the south comes the storm, And from the north wind the cold.
37:10 From the breath of God ice is made, And the expanse of the waters is frozen.
37:11 He also loads the clouds with moisture; He disperses the cloud of His lightning.
37:12 It changes direction, turning around by His guidance, That it may do whatever He commands it On the face of the inhabited earth.
37:13 Whether for correction, or for His earth, Or for goodness, He causes it to happen.
37:14 Listen to this, Job; Stand and consider the wonders of God.
37:15 Do you know how God establishes them, And makes the lightning of His clouds to shine?
37:16 Do you know about the hovering of the clouds, The wonders of One who is perfect in knowledge,
37:17 You whose garments are hot When the land is still because of the south wind?
37:18 Can you, with Him, spread out the skies, Strong as a cast metal mirror?
37:19 Teach us what we are to say to Him; We cannot present because of darkness.
37:20 Shall it be told Him that I would speak? Or should a man say that he would be swallowed up?
37:21 Now do not see the light which is bright in the skies; But the wind has passed and cleared them.
37:22 From the north comes golden ; Around God is awesome majesty.
37:23 The Almighty—we cannot find Him; He is exalted in power And He will not violate justice and abundant righteousness.
37:24 Therefore people fear Him; He does not regard any who are wise of heart.
38:1 Then the answered Job from the whirlwind and said,
38:2 Who is this who darkens plan By words without knowledge?
38:3 Now tighten the belt on your waist like a man, And I shall ask you, and you inform Me!
38:4 Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth? Tell , if you have understanding,
38:5 Who set its measurements? Since you know. Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
38:6 On what were its bases sunk? Or who laid its cornerstone,
38:7 When the morning stars sang together And all the sons of God shouted for joy?
38:8 Or enclosed the sea with doors When it went out from the womb, bursting forth;
38:9 When I made a cloud its garment, And thick darkness its swaddling bands,
38:10 And I placed boundaries on it And set a bolt and doors,
38:11 And I said, As far as this point you shall come, but no farther; And here your proud waves shall stop?
38:12 Have you ever in your life commanded the morning, made the dawn know its place,
38:13 So that it would take hold of the ends of the earth, And the wicked would be shaken off from it?
38:14 It is changed like clay the seal; And they stand out like a garment.
38:15 Their light is withheld from the wicked, And the uplifted arm is broken.
38:16 Have you entered the springs of the sea, And walked in the depth of the ocean?
38:17 Have the gates of death been revealed to you, And have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
38:18 Have you understood the expanse of the earth? Tell , if you know all this.
38:19 Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And darkness, where is its place,
38:20 That you would take it to its territory, And discern the paths to its home?
38:21 You know, for you were born then, And the number of your days is great!
38:22 Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, And have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
38:23 Which I have reserved for a time of distress, For a day of war and battle?
38:24 Where is the way that the light is divided, the east wind scattered on the earth?
38:25 Who has split a channel for the flood, And a way for the thunderbolt,
38:26 To bring rain on a land without people, a desert without a person in it,
38:27 To satisfy the waste and desolate land, And to make the seeds of grass to sprout?
38:28 Does the rain have a father? Or who has fathered the drops of dew?
38:29 From whose womb has come the ice? And the frost of heaven, who has given it birth?
38:30 Water becomes hard like stone, And the surface of the deep is imprisoned.
38:31 Can you tie up the chains of the Pleiades, Or untie the cords of Orion?
38:32 Can you bring out a constellation in its season, And guide the Bear with her satellites?
38:33 Do you know the ordinances of the heavens, Or do you establish their rule over the earth?
38:34 Can you raise your voice to the clouds, So that an abundance of water will cover you?
38:35 Can you send flashes of lightning, so that they may go And say to you, Here we are?
38:36 Who has put wisdom in the innermost being, Or given understanding to the mind?
38:37 Who can count the clouds by wisdom, And pour out the water jars of the heavens,
38:38 When the dust hardens into a mass And the clods stick together?
38:39 Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, Or satisfy the appetite of young lions,
38:40 When they crouch in hiding places, lie in wait in lair?
38:41 Who prepares feed for the raven When its young cry to God, wander about without food?
39:1 Do you know the time the mountain goats give birth? Do you observe the calving of the deer?
39:2 Can you count the months they fulfill, Or do you know the time they give birth?
39:3 They kneel down, they deliver their young, They get rid of their labor pains.
39:4 Their offspring become strong, they grow up in the open field; They leave and do not return to them.
39:5 Who sent the wild donkey out free? And who opened the bonds of the swift donkey,
39:6 To whom I gave the wilderness as his home, And the salt land as his dwelling place?
39:7 He laughs at the turmoil of the city, He does not hear the shouting of the taskmaster.
39:8 He explores the mountains of his pasture, And searches after every green thing.
39:9 Will the wild bull be willing to serve you, Or will he spend the night at your feeding trough?
39:10 Can you tie down the wild bull in a furrow with ropes, Or will he plow the valleys after you?
39:11 Will you trust him because his strength is great, And leave your labor to him?
39:12 Will you have faith in him that he will return your grain And gather your threshing floor?
39:13 The wings of the ostrich flap joyously, With the pinion and feathers of love,
39:14 For she abandons her eggs to the earth And warms them in the dust,
39:15 And she forgets that a foot may crush them, Or that a wild animal may trample them.
39:16 She treats her young cruelly, as if were not hers; Though her labor is for nothing, is unconcerned,
39:17 Because God has made her forget wisdom, And has not given her a share of understanding.
39:18 When she rushes away on high, She laughs at the horse and his rider.
39:19 Do you give the horse might? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
39:20 Do you make him leap like locusts? His majestic snorting is frightening.
39:21 He paws in the valley, and rejoices in strength; He goes out to meet the battle.
39:22 He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; And he does not turn back from the sword.
39:23 The quiver rattles against him, The flashing spear and javelin.
39:24 He races over the ground with a roar and fury, And he does not stand still when the sound of the trumpet.
39:25 As often as the trumpet he says, Aha! And he senses the battle from afar, And the thunder of the captains and the war cry.
39:26 Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars, Stretching his wings toward the south?
39:27 Is it at your command that the eagle flies high, And makes his nest on high?
39:28 He dwells and spends his nights on the cliff, On the rocky cliff, an inaccessible place.
39:29 From there he tracks food; His eyes look at from afar.
39:30 His young ones also lick up blood greedily; And where the slain are, there he is.

40:3 Then Job answered the and said,
40:4 Behold, I am insignificant; what can I say in response to You? I put my hand on my mouth.
40:5 I have spoken once, and I will not reply; Or twice, and I will add nothing .

40:7 Now tighten the belt on your waist like a man; I will ask you, and you instruct Me.
40:8 Will you really nullify My judgment? Will you condemn Me so that you may be justified?
40:9 Or do you have an arm like God, And can you thunder with a voice like His?
40:10 Adorn yourself with pride and dignity, And clothe yourself with honor and majesty.
40:11 Let out your outbursts of anger, And look at everyone who is arrogant, and humble him.
40:12 Look at everyone who is arrogant, humble him, And trample down the wicked where they stand.
40:13 Hide them together in the dust; Imprison them in the hidden .
40:14 Then I will also confess to you, That your own right hand can save you.
40:15 Behold, Behemoth, which I made as well as you; He eats grass like an ox.
40:16 Behold, his strength in his waist, And his power in the muscles of his belly.
40:17 He hangs his tail like a cedar; The tendons of his thighs are knit together.
40:18 His bones are tubes of bronze; His limbs are like bars of iron.
40:19 He is the first of the ways of God; Let his Maker bring His sword near.
40:20 Indeed the mountains bring him food, And all the animals of the field play there.
40:21 He lies down under the lotus plants, In the hiding place of the reeds and the marsh.
40:22 The lotus plants cover him with shade; The willows of the brook surround him.
40:23 If a river rages, he is not alarmed; He is confident, though the Jordan rushes to his mouth.
40:24 Can anyone capture him when he is on watch, Can anyone pierce nose with barbs?
41:1 Can you drag out Leviathan with a fishhook, And press down his tongue with a rope?
41:2 Can you put a rope in his nose, And pierce his jaw with a hook?
41:3 Will he make many pleas to you, Or will he speak to you gentle words?
41:4 Will he make a covenant with you? Will you take him as a servant forever?
41:5 Will you play with him as with a bird, And tie him down for your young girls?
41:6 Will the traders bargain for him? Will they divide him among the merchants?
41:7 Can you fill his skin with harpoons, Or his head with fishing spears?
41:8 Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle; you will not do it again!
41:9 Behold, your expectation is false; Will you be hurled down even at the sight of him?
41:10 No one is so reckless that he dares to stir him; Who then is he who opposes Me?
41:11 Who has been first to Me, that I should repay ? is under the entire heaven is Mine.
41:12 I will not be silent about his limbs, Or his mighty strength, or his graceful frame.
41:13 Who can strip off his outer covering? Who can pierce his double armor?
41:14 Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth there is terror.
41:15 strong scales are pride, Locked a tight seal.
41:16 One is so close to another That no air can come between them.
41:17 They are joined one to another; They clasp each other and cannot be separated.
41:18 His sneezes flash forth light, And his eyes are like the eye of dawn.
41:19 From his mouth go burning torches; Sparks of fire leap forth.
41:20 From his nostrils smoke goes out As a boiling pot and reeds.
41:21 His breath sets coals aglow, And a flame goes forth from his mouth.
41:22 In his neck dwells strength, And dismay leaps before him.
41:23 The folds of his flesh are joined together, Firm and immovable on him.
41:24 His heart is as firm as a stone, And as firm as a lower millstone.
41:25 When he rises up, the mighty are afraid; Because of the crashing they are bewildered.
41:26 The sword that reaches him cannot prevail, Nor the spear, the dart, or the javelin.
41:27 He regards iron as straw, Bronze as rotten wood.
41:28 The arrow cannot make him flee; Slingstones are turned into stubble for him.
41:29 Clubs are regarded as stubble; He laughs at the rattling of the javelin.
41:30 His underparts are sharp pieces of pottery; He spreads out a threshing sledge on the mud.
41:31 He makes the depths boil like a pot; He makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
41:32 Behind him he illuminates a pathway; One would think the deep to be gray-haired.
41:33 Nothing on earth is like him, One made without fear.
41:34 He looks on everything that is high; He is king over all the sons of pride.
42:1 Then Job answered the and said,
42:2 I know that You can all things, And that no plan is impossible for You.
42:3 Who is this who conceals advice without knowledge? Therefore I have declared that which I did not understand, Things too wonderful for me, which I do not know.
42:4 Please listen, and I will speak; I will ask You, and You instruct me.
42:5 I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear; But now my eye sees You;
42:6 Therefore I retract, And I repent, on dust and ashes.
42:7 It came about after the had spoken these words to Job, that the said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken of Me what is trustworthy, as My servant Job .
42:8 Now therefore, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to My servant Job, and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves, and My servant Job will pray for you. For I will accept him so as not to do with you foolishness , because you have not spoken of Me what is trustworthy, as My servant Job .
42:9 So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the told them; and the accepted Job.
42:10 The also restored the fortunes of Job when he prayed for his friends, and the increased double all that Job had.
42:11 Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all who had known him before came to him, and they ate bread with him in his house; and they sympathized with him and comforted him for all the adversities that the had brought on him. And each one gave him a piece of money, and each a ring of gold.
42:12 The blessed the latter of Job more than his beginning; and he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
42:13 He also had seven sons and three daughters.
42:14 He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
42:15 In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Jobs daughters; and their father gave them inheritances among their brothers.
42:16 After this, Job lived 140 years, and saw his sons and his grandsons, four generations.
42:17 And Job died, an old man and full of days.
PSALMS
PROVERBS
1:1 The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel:
1:2 To know wisdom and instruction, To discern the sayings of understanding,
1:3 To receive instruction in wise behavior, Righteousness, justice, and integrity;
1:4 To give prudence to the naive, To the youth knowledge and discretion,
1:5 A wise person will hear and increase in learning, And a person of understanding will acquire wise counsel,
1:6 To understand a proverb and a saying, The words of the wise and their riddles.
1:7 The fear of the is the beginning of knowledge; Fools despise wisdom and instruction.
1:8 Listen, my son, to your fathers instruction, And do not ignore your mothers teaching;
1:9 For they are a graceful wreath for your head And necklaces for your neck.
1:10 My son, if sinners entice you, Do not consent.
1:11 If they say, Come with us, Lets lie in wait for blood, Lets ambush the innocent without cause;
1:12 Lets swallow them alive like Sheol, Even whole, like those who go down to the pit;
1:13 We will find all of precious wealth, We will fill our houses with plunder;
1:14 Throw in your lot with us; We will all have one money bag,
1:15 My son, do not walk on the way with them. Keep your feet from their path,
1:16 For their feet run to evil, And they are quick to shed blood.
1:17 Indeed, it is useless to spread the net In the sight of any bird;
1:18 But they lie in wait for their own blood; They ambush their own lives.
1:19 Such are the ways of everyone who makes unjust gain; It takes away the life of its possessors.
1:20 Wisdom shouts in the street, She raises her voice in the public square;
1:21 At the head of the noisy she cries out; At the entrance of the gates in the city she declares her sayings:
1:22 How long, you naive ones, will you love simplistic thinking? And scoffers delight themselves in scoffing And fools hate knowledge?
1:23 Turn to my rebuke, Behold, I will pour out my spirit on you; I will make my words known to you.
1:24 Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and no one paid attention;
1:25 And you neglected all my advice And did not want my rebuke;
1:26 I will also laugh at your disaster; I will mock when your dread comes,
1:27 When your dread comes like a storm And your disaster comes like a whirlwind, When distress and anguish come upon you.
1:28 Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; They will seek me diligently but will not find me,
1:29 Because they hated knowledge And did not choose the fear of the .
1:30 They did not accept my advice, They disdainfully rejected every rebuke from me.
1:31 So they shall eat of the fruit of their own way, And be filled with their own schemes.
1:32 For the faithlessness of the naive will kill them, And the complacency of fools will destroy them.
1:33 But whoever listens to me will live securely And will be at ease from the dread of evil.
2:1 My son, if you will receive my words And treasure my commandments within you,
2:2 Make your ear attentive to wisdom; Incline your heart to understanding.
2:3 For if you cry out for insight, raise your voice for understanding;
2:4 If you seek her as silver And search for her as for hidden treasures;
2:5 Then you will understand the fear of the , And discover the knowledge of God.
2:6 For the gives wisdom; From His mouth knowledge and understanding.
2:7 He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; a shield to those who walk in integrity,
2:8 Guarding the paths of justice, And He watches over the way of His godly ones.
2:9 Then you will discern righteousness, justice, And integrity, every good path.
2:10 For wisdom will enter your heart, And knowledge will be delightful to your soul;
2:11 Discretion will watch over you, Understanding will guard you,
2:12 To rescue you from the way of evil, From a person who speaks perverse things;
2:13 those who leave the paths of uprightness To walk in the ways of darkness;
2:14 Who delight in doing evil rejoice in the perversity of evil;
2:15 Whose paths are crooked, And who are devious in their ways;
2:16 To rescue you from the strange woman, From the foreign woman who flatters with her words,
2:17 Who leaves the companion of her youth And forgets the covenant of her God;
2:18 For her house sinks down to death, And her tracks to the dead;
2:19 None who go to her return, Nor do they reach the paths of life.
2:20 So you will walk in the way of good people And keep to the paths of the righteous.
2:21 For the upright will live in the land, And the blameless will remain in it;
2:22 But the wicked will be eliminated from the land, And the treacherous will be torn away from it.
3:1 My son, do not forget my teaching, But have your heart comply with my commandments;
3:2 For length of days and years of life And peace they will add to you.
3:3 Do not let kindness and truth leave you; Bind them around your neck, Write them on the tablet of your heart.
3:4 So you will find favor and a good reputation In the sight of God and man.
3:5 Trust in the with all your heart And do not lean on your own understanding.
3:6 In all your ways acknowledge Him, And He will make your paths straight.
3:7 Do not be wise in your own eyes; Fear the and turn away from evil.
3:8 It will be healing to your body And refreshment to your bones.
3:9 Honor the from your wealth, And from the first of all your produce;
3:10 Then your barns will be filled with plenty, And your vats will overflow with new wine.
3:11 My son, do not reject the discipline of the Or loathe His rebuke,
3:12 For whom the loves He disciplines, as a father the son in whom he delights.
3:13 Blessed is a person who finds wisdom, And one who obtains understanding.
3:14 For her profit is better than the profit of silver, And her produce better than gold.
3:15 She is more precious than jewels, And nothing you desire compares with her.
3:16 Long life is in her right hand; In her left hand are riches and honor.
3:17 Her ways are pleasant ways, And all her paths are peace.
3:18 She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, And happy are those who hold on to her.
3:19 The founded the earth by wisdom, He established the heavens by understanding.
3:20 By His knowledge the ocean depths were burst open, And the clouds drip with dew.
3:21 My son, they do not escape from your sight; Comply with sound wisdom and discretion,
3:22 And they will be life to your soul And adornment to your neck.
3:23 Then you will walk in your way securely, And your foot will not stumble.
3:24 When you lie down, you will not be afraid; When you lie down, your sleep will be sweet.
3:25 Do not be afraid of sudden danger, Nor of trouble from the wicked when it comes;
3:26 For the will be your confidence, And will keep your foot from being caught.
3:27 Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, When it is in your power to do .
3:28 Do not say to your neighbor, Go, and come back, And tomorrow I will give , When you have it with you.
3:29 Do not devise harm against your neighbor, While he lives securely beside you.
3:30 Do not contend with a person for no reason, If he has done you no harm.
3:31 Do not envy a violent person, And do not choose any of his ways.
3:32 For the devious are an abomination to the ; But He is intimate with the upright.
3:33 The curse of the is on the house of the wicked, But He blesses the home of the righteous.
3:34 Though He scoffs at the scoffers, Yet He gives grace to the needy.
3:35 The wise will inherit honor, But fools increase dishonor.
4:1 Listen, sons, to the instruction of a father, And pay attention so that you may gain understanding,
4:2 For I give you good teaching; Do not abandon my instruction.
4:3 When I was a son to my father, Tender and the only son in the sight of my mother,
4:4 He taught me and said to me, Let your heart take hold of my words; Keep my commandments and live;
4:5 Acquire wisdom! Acquire understanding! Do not forget nor turn away from the words of my mouth.
4:6 Do not abandon her, and she will guard you; Love her, and she will watch over you.
4:7 The beginning of wisdom : Acquire wisdom; And with all your possessions, acquire understanding.
4:8 Prize her, and she will exalt you; She will honor you if you embrace her.
4:9 She will place on your head a garland of grace; She will present you with a crown of beauty.
4:10 Listen, my son, and accept my sayings, And the years of your life will be many.
4:11 I have instructed you in the way of wisdom; I have led you in upright paths.
4:12 When you walk, your steps will not be hampered; And if you run, you will not stumble.
4:13 Take hold of instruction; do not let go. Guard her, for she is your life.
4:14 Do not enter the path of the wicked And do not proceed in the way of evil people.
4:15 Avoid it, do not pass by it; Turn away from it and pass on.
4:16 For they cannot sleep unless they do evil; And they are robbed of sleep unless they make stumble.
4:17 For they eat the bread of wickedness, And drink the wine of violence.
4:18 But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn That shines brighter and brighter until the full day.
4:19 The way of the wicked is like darkness; They do not know over what they stumble.
4:20 My son, pay attention to my words; Incline your ear to my sayings.
4:21 They are not to escape from your sight; Keep them in the midst of your heart.
4:22 For they are life to those who find them, And healing to all their body.
4:23 Watch over your heart with all diligence, For from it the springs of life.
4:24 Rid yourself of a deceitful mouth And keep devious speech far from you.
4:25 Let your eyes look directly ahead And let your gaze be fixed straight in front of you.
4:26 Watch the path of your feet, And all your ways will be established.
4:27 Do not turn to the right or to the left; Turn your foot from evil.
5:1 My son, pay attention to my wisdom, Incline your ear to my understanding,
5:2 So that you may maintain discretion And your lips may comply with knowledge.
5:3 For the lips of an adulteress drip honey, And her speech is smoother than oil;
5:4 But in the end she is bitter as wormwood, Sharp as a two-edged sword.
5:5 Her feet go down to death, Her steps take hold of Sheol.
5:6 She does not ponder the path of life; Her ways are unstable, she does not know .
5:7 Now then, sons, listen to me And do not turn away from the words of my mouth.
5:8 Keep your way far from her, And do not go near the door of her house,
5:9 Otherwise you will give your vigor to others, And your years to the cruel one;
5:10 And strangers will be filled with your strength, And your hard-earned possessions to the house of a foreigner;
5:11 And you will groan in the end, When your flesh and your body are consumed;
5:12 And you say, How I hated instruction! And my heart disdainfully rejected rebuke!
5:13 I did not listen to the voice of my teachers, Nor incline my ear to my instructors!
5:14 I was almost in total ruin In the midst of the assembly and congregation.
5:15 Drink water from your own cistern, And fresh water from your own well.
5:16 Should your springs overflow into the street, Streams of water in the public squares?
5:17 Let them be yours alone, And not for strangers with you.
5:18 Let your fountain be blessed, And rejoice in the wife of your youth.
5:19 a loving doe and a graceful mountain goat, Let her breasts satisfy you at all times; Be exhilarated always with her love.
5:20 For why should you, my son, be exhilarated with an adulteress, And embrace the breasts of a foreigner?
5:21 For the ways of everyone are before the eyes of the , And He observes all his paths.
5:22 His own wrongdoings will trap the wicked, And he will be held by the ropes of his sin.
5:23 He will die for lack of instruction, And in the greatness of his foolishness he will go astray.
6:1 My son, if you have become a guarantor for your neighbor, have given a handshake for a stranger,
6:2 you have been ensnared by the words of your mouth, caught by the words of your mouth,
6:3 Then do this, my son, and save yourself: Since you have come into the hand of your neighbor, Go, humble yourself, and be urgent with your neighbor .
6:4 Give no sleep to your eyes, Nor slumber to your eyelids;
6:5 Save yourself like a gazelle from hand, And like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
6:6 Go to the ant, you lazy one, Observe its ways and be wise,
6:7 Which, having no chief, Officer, or ruler,
6:8 Prepares its food in the summer gathers its provision in the harvest.
6:9 How long will you lie down, you lazy one? When will you arise from your sleep?
6:10 A little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to rest,
6:11 Then your poverty will come in like a drifter, And your need like an armed man.
6:12 A worthless person, a wicked man, Is one who walks with a perverse mouth,
6:13 Who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, Who points with his fingers;
6:14 Who, perversion in his heart, continually devises evil, Who spreads strife.
6:15 Therefore his disaster will come suddenly; Instantly he will be broken and there will be no healing.
6:16 There are six things that the hates, Seven that are an abomination to Him:
6:17 Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, And hands that shed innocent blood,
6:18 A heart that devises wicked plans, Feet that run rapidly to evil,
6:19 A false witness declares lies, And one who spreads strife among brothers.
6:20 My son, comply with the commandment of your father, And do not ignore the teaching of your mother;
6:21 Bind them continually on your heart; Tie them around your neck.
6:22 When you walk, they will guide you; When you sleep, they will watch over you; And when you awake, they will talk to you.
6:23 For the commandment is a lamp and the teaching is light; And rebukes for discipline are the way of life
6:24 To keep you from the evil woman, From the smooth tongue of the foreign woman.
6:25 Do not desire her beauty in your heart, Nor let her capture you with her eyelids.
6:26 For the price of a prostitute to a loaf of bread, And an adulteress hunts for a precious life.
6:27 Can anyone take fire in his lap And his clothes not be burned?
6:28 Or can a person walk on hot coals And his feet not be scorched?
6:29 So is the one who goes in to his neighbors wife; Whoever touches her will not go unpunished.
6:30 do not despise a thief if he steals To satisfy himself when he is hungry;
6:31 But when he is found, he must repay seven times ; He must give up all the property of his house.
6:32 One who commits adultery with a woman is lacking sense; He who would destroy himself commits it.
6:33 He will find wounds and disgrace, And his shame will not be removed.
6:34 For jealousy enrages a man, And he will not have compassion on the day of vengeance.
6:35 He will not accept any settlement, Nor will he be satisfied though you make a large gift.
7:1 My son, keep my words And treasure my commandments within you.
7:2 Keep my commandments and live, And my teaching as the apple of your eye.
7:3 Bind them on your fingers; Write them on the tablet of your heart.
7:4 Say to wisdom, You are my sister, And call understanding intimate friend,
7:5 So that they may keep you from an adulteress, From the foreigner who flatters with her words.
7:6 For at the window of my house I looked out through my lattice,
7:7 And I saw among the naive, discerned among the youths A young man lacking sense,
7:8 Passing through the street near her corner; And he walks along the way to her house,
7:9 In the twilight, in the evening, In the middle of the night and the darkness.
7:10 And behold, a woman to meet him, Dressed as a prostitute and cunning of heart.
7:11 She is boisterous and rebellious, Her feet do not remain at home;
7:12 now in the streets, now in the public squares, And lurks by every corner.
7:13 So she seizes him and kisses him, And with a brazen face she says to him:
7:14 I was due to offer peace offerings; Today I have paid my vows.
7:15 Therefore I have come out to meet you, To seek your presence diligently, and I have found you.
7:16 I have spread my couch with coverings, With colored linens of Egypt.
7:17 I have sprinkled my bed With myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
7:18 Come, lets drink our fill of love until morning; Lets delight ourselves with caresses.
7:19 For my husband is not at home; He has gone on a long journey.
7:20 He has taken a bag of money with him. At the full moon he will come home.
7:21 With her many persuasions she entices him; With her flattering lips she seduces him.
7:22 Suddenly he follows her As an ox goes to the slaughter, Or as walks in ankle bracelets to the discipline of a fool,
7:23 Until an arrow pierces through his liver; As a bird hurries to the snare, So he does not know that it his life.
7:24 Now therefore, sons, listen to me, And pay attention to the words of my mouth.
7:25 Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways, Do not stray into her paths.
7:26 For many are the victims she has brought to ruin, And numerous are all those slaughtered by her.
7:27 Her house is the way to Sheol, Descending to the chambers of death.
8:1 Does not wisdom call, And understanding raise her voice?
8:2 On top of the heights beside the way, Where the paths meet, she takes her stand;
8:3 Beside the gates, at the opening to the city, At the entrance of the doors, she cries out:
8:4 To you, people, I call, And my voice is to mankind.
8:5 You naive ones, understand prudence; And, you fools, understand wisdom!
8:6 Listen, for I will speak noble things; And the opening of my lips right things.
8:7 For my mouth will proclaim truth; And wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
8:8 All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; There is nothing crooked or perverted in them.
8:9 They are all straightforward to him who understands, And right to those who find knowledge.
8:10 Accept my instruction and not silver, And knowledge rather than choice gold.
8:11 For wisdom is better than jewels; And all desirable things cannot compare with her.
8:12 I, wisdom, dwell with prudence, And I find knowledge discretion.
8:13 The fear of the is to hate evil; Pride, arrogance, the evil way, And the perverted mouth, I hate.
8:14 Advice is mine and sound wisdom; I am understanding, power is mine.
8:15 By me kings reign, And rulers decree justice.
8:16 By me princes rule, and nobles, All who judge rightly.
8:17 I love those who love me; And those who diligently seek me will find me.
8:18 Riches and honor are with me, Enduring wealth and righteousness.
8:19 My fruit is better than gold, even pure gold; And my yield than choice silver.
8:20 I walk in the way of righteousness, In the midst of the paths of justice,
8:21 To endow those who love me with wealth, That I may fill their treasuries.
8:22 The created me at the beginning of His way, Before His works of old.
8:23 From eternity I was established, From the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth.
8:24 When there were no ocean depths, I was born, When there were no springs abounding with water.
8:25 Before the mountains were settled, Before the hills, I was born;
8:26 While He had not yet made the earth and the fields, Nor the first dust of the world.
8:27 When He established the heavens, I was there; When He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,
8:28 When He made firm the skies above, When the springs of the deep became fixed,
8:29 When He set a boundary for the sea So that the water would not violate His command, When He marked out the foundations of the earth;
8:30 Then I was beside Him, a master workman; And I was delight daily, Rejoicing always before Him,
8:31 Rejoicing in the world, His earth, And my delight in the sons of mankind.
8:32 Now then, sons, listen to me, For blessed are those who keep my ways.
8:33 Listen to instruction and be wise, And do not neglect .
8:34 Blessed is the person who listens to me, Watching daily at my gates, Waiting at my doorposts.
8:35 For one who finds me finds life, And obtains favor from the .
8:36 But one who sins against me injures himself; All those who hate me love death.
9:1 Wisdom has built her house, She has carved out her seven pillars;
9:2 She has prepared her food, she has mixed her wine; She has also set her table;
9:3 She has sent out her attendants, she calls out From the tops of the heights of the city:
9:4 Whoever is naive, let him turn in here! To him who lacks understanding she says,
9:5 Come, eat of my food And drink of the wine I have mixed.
9:6 Abandon foolishness and live, And proceed in the way of understanding.
9:7 One who corrects a scoffer gets dishonor for himself, And one who rebukes a wicked person insults for himself.
9:8 Do not rebuke a scoffer, or he will hate you; Rebuke a wise person and he will love you.
9:9 Give to a wise person and he will become still wiser; Teach a righteous person and he will increase insight.
9:10 The fear of the is the beginning of wisdom, And the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
9:11 For by me your days will be multiplied, And years of life will be added to you.
9:12 If you are wise, you are wise for yourself, And if you scoff, you alone will suffer .
9:13 A woman of foolishness is boisterous, a lack of understanding and knows nothing.
9:14 She sits at the doorway of her house, On a seat by the high places of the city,
9:15 Calling to those who pass by, Who are going straight on their paths:
9:16 Whoever is naive, let him turn in here, And to him who lacks understanding she says,
9:17 Stolen water is sweet; And bread in secret is pleasant.
9:18 But he does not know that the dead are there, her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
10:1 The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a father glad, But a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
10:2 Ill-gotten gains do not benefit, But righteousness rescues from death.
10:3 The will not allow the righteous to hunger, But He will reject the craving of the wicked.
10:4 Poor is one who works with a lazy hand, But the hand of the diligent makes rich.
10:5 He who gathers in summer is a son who acts wisely, he who sleeps in harvest is a son who acts shamefully.
10:6 Blessings are on the head of the righteous, But the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
10:7 The mentioning of the righteous is a blessing, But the name of the wicked will rot.
10:8 The wise of heart will receive commands, But a babbling fool will come to ruin.
10:9 One who walks in integrity walks securely, But one who perverts his ways will be found out.
10:10 He who winks the eye causes trouble, And a babbling fool will come to ruin.
10:11 The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, But the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
10:12 Hatred stirs up strife, But love covers all offenses.
10:13 On the lips of the discerning, wisdom is found, But a rod is for the back of him who has no sense.
10:14 Wise people store up knowledge, But with the mouth of the foolish, ruin is at hand.
10:15 The rich persons wealth is his fortress, The ruin of the poor is their poverty.
10:16 The wages of the righteous is life, The income of the wicked, punishment.
10:17 One who is the path of life follows instruction, But one who ignores a rebuke goes astray.
10:18 One who conceals hatred lying lips, And one who spreads slander is a fool.
10:19 When there are many words, wrongdoing is unavoidable, But one who restrains his lips is wise.
10:20 The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, The heart of the wicked is little.
10:21 The lips of the righteous feed many, But fools die for lack of understanding.
10:22 It is the blessing of the that makes rich, And He adds no sorrow to it.

25:1 These also are proverbs of Solomon which the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, transcribed.
25:2 It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
25:3 the heavens for height and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.
25:4 Take away the impurities from the silver, And there comes out a vessel for the smith;
25:5 Take away the wicked before the king, And his throne will be established in righteousness.
25:6 Do not boast in the presence of the king, And do not stand in the place as great people;
25:7 For it is better that it be said to you, Come up here, Than for you to be placed lower in the presence of the prince, Whom your eyes have seen.
25:8 Do not go out hastily to argue ; Otherwise, what will you do in the end, When your neighbor humiliates you?
25:9 Argue your case with your neighbor, And do not reveal the secret of another,
25:10 Or one who hears will put you to shame, And the evil report about you will not pass away.
25:11 apples of gold in settings of silver, Is a word spoken at the proper time.
25:12 an earring of gold and a jewelry piece of fine gold, Is a wise person who offers rebukes to a listening ear.
25:13 Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest Is a faithful messenger to those who send him, For he refreshes the soul of his masters.
25:14 clouds and wind without rain Is a person who boasts of his gifts falsely.
25:15 Through patience a ruler may be persuaded, And a gentle tongue breaks bone.
25:16 Have you found honey? Eat what you need, So that you do not have it in excess and vomit it.
25:17 Let your foot rarely be in your neighbors house, Or he will become weary of you and hate you.
25:18 a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow Is a person who gives false testimony against his neighbor.
25:19 a bad tooth and an unsteady foot Is confidence in a treacherous person in time of trouble.
25:20 one who takes off a garment on a cold day, vinegar on soda, Is one who sings songs to a troubled heart.
25:21 If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; And if he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
25:22 For you will heap burning coals on his head, And the will reward you.
25:23 The north wind brings rain, And a gossiping tongue an angry face.
25:24 It is better to live on a corner of the roof, Than in a house shared with a contentious woman.
25:25 cold water to a weary soul, So is good news from a distant land.
25:26 a trampled spring and a polluted well, is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.
25:27 It is not good to eat much honey, Nor is it glory to search out ones own glory.
25:28 a city that is broken into without walls is a person who has no self-control over his spirit.

30:1 The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, the pronouncement. The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
30:2 I am certainly more stupid than any man, And I do not have the understanding of a man;
30:3 Nor have I learned wisdom, Nor do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.
30:4 Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has wrapped the waters in His garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name or His Sons name? Surely you know!
30:5 Every word of God is pure; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
30:6 Do not add to His words Or He will rebuke you, and you will be proved a liar.
30:7 Two things I have asked of You; Do not refuse me before I die:
30:8 Keep deception and lies far from me, Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is my portion,
30:9 So that I will not be full and deny and say, Who is the ? And that I will not become impoverished and steal, And profane the name of my God.
30:10 Do not slander a slave to his master, Or he will curse you and you will be found guilty.
30:11 There is a kind who curses his father And does not bless his mother.
30:12 There is a kind who is pure in his own eyes, Yet is not washed from his filthiness.
30:13 There is a kind—oh how lofty are his eyes! And his eyelids are raised .
30:14 There is a kind whose teeth are swords And his jaw teeth knives, To devour the poor from the earth And the needy from among mankind.
30:15 The leech has two daughters: Give Give. There are three things that will not be satisfied, Four that will not say, Enough:
30:16 Sheol, the infertile womb, Earth that is never satisfied with water, And fire that never says, Enough.
30:17 The eye that mocks a father And scorns a mother, The ravens of the valley will pick it out, And the young eagles will eat it.
30:18 There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Four which I do not understand:
30:19 The way of the eagle in the sky, The way of a snake on a rock, The way of a ship in the middle of the sea, And the way of a man with a virgin.
30:20 This is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth, And says, I have done no wrong.
30:21 Under three things the earth quakes, And under four, it cannot endure:
30:22 Under a slave when he becomes king, And a fool when he is satisfied with food,
30:23 Under an unloved woman when she gets a husband, And a female servant when she dispossesses her mistress.
30:24 Four things are small on the earth, But they are exceedingly wise:
30:25 The ants are not a strong people, But they prepare their food in the summer;
30:26 The rock hyraxes are not a mighty people, Yet they make their houses in the rocks;
30:27 The locusts have no king, Yet all of them go out in ranks;
30:28 The lizard you may grasp with the hands, Yet it is in kings palaces.
30:29 There are three things which are stately in march, Even four which are stately when they walk:
30:30 The lion, is mighty among animals And does not retreat from anything,
30:31 The strutting rooster or the male goat, And a king army is with him.
30:32 If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, Or if you have plotted , hand on your mouth.
30:33 For the churning of milk produces butter, And pressing the nose produces blood; So the churning of anger produces strife.
31:1 The words of King Lemuel, the pronouncement which his mother taught him:
31:2 What, my son? And what, son of my womb? And what, son of my vows?
31:3 Do not give your strength to women, Or your ways to that which destroys kings.
31:4 It is not for kings, Lemuel, It is not for kings to drink wine, Or for rulers to desire intoxicating drink,
31:5 Otherwise they will drink and forget what is decreed, And pervert the rights of all the needy.
31:6 Give intoxicating drink to one who is perishing, And wine to one whose life is bitter.
31:7 Let him drink and forget his poverty, And remember his trouble no more.
31:8 Open your mouth for the people who cannot speak, For the rights of all the unfortunate.
31:9 Open your mouth, judge righteously, And defend the rights of the poor and needy.
31:10 An excellent wife, who can find ? For her worth is far above jewels.
31:11 The heart of her husband trusts in her, And he will have no lack of gain.
31:12 She does him good and not evil All the days of her life.
31:13 She looks for wool and linen, And works with her hands in delight.
31:14 She is like merchant ships; She brings her food from afar.
31:15 And she rises while it is still night And gives food to her household, And portions to her attendants.
31:16 She considers a field and buys it; From her earnings she plants a vineyard.
31:17 She surrounds her waist with strength And makes her arms strong.
31:18 She senses that her profit is good; Her lamp does not go out at night.
31:19 She stretches out her hands to the distaff, And her hands grasp the spindle.
31:20 She extends her hand to the poor, And she stretches out her hands to the needy.
31:21 She is not afraid of the snow for her household, For all her household are clothed with scarlet.
31:22 She makes coverings for herself; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
31:23 Her husband is known in the gates, When he sits among the elders of the land.
31:24 She makes linen garments and sells , And supplies belts to the tradesmen.
31:25 Strength and dignity are her clothing, And she smiles at the future.
31:26 She opens her mouth in wisdom, And the teaching of kindness is on her tongue.
31:27 She watches over the activities of her household, And does not eat the bread of idleness.
31:28 Her children rise up and bless her; Her husband , and he praises her, :
31:29 Many daughters have done nobly, But you excel them all.
31:30 Charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, a woman who fears the , she shall be praised.
