JOEL
1:1 The word of the that came to Joel, the son of Pethuel:
1:2 Hear this, you elders, And listen, all inhabitants of the land. Has this happened in your days, Or in your fathers days?
1:3 Tell your sons about it, And your sons their sons, And their sons the next generation.
1:4 What the gnawing locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten; And what the swarming locust has left, the creeping locust has eaten; And what the creeping locust has left, the stripping locust has eaten.
1:5 Awake, you heavy drinkers, and weep; And wail, all you wine drinkers, Because of the sweet wine, For it has been eliminated from your mouth.
1:6 For a nation has invaded my land, Mighty and without number; Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, And it has the jaws of a lioness.
1:7 It has made my vine a waste And my fig tree a stump. It has stripped them bare and hurled away; Their branches have become white.
1:8 Wail like a virgin clothed with sackcloth For the groom of her youth.
1:9 The grain offering and the drink offering have been cut off From the house of the . The priests mourn, The ministers of the .
1:10 The field is ruined, The land mourns; For the grain is ruined, The new wine has dried up, Fresh oil has failed.
1:11 Be ashamed, you farm workers, Wail, you vinedressers, For the wheat and the barley; Because the harvest of the field is destroyed.
1:12 The vine has dried up And the fig tree has withered; The pomegranate, the palm also, and the apple tree, All the trees of the field have dried up. Indeed, joy has dried up From the sons of mankind.
1:13 Put on And mourn, you priests; Wail, you ministers of the altar! Come, spend the night in sackcloth, You ministers of my God, For the grain offering and the drink offering Have been withheld from the house of your God.
1:14 Consecrate a fast, Proclaim a solemn assembly; Gather the elders all the inhabitants of the land To the house of the your God, And cry out to the .
1:15 Woe for the day! For the day of the is near, And it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
1:16 Has food not been cut off before our eyes, Joy and rejoicing from the house of our God?
1:17 The seeds have dried up under their shovels; The storehouses have become desolate, The grain silos are ruined, Because the grain has dried up.
1:18 How the animals have groaned! The herds of cattle have wandered aimlessly Because there is no pasture for them; Even the flocks of sheep have suffered.
1:19 To You, , I cry out; For fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, And the flame has burned up all the trees of the field.
1:20 Even the animals of the field pant for You; For the stream beds of water are dried up, And fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
2:1 Blow a trumpet in Zion, And sound an alarm on My holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, For the day of the is coming; Indeed, it is near,
2:2 A day of darkness and gloom, A day of clouds and thick darkness. As dawn is spread over the mountains, there is a great and mighty people; There has never been like it, Nor will there be again after it To the years of many generations.
2:3 A fire consumes before them, And behind them a flame devours. The land is like the Garden of Eden before them, But a desolate wilderness behind them, And nothing at all escapes them.
2:4 Their appearance is like the appearance of horses; And like war horses, so they run.
2:5 With a noise as of chariots They leap about on the tops of the mountains, Like the crackling of a flame of fire consuming the stubble, Like a mighty people drawn up for battle.
2:6 Before them the people are in anguish; All faces turn pale.
2:7 They run like warriors, They climb the wall like soldiers; And each of them marches in line, Nor do they lose their way.
2:8 They do not crowd each other, Every warrior of them marches in his path; When they burst through the defenses, They do not break ranks.
2:9 They storm the city, They run on the wall; They climb into the houses, They enter through the windows like a thief.
2:10 Before them the earth quakes, The heavens tremble, The sun and the moon become dark, And the stars lose their brightness.
2:11 The utters His voice before His army; His camp is indeed very great, For mighty is one who carries out His word. The day of the is indeed great and very awesome, And who can endure it?
2:12 Yet even now, declares the , Return to Me with all your heart, And with fasting, weeping, and mourning;
2:13 And tear your heart and not your garments. Now return to the your God, For He is gracious and compassionate, Slow to anger, abounding in mercy And relenting of catastrophe.
2:14 Who knows, He might turn and relent, And leave a blessing behind Him, a grain offering and a drink offering For the your God.
2:15 Blow a trumpet in Zion, Consecrate a fast, proclaim a solemn assembly,
2:16 Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, Assemble the elders, Gather the children and the nursing infants. Have the groom come out of his room And the bride out of her bridal chamber.
2:17 Let the priests, the ministers, Weep between the porch and the altar, And let them say, Spare Your people, , And do not make Your inheritance a disgrace, With the nations jeering at them. Why should among the peoples say, Where is their God?
2:18 Then the will be zealous for His land, And will have compassion for His people.
2:19 The will answer and say to His people, Behold, I am going to send you grain, new wine, and oil, And you will be satisfied with them; And I will never again make you a disgrace among the nations.
2:20 But I will remove the northern far from you, And I will drive it into a dry and desolate land, Its advance guard into the eastern sea, And its rear guard into the western sea. And its stench will ascend and its odor of decay will come up, Because it has done great things.
2:21 Do not fear, land; shout for joy and rejoice, For the has done great things.
2:22 Do not fear, animals of the field, For the pastures of the wilderness have turned green, For the tree has produced its fruit, The fig tree and the vine have yielded in full.
2:23 So shout for joy, you sons of Zion, And rejoice in the your God; For He has given you the early rain for vindication. And He has brought down for you the rain, The early and latter rain as before.
2:24 The threshing floors will be full of grain, And the vats will overflow with the new wine and oil.
2:25 Then I will compensate you for the years That the swarming locust has eaten, The creeping locust, the stripping locust, and the gnawing locust— My great army which I sent among you.
2:26 You will have plenty to eat and be satisfied, And you will praise the name of the your God, Who has dealt wondrously with you; Then My people will never be put to shame.
2:27 So you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, And that I am the your God And there is no other; And My people will never be put to shame.
2:28 It will come about after this That I will pour out My Spirit on all mankind; And your sons and your daughters will prophesy, Your old men will have dreams, Your young men will see visions.
2:29 And even on the male and female servants I will pour out My Spirit in those days.
2:30 I will display wonders in the sky and on the earth, Blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
2:31 The sun will be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the great and awesome day of the comes.
2:32 And it will come about everyone who calls on the name of the Will be saved; For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem There will be those who escape, Just as the has said, Even among the survivors whom the calls.

3:17 Then you will know that I am the your God, Dwelling on Zion, My holy mountain. So Jerusalem will be holy, And strangers will no longer pass through it.

AMOS
1:1 The words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
1:2 And he said, The roars from Zion, And from Jerusalem He utters His voice; And the shepherds pasture grounds mourn, And the summit of Carmel dries up.
1:3 This is what the says: For three offenses of Damascus, and for four, I will not revoke its , Because they threshed Gilead with iron sledges.
1:4 So I will send fire upon the house of Hazael, And it will consume the citadels of Ben-hadad.
1:5 I will also break the bar of Damascus, And eliminate inhabitant from the Valley of Aven, As well as him who holds the scepter, from Beth-eden; So the people of Aram will be exiled to Kir, Says the .

1:7 So I will send fire on the wall of Gaza And it will consume her citadels.
1:8 I will also eliminate inhabitant from Ashdod, As well as him who holds the scepter, from Ashkelon; And I will direct My power against Ekron, And the remnant of the Philistines will perish, Says the Lord .
1:9 This is what the says: For three offenses of Tyre, and for four, I will not revoke its , Because they turned an entire population over to Edom And did not remember covenant of brotherhood.
1:10 So I will send fire on the wall of Tyre, And it will consume her citadels.
1:11 This is what the says: For three offenses of Edom, and for four, I will not revoke its , Because he pursued his brother with the sword And stifled his compassion; His anger also tore continually, And he maintained his fury forever.
1:12 So I will send fire upon Teman And it will consume the citadels of Bozrah.
1:13 This is what the says: For three offenses of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not revoke its , Because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead In order to enlarge their borders.
1:14 So I will kindle a fire on the wall of Rabbah, And it will consume her citadels Amid war cries on the day of battle, amid a storm on the day of tempest.
1:15 Their king will go into exile, He and his princes together, says the .
2:1 This is what the says: For three offenses of Moab, and for four, I will not revoke its , Because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.

2:3 I will also eliminate the judge from her midst And slay all her leaders with him, says the .
2:4 This is what the says: For three offenses of Judah, and for four, I will not revoke its , Because they rejected the Law of the And have not kept His statutes; Their lies also have led them astray, Those which their fathers followed.
2:5 So I will send fire upon Judah, And it will consume the citadels of Jerusalem.
2:6 This is what the says: For three offenses of Israel, and for four, I will not revoke its , Because they sell the righteous for money, And the needy for a pair of sandals.
2:7 These who trample the head of the helpless to the dust of the earth Also divert the way of the humble; And a man and his father resort to the girl So as to profane My holy name.

2:9 Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, Though his height like the height of cedars And he strong as the oaks; I also destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
2:10 And it was I who brought you up from the land of Egypt, And led you in the wilderness for forty years So that you might take possession of the land of the Amorite.
2:11 Then I raised up some of your sons to be prophets, And some of your young men to be Nazirites. Is this not so, you sons of Israel? declares the .
2:12 But you made the Nazirites drink wine, And you commanded the prophets, saying, You shall not prophesy!
2:13 Behold, I am making a rut beneath you, Just as a wagon makes a rut when filled with sheaves.
2:14 Refuge will be lost from the swift, And the strong will not strengthen his power, Nor the warrior save his life.
2:15 The one who grasps the bow will not stand , The swift of foot will not escape, Nor will the one who rides the horse save his life.
2:16 Even the bravest among the warriors will flee naked on that day, declares the .
3:1 Hear this word which the has spoken against you, sons of Israel, against the entire family which He brought up from the land of Egypt:
3:2 You only have I known among all the families of the earth; Therefore I will punish you for all your wrongdoing.
3:3 Do two people walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
3:4 Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl from his den unless he has captured ?
3:5 Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when there is no device in it? Does a trap spring up from the earth when it captures nothing at all?
3:6 If a trumpet is blown in a city, will the people not tremble? If a disaster occurs in a city, has the not brought it about?
3:7 Certainly the Lord does nothing Unless He reveals His secret plan To His servants the prophets.

5:2 She has fallen, she will not rise again— The virgin Israel. She lies unnoticed on her land; There is no one to raise her up.
5:3 For this is what the Lord says: The city which goes forth a thousand Will have a hundred left, And the one which goes forth a hundred Will have ten left to the house of Israel.
5:4 For this is what the says to the house of Israel: Seek Me so that you may live.
5:5 But do not resort to Bethel And do not come to Gilgal, Nor cross over to Beersheba; For Gilgal will certainly go into captivity And Bethel will come to nothing.
5:6 Seek the so that you may live, Or He will break through like a fire, house of Joseph, And it will consume with no one to extinguish for Bethel,
5:7 those who turn justice into wormwood, And throw righteousness to the earth.
5:8 He who made the Pleiades and Orion, And changes deep darkness into morning, Who also darkens day night, Who calls for the waters of the sea And pours them out on the surface of the earth, The is His name.
5:9 He who makes destruction flash upon the strong, So that destruction comes upon the fortress.
5:10 They hate him who rebukes in the gate, And they despise him who speaks integrity.
5:11 Therefore because you impose heavy rent on the poor And take a tribute of grain from them, you have built houses of cut stone, Yet you will not live in them; You have planted beautiful vineyards, yet you will not drink their wine.
5:12 For I know your offenses are many and your sins are great, who are hostile to the righteous accept bribes, And turn away the poor at the gate.
5:13 Therefore at such a time the prudent person keeps quiet, because it is an evil time.

1:1 The word of the came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
1:2 Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and cry out against it, because their wickedness has come up before Me.
1:3 But Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the . So he went down to Joppa, found a ship that was going to Tarshish, paid the fare, and boarded it to go with them to Tarshish away from the presence of the .
1:4 However, the hurled a great wind on the sea and there was a great storm on the sea, so that the ship was about to break up.
1:5 Then the sailors became afraid and every man cried out to his god, and they hurled the cargo which was in the ship into the sea to lighten for them. But Jonah had gone below into the stern of the ship, had lain down, and fallen sound asleep.
1:6 So the captain approached him and said, How is it that you are sleeping? Get up, call on your god! Perhaps god will be concerned about us so that we will not perish.
1:7 And each man said to his mate, Come, lets cast lots so that we may find out on whose account this catastrophe us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
1:8 Then they said to him, Tell us, now! On whose account this catastrophe us? What is your occupation, and where do you come from? What is your country, and from what people are you?
1:9 So he said to them, I am a Hebrew, and I fear the God of heaven who made the sea and the dry land.
1:10 Then the men became extremely afraid, and they said to him, How could you do this? For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the , because he had told them.
1:11 So they said to him, What should we do to you so that the sea will become calm for us?—for the sea was becoming increasingly stormy.
1:12 And he said to them, Pick me up and hurl me into the sea. Then the sea will become calm for you, because I know that on account of me this great storm upon you.
1:13 However, the men rowed to return to land, but they could not, because the sea was becoming stormier against them.
1:14 Then they cried out to the and said, We earnestly pray, O , do not let us perish on account of this mans life, and do not put innocent blood on us; for You, , have done as You pleased.
1:15 So they picked up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped its raging.
1:16 Then the men became extremely afraid of the , and they offered a sacrifice to the and made vows.
1:17 And the designated a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the stomach of the fish for three days and three nights.

2:3 For You threw me into the deep, Into the heart of the seas, And the current flowed around me. All Your breakers and waves passed over me.
2:4 So I said, I have been cast out of Your sight. Nevertheless I will look again toward Your holy temple.
2:5 Water encompassed me to the point of death. The deep flowed around me, Seaweed was wrapped around my head.
2:6 I descended to the base of the mountains. The earth its bars around me forever, But You have brought up my life from the pit, my God.
2:7 While I was fainting away, I remembered the , And my prayer came to You, Into Your holy temple.
2:8 Those who are followers of worthless idols Abandon their faithfulness,
2:9 But I will sacrifice to You With a voice of thanksgiving. That which I have vowed I will pay. Salvation is from the .
2:10 Then the commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah up onto the dry land.

4:11 Should I not also have compassion on Nineveh, the great city in which there are more than 120,000 people, who do not know between their right hand and their left, many animals?

ZECHARIAH
1:1 In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the word of the came to Zechariah the prophet, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo saying,
1:2 The was very angry with your fathers.
1:3 Therefore say to them, This is what the of armies says: Return to Me, declares the of armies, that I may return to you, says the of armies.
1:4 Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying, This is what the of armies says: Return now from your evil ways and from your evil deeds. But they did not listen or pay attention to Me, declares the .
1:5 Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever?
1:6 But did My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, not overtake your fathers? Then they repented and said, Just as the of armies planned to do to us in accordance with our ways and our deeds, so He has dealt with us.
1:7 On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, that is, the month Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the came to Zechariah the prophet, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, as follows:
1:8 I saw at night, and behold, a man was riding on a red horse, and he was standing among the myrtle trees which were in the ravine, with red, sorrel, and white horses behind him.
1:9 Then I said, What are these, my lord? And the angel who was speaking with me said to me, I will show you what these are.
1:10 And the man who was standing among the myrtle trees responded and said, These are the ones whom the has sent to patrol the earth.
1:11 So they responded to the angel of the who was standing among the myrtle trees and said, We have patrolled the earth, and behold, all the earth is still and quiet.
1:12 Then the angel of the said, of armies, how long will You take no pity on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which You have been indignant for these seventy years?
1:13 And the responded to the angel who was speaking with me with gracious words, comforting words.
1:14 So the angel who was speaking with me said to me, Proclaim, saying, This is what the of armies says: I am exceedingly jealous for Jerusalem and Zion.
1:15 But I am very angry with the nations who are carefree; for while I was a little angry, they furthered the disaster.
1:16 Therefore the says this: I will return to Jerusalem with compassion; My house will be built in it, declares the of armies, and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.
1:17 Again, proclaim, saying, This is what the of armies says: My cities will again overflow with prosperity, and the will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.
1:18 Then I raised my eyes and looked, and behold, four horns.
1:19 So I said to the angel who was speaking with me, What are these? And he said to me, These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.
1:20 Then the showed me four craftsmen.
1:21 And I said, What are these coming to do? And he said, These are the horns that have scattered Judah so that no one lifts up his head; but these have come to frighten them, to throw down the horns of the nations who have lifted up horns against the land of Judah in order to scatter it.
2:1 Then I raised my eyes and looked, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand.
2:2 So I said, Where are you going? And he said to me, To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long it is.
2:3 And behold, the angel who had been speaking with me was going out, and another angel was going out to meet him.
2:4 And he said to him, Run, speak to that young man there, saying, Jerusalem will be inhabited as open country because of the multitude of people and cattle within it.
2:5 But I, declares the , will be a wall of fire to her on all sides, and I will be the glory in her midst.
2:6 You there! Flee from the land of the north, declares the , because I have spread you out like the four winds of the heavens, declares the .
2:7 You, Zion! Escape, you who are living the daughter of Babylon.
2:8 For the of armies says this: After glory He has sent me against the nations that plunder you, for the one who touches you, touches the apple of His eye.
2:9 For behold, I am going to wave My hand over them so that they will be plunder for their slaves. Then you will know that the of armies has sent Me.
2:10 Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for behold I am coming and I will dwell in your midst, declares the .
2:11 And many nations will join themselves to the on that day and will become My people. Then I will dwell in your midst, and you will know that the of armies has sent Me to you.
2:12 And the will possess Judah as His portion in the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem.
2:13 Be silent, all mankind, before the ; for He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.

5:1 Then I raised my eyes again and looked, and behold, a flying scroll.
5:2 And he said to me, What do you see? And I said, I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits, and its width ten cubits.
5:3 Then he said to me, This is the curse that is going forth over the face of the entire land; everyone who steals certainly will be purged away according to the writing on one side, and everyone who swears will be purged away according to the writing on the other side.
5:4 I will make it go forth, declares the of armies, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by My name; and it will spend the night within that house and destroy it with its timber and stones.
5:5 Then the angel who had been speaking with me went out and said to me, Now raise your eyes and see what this is that is going forth.
5:6 And I said, What is it? Then he said, This is the ephah going forth. Again he said, This is their appearance in all the land.
5:7 And behold, a lead cover was lifted up. , And this is a woman sitting inside the ephah.
5:8 Then he said, This is Wickedness! And he thrust her into the middle of the ephah and threw the lead weight on its opening.
5:9 Then I raised my eyes and looked, and there two women were coming out with the wind in their wings; and they had wings like the wings of the stork, and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heavens.
5:10 So I said to the angel who was speaking with me, Where are they taking the ephah?
5:11 Then he said to me, To build a temple for her in the land of Shinar; and when it is prepared, she will be set there on her own pedestal.

6:2 With the first chariot red horses, with the second chariot black horses,
6:3 with the third chariot white horses, and with the fourth chariot strong spotted horses.
6:4 So I responded and said to the angel who was speaking with me, What are these, my lord?
6:5 The angel replied to me, These are the four spirits of heaven, going out after taking their stand before the Lord of all the earth,
6:6 with one of which the black horses are going out to the north country; and the white ones are to go out after them, while the spotted ones are to go out to the south country.
6:7 When the strong ones went out, they were eager to go to patrol the earth. And He said, Go, patrol the earth. So they patrolled the earth.
6:8 Then He called out to me and spoke to me, saying, See, those who are going to the land of the north have appeased My wrath in the land of the north.

6:13 Yes, it is He who will build the temple of the , and He who will bear the majesty and sit and rule on His throne. So He will be a priest on His throne, and the counsel of peace will be between the two offices.
6:14 Now the crown will become a reminder in the temple of the to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen the son of Zephaniah.
6:15 Those who are far away will come and build the temple of the . Then you will know that the of armies has sent me to you. And it will take place if you completely obey the your God.

8:15 so I have again determined in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not fear!
8:16 These are the things which you shall do: speak the truth to one another; judge with truth and judgment for peace at your gates.
8:17 Also let none of you devise evil in your heart against another, and do not love perjury; for all these are what I hate, declares the .

11:6 For I will no longer have compassion for the inhabitants of the land, declares the ; but behold, I will let the people fall, each into anothers power and into the power of his king; and they will crush the land, and I will not rescue from their power.

11:8 Then I did away with the three shepherds in one month, for my soul was impatient with them, and their soul also was tired of me.
11:9 Then I said, I will not pasture you. What is to die, let it die, and what is to perish, let it perish; and let those who are left eat one anothers flesh.
11:10 And I took my staff Favor and cut it in pieces, to break my covenant which I had made with all the peoples.
11:11 So it was broken on that day, and so the afflicted of the flock who were watching me realized that it was the word of the .
11:12 And I said to them, If it is good in your sight, give my wages; but if not, never mind! So they weighed out thirty of silver as my wages.
11:13 Then the said to me, Throw it to the potter, magnificent price at which I was valued by them. So I took the thirty of silver and threw them to the potter the house of the .
11:14 Then I cut in pieces my second staff Union, to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
11:15 And the said to me, Take again for yourself the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
11:16 For behold, I am going to raise up a shepherd in the land who will not care for the perishing, seek the scattered, heal the broken, provide for the one who is exhausted, but will devour the flesh of the fat and tear off their hoofs.
11:17 Woe to the worthless shepherd Who abandons the flock! A sword will be on his arm And on his right eye! His arm will be totally withered, And his right eye will be blind.

14:13 And it will come about on that day that a great panic from the will fall on them; and they will seize one anothers hand, and the hand of one will be raised against the hand of another.
14:14 Judah also will fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered, gold, silver, and garments in great abundance.
14:15 And just like this plague, there will be a plague on the horse, the mule, the camel, the donkey, and all the cattle that will be in those camps.
14:16 Then it will come about that any who are left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up from year to year to worship the King, the of armies, and to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
14:17 And it will be that whichever of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the of armies, there will be no rain on them.
14:18 And if the family of Egypt does not go up or enter, then no on them; it will be the plague with which the strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
14:19 This will be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.

MALACHI
1:1 The pronouncement of the word of the to Israel through Malachi:
1:2 I have loved you, says the . But you say, How have You loved us? Esau not Jacobs brother? declares the . Yet I have loved Jacob;
1:3 but I have hated Esau, and I have made his mountains a desolation and his inheritance to the jackals of the wilderness.
1:4 Though Edom says, We have been beaten down, but we will return and build up the ruins; this is what the of armies says: They may build, but I will tear down; and will call them the territory of wickedness, and the people with whom the is indignant forever.
1:5 And your eyes will see , and you will say, The be exalted beyond the border of Israel!
1:6 A son honors father, and a servant his master. Then if I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is My respect? says the of armies to you, the priests who despise My name! But you say, How have we despised Your name?
1:7 presenting defiled food upon My altar. But you say, How have we defiled You? In that you say, The table of the is to be despised.
1:8 And when you present a blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? Or when you present a lame or sick , is it not evil? So offer it to your governor! Would he be pleased with you, or would he receive you kindly? says the of armies.
1:9 But now, do indeed plead for Gods favor, so that He will be gracious to us. With such an offering on your part, will He receive any of you kindly? says the of armies.
1:10 If only there were one among you who would shut the gates, so that you would not kindle My altar for nothing! I am not pleased with you, says the of armies, nor will I accept an offering from your hand.
1:11 For from the rising of the sun even to its setting, My name great among the nations, and in every place frankincense is going to be offered to My name, and a grain offering pure; for My name great among the nations, says the of armies.
1:12 But you are profaning it by your saying, The table of the Lord is defiled, and as for its fruit, its food is to be despised.
1:13 You also say, See, how tiresome it is! And you view it as trivial, says the of armies, and you bring what was taken by robbery and lame or sick; so you bring the offering! Should I accept it from your hand? says the .
1:14 But cursed be the swindler who has a male in his flock and vows , but sacrifices a blemished to the Lord, for I am a great King, says the of armies, and My name is feared among the nations.
2:1 And now, this commandment is for you, the priests.
2:2 If you do not listen, and if you do not take it to heart to give honor to My name, says the of armies, then I will send the curse upon you and I will curse your blessings; and indeed, I have cursed them , because you are not taking to heart.
2:3 Behold, I am going to rebuke your descendants, and I will spread dung on your faces, the dung of your feasts; and you will be taken away with it.
2:4 Then you will know that I have sent this commandment to you, so that My covenant may continue with Levi, says the of armies.
2:5 My covenant with him was life and peace, and I gave them to him reverence; so he revered Me and was in awe of My name.
2:6 True instruction was in his mouth and injustice was not found on his lips; he walked with Me in peace and justice, and he turned many back from wrongdoing.
2:7 For the lips of a priest should maintain knowledge, and should seek instruction from his mouth; for he is the messenger of the of armies.
2:8 But as for you, you have turned aside from the way; you have caused many to stumble by the instruction; you have ruined the covenant of Levi, says the of armies.
2:9 So I also have made you despised and of low reputation in the view of all the people, since you are not keeping My ways but are showing partiality in the instruction.
2:10 Do we not all have one Father? Is it not one God has created us? Why do we deal treacherously, each against his brother so as to profane the covenant of our fathers?
2:11 Judah has dealt treacherously, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah has profaned the sanctuary of the which He loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
2:12 for the man who does this, may the eliminate from the tents of Jacob who is awake and answers, or who presents an offering to the of armies.
2:13 And this is another thing you do: you cover the altar of the with tears, with weeping and sighing, because He no longer gives attention to the offering or accepts favor from your hand.
2:14 Yet you say, For what reason? Because the has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your marriage companion and your wife by covenant.
2:15 But not one has done who has a remnant of the Spirit. And why the one? He was seeking a godly offspring. Be careful then about your spirit, and none deals treacherously against the wife of your youth.
2:16 For I hate divorce, says the , the God of Israel, and him who covers his garment with violence, says the of armies. So be careful about your spirit, that you do not deal treacherously.
2:17 You have wearied the with your words. Yet you say, How have we wearied ? In that you say, Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the , and He delights in them, or, Where is the God of justice?
3:1 Behold, I am sending My messenger, and he will clear a way before Me. And the Lord, whom you are seeking, will suddenly come to His temple; and the messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight, behold, He is coming, says the of armies.
3:2 But who can endure the day of His coming? And who can stand when He appears? For He is like a refiners fire, and like launderers soap.
3:3 And He will sit as a smelter and purifier of silver, and He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, so that they may present to the offerings in righteousness.
3:4 Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the as in the days of old, and as in former years.
3:5 Then I will come near to you for judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, the adulterers, against those who swear falsely, those who oppress the wage earner in his wages the widow or the orphan, and those who turn away the stranger and do not fear Me, says the of armies.
3:6 For I, the , do not change; therefore you, the sons of Jacob, have not come to an end.
3:7 From the days of your fathers you have turned away from My statutes and have not kept . Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the of armies. But you say, How shall we return?
3:8 Would anyone rob God? Yet you are robbing Me! But you say, How have we robbed You? tithes and offerings.
3:9 You are cursed with a curse, for you are robbing Me, the entire nation !
3:10 Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in My house, and put Me to the test now in this, says the of armies, if I do not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out for you a blessing until it overflows.
3:11 Then I will rebuke the devourer for you, so that it will not destroy the fruit of your ground; nor will the vine in the field prove fruitless to you, says the of armies.
3:12 All the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a delightful land, says the of armies.
3:13 Your words have been arrogant against Me, says the . Yet you say, What have we spoken against You?
3:14 You have said, It is pointless to serve God; and what benefit that we have done what He required, and that we have walked in mourning before the of armies?

3:18 So you will again distinguish between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not serve Him.
4:1 For behold, the day is coming, burning like a furnace; and all the arrogant and every evildoer will be chaff; and the day that is coming will set them ablaze, says the of armies, so that it will leave them neither root nor branches.
4:2 But for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings; and you will go forth and frolic like calves from the stall.

MATTHEW
1:1 The record of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham:
1:2 Abraham fathered Isaac, Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.
1:3 Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram.
1:4 Ram fathered Amminadab, Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
1:5 Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse.
1:6 Jesse fathered David the king. David fathered Solomon by her of Uriah.
1:7 Solomon fathered Rehoboam, Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asa.
1:8 Asa fathered Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah.
1:9 Uzziah fathered Jotham, Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah.
1:10 Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, Manasseh fathered Amon, and Amon fathered Josiah.
1:11 Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
1:12 After the deportation to Babylon: Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel.
1:13 Zerubbabel fathered Abihud, Abihud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor.
1:14 Azor fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud.
1:15 Eliud fathered Eleazar, Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob.
1:16 Jacob fathered Joseph the husband of Mary, by whom Jesus was born, who is called the Messiah.
1:17 So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to the Messiah, fourteen generations.
1:18 Now the birth of Jesus the Messiah was as follows: when His mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
1:19 And her husband Joseph, since he was a righteous man and did not want to disgrace her, planned to send her away secretly.
1:20 But when he had thought this over, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife; for the Child who has been conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
1:21 She will give birth to a Son; and you shall name Him Jesus, for He will save His people from their sins.
1:22 Now all this took place so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet would be fulfilled:
1:23 , , , which translated means, .
1:24 And Joseph awoke from his sleep and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took as his wife,
1:25 but kept her a virgin until she gave birth to a Son; and he named Him Jesus.

27:1 Now when morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people conferred together against Jesus to put Him to death;
27:2 and they bound Him and led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.
27:3 Then when Judas, who had betrayed Him, saw that He had been condemned, he felt remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
27:4 saying, I have sinned by betraying innocent blood. But they said, What to us? You shall see yourself!
27:5 And he threw the pieces of silver into the temple sanctuary and left; and he went away and hanged himself.
27:6 The chief priests took the pieces of silver and said, It is not lawful to put them in the temple treasury, since it is money paid for blood.
27:7 And they conferred together and with the money bought the Potters Field as a burial place for strangers.
27:8 For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
27:9 Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: , by the sons of Israel;
27:10 , .
27:11 Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned Him, saying, You are the King of the Jews? And Jesus said to him,
27:12 And while He was being accused by the chief priests and elders, He did not offer any answer.
27:13 Then Pilate said to Him, Do You not hear how many things they are testifying against You?
27:14 And He did not answer him in regard to even a single charge, so the governor was greatly amazed.
27:15 Now at Feast the governor was accustomed to release for the people one prisoner whom they wanted.
27:16 And at that time they were holding a notorious prisoner called Barabbas.
27:17 So when the people gathered together, Pilate said to them, Whom do you want me to release for you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?
27:18 For he knew that because of envy they had handed Him over.
27:19 And while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him , saying, nothing with that righteous Man; for last night I suffered greatly in a dream because of Him.
27:20 But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas, and to put Jesus to death.
27:21 And the governor said to them, Which of the two do you want me to release for you? And they said, Barabbas.
27:22 Pilate said to them, Then what shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ? They all said, Crucify Him!
27:23 But he said, Why, what evil has He done? Yet they kept shouting all the more, saying, Crucify Him!
27:24 Now when Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather that a riot was starting, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd, saying, I am innocent of this Mans blood; you yourselves shall see.
27:25 And all the people replied, His blood on us and on our children!
27:26 Then he released Barabbas for them; but after having Jesus flogged, he handed Him over to be crucified.
27:27 Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the Praetorium and gathered the whole cohort to Him.
27:28 And they stripped Him and put a red cloak on Him.
27:29 And after twisting together a crown of thorns, they put it on His head, and a reed in His right hand; and they knelt down before Him and mocked Him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!
27:30 And they spit on Him, and took the reed and beat Him on the head.
27:31 And after they had mocked Him, they took the cloak off Him and put His garments back on Him, and led Him away to crucify .
27:32 As they were coming out, they found a man of Cyrene named Simon, whom they compelled to carry His cross.
27:33 And when they came to a place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull,
27:34 they gave Him wine mixed with bile to drink; and after tasting , He was unwilling to drink .
27:35 And when they had crucified Him, they divided His garments among themselves by casting lots.
27:36 And sitting down, they to keep watch over Him there.
27:37 And above His head they put up the charge against Him which read, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
27:38 At that time two rebels were being crucified with Him, one on the right and one on the left.
27:39 And those passing by were speaking abusively to Him, shaking their heads,
27:40 and saying, You who destroy the temple and rebuild in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross.
27:41 In the same way the chief priests also, along with the scribes and elders, were mocking and saying,
27:42 He saved others; He cannot save Himself! He is the King of Israel; let Him now come down from the cross, and we will believe in Him.
27:43 ; now, ; for He said, I am the Son of God.
27:44 And the rebels who had been crucified with Him were also insulting Him in the same .
27:45 Now from the sixth hour darkness fell upon all the land until the ninth hour.
27:46 And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, that is,
27:47 And some of those who were standing there, when they heard it, said, This man is calling for Elijah.
27:48 And immediately one of them ran, and taking a sponge, he filled it with sour wine and put it on a reed, and gave Him a drink.
27:49 But the rest said, Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.
27:50 And Jesus cried out again with a loud voice, and gave up His spirit.
27:51 And behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom; and the earth shook and the rocks were split.
27:52 Also the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised;
27:53 and coming out of the tombs after His resurrection, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.
27:54 Now as for the centurion and those who were with him keeping guard over Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and the things that were happening, they became extremely frightened and said, Truly this was the Son of God!
27:55 And many women were there watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee while caring for Him.
27:56 Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
27:57 Now when it was evening, a rich man from Arimathea came, named Joseph, who himself had also become a disciple of Jesus.
27:58 This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be given .
27:59 And Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
27:60 and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock; and he rolled a large stone against the entrance of the tomb and went away.
27:61 And Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
27:62 Now on the next day, which is after the preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered together with Pilate,
27:63 and they said, Sir, we remember that when that deceiver was still alive, He said, After three days I am rising.
27:64 Therefore, give orders for the tomb to be made secure until the third day; otherwise, His disciples may come and steal Him, and say to the people, He has risen from the dead, and the last deception will be worse than the first.
27:65 Pilate said to them, You have a guard; go, make it secure as you know how.
27:66 And they went and made the tomb secure with the guard, sealing the stone.
28:1 Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the tomb.
28:2 And behold, a severe earthquake had occurred, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and came and rolled away the stone, and sat upon it.
28:3 And his appearance was like lightning, and his clothing as white as snow.
28:4 The guards shook from fear of him and became like dead men.
28:5 And the angel said to the women, Do not be afraid; for I know that you are looking for Jesus who has been crucified.
28:6 He is not here, for He has risen, just as He said. Come, see the place where He was lying.
28:7 And go quickly and tell His disciples that He has risen from the dead; and behold, He is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see Him; behold, I have told you.
28:8 And they left the tomb quickly with fear and great joy, and ran to report to His disciples.
28:9 And behold, Jesus met them and said, And they came up and took hold of His feet, and worshiped Him.

28:13 and said, You are to say, His disciples came at night and stole Him while we were asleep.

28:15 And they took the money and did as they had been instructed; and this story was widely spread among the Jews to this day.

1:4 John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
1:5 And all the country of Judea was going out to him, and all the people of Jerusalem; and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
1:6 John was clothed with camels hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his diet was locusts and wild honey.
1:7 And he was preaching, saying, After me One is coming who is mightier than I, and I am not fit to bend down and untie the straps of His sandals.
1:8 I baptized you with water; but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.
1:9 In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
1:10 And immediately coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens opening, and the Spirit, like a dove, descending upon Him;
1:11 and a voice came from the heavens: You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.
1:12 And immediately the Spirit brought Him out into the wilderness.
1:13 And He was in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted by Satan; and He was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving Him.
1:14 Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of God,

1:21 They went into Capernaum; and immediately on the Sabbath entered the synagogue and to teach.
1:22 And they were amazed at His teaching; for He was teaching them as having authority, and not as the scribes.
1:23 Just then there was a man in their synagogue with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,

1:28 Immediately the news about Him spread everywhere into all the surrounding region of Galilee.

1:30 Now Simons mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever; and they immediately spoke to Jesus about her.

5:1 They came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gerasenes.
5:2 When He got out of the boat, immediately a man from the tombs with an unclean spirit met Him.
5:3 He lived among the tombs; and no one was able to bind him anymore, not even with a chain,
5:4 because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles broken in pieces; and no one was strong enough to subdue him.
5:5 Constantly, night and day, he was screaming among the tombs and in the mountains, and cutting himself with stones.
5:6 Seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran up and bowed down before Him;
5:7 and shouting with a loud voice, he said, What business do You have with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore You by God, do not torment me!
5:8 For He had been saying to him,
5:9 And He was asking him, And he said to Him, My name is Legion, for we are many.
5:10 And he begged Him earnestly not to send them out of the region.
5:11 Now there was a large herd of pigs feeding nearby on the mountain.
5:12 And begged Him, saying, Send us into the pigs so that we may enter them.
5:13 gave them permission. And coming out, the unclean spirits entered the pigs; and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand ; and they were drowned in the sea.
5:14 Their herdsmen ran away and reported in the city and in the countryside. And came to see what it was that had happened.
5:15 And they came to Jesus and saw the man who had been demon-possessed sitting down, clothed and in his right mind, the man who had had the legion; and they became frightened.
5:16 Those who had seen described to them how it had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs.
5:17 And they began to beg Him to leave their region.
5:18 And as He was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was begging Him that he might accompany Him.
5:19 And He did not let him, but He said to him,
5:20 And he went away and began to proclaim in Decapolis what great things Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.
5:21 When Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him; and He stayed by the seashore.
5:22 And one of the synagogue officials, named Jairus, came, and upon seeing Him, fell at His feet
5:23 and pleaded with Him earnestly, saying, My little daughter is at the point of death; come and lay Your hands on her, so that she will get well and live.
5:24 And He went off with him; and a large crowd was following Him and pressing in on Him.
5:25 A woman who had had a hemorrhage for twelve years,
5:26 and had endured much at the hands of many physicians, and had spent all that she had and was not helped at all, but instead had become worse—

14:53 They led Jesus away to the high priest; and all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes gathered together.
14:54 And Peter had followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest; and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the fire.
14:55 Now the chief priests and the entire Council were trying to obtain testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, and they were not finding any.
14:56 For many people were giving false testimony against Him, and their testimonies were not consistent.
14:57 And some stood up and giving false testimony against Him, saying,
14:58 We heard Him say, I will destroy this temple that was made by hands, and in three days I will build another, made without hands.
14:59 And not even in this respect was their testimony consistent.
14:60 And the high priest stood up forward and questioned Jesus, saying, Do You not offer any answer for what these men are testifying against You?
14:61 But He kept silent and did not offer any answer. Again the high priest was questioning Him, and said to Him, Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed ?
14:62 And Jesus said,
14:63 Tearing his clothes, the high priest said, What further need do we have of witnesses?
14:64 You have heard the blasphemy; how does it seem to you? And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.
14:65 And some began to spit on Him, and to blindfold Him, and to beat Him with their fists and say to Him, Prophesy! Then the officers took custody of Him and slapped Him .
14:66 And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the slave women of the high priest came,
14:67 and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, You were with Jesus the Nazarene as well.
14:68 But he denied , saying, I neither know nor understand what you are talking about. And he went out onto the porch.
14:69 The slave woman saw him, and began once more to say to the bystanders, This man is of them!
14:70 But again he denied it. And after a little while the bystanders were again saying to Peter, You really are of them, for you are a Galilean as well.
14:71 But he began to curse and to swear, I do not know this Man of whom you speak!
14:72 And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered how Jesus had made the remark to him, And he hurried on and weep.
15:1 Early in the morning the chief priests with the elders, scribes, and the entire Council immediately held a consultation; and they bound Jesus and led Him away, and turned Him over to Pilate.
15:2 Pilate questioned Him: You are the King of the Jews? And He answered him,
15:3 And the chief priests accusing Him of many things.
15:4 But Pilate questioned Him again, saying, Do You offer nothing in answer? See how many charges they are bringing against You!
15:5 But Jesus said nothing further in answer, so Pilate was amazed.
15:6 Now at Feast he used to release for them one prisoner whom they requested.
15:7 And the one named Barabbas had been imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder in the revolt.
15:8 And the crowd went up and began asking as he had been accustomed to do for them.
15:9 Pilate answered them, saying, Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?
15:10 For he was aware that the chief priests had handed Him over because of envy.
15:11 But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to release Barabbas for them instead.
15:12 And responding again, Pilate said to them, Then what shall I do with Him whom you call the King of the Jews?
15:13 They shouted back, Crucify Him!
15:14 But Pilate said to them, Why, what evil has He done? But they shouted all the more, Crucify Him!
15:15 Intent on satisfying the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas for them, and after having Jesus flogged, he handed Him over to be crucified.
15:16 Now the soldiers took Him away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium), and they called together the whole cohort.
15:17 And they dressed Him in purple, and after twisting together a crown of thorns, they put it on Him;
15:18 and they began saluting Him: Hail, King of the Jews!
15:19 And they beat His head with a reed and spit on Him, and kneeling, they bowed down before Him.
15:20 And after they had mocked Him, they took the purple off Him and put His garments on Him. And they led Him out to crucify Him.
15:21 And they compelled a passer-by coming from the country, Simon of Cyrene (the father of Alexander and Rufus), to carry His cross.
15:22 Then they brought Him to the place Golgotha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.
15:23 And they tried to give Him wine mixed with myrrh; but He did not take .
15:24 And they crucified Him, and divided up His garments among themselves, casting lots for them what each man would take.
15:25 Now it was the third hour when they crucified Him.
15:26 The inscription of the charge against Him read, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
15:27 And they crucified two rebels with Him, one on His right and one on His left.
15:29 Those passing by were hurling abuse at Him, shaking their heads and saying, Ha! You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
15:30 save Yourself by coming down from the cross!
15:31 In the same way the chief priests also, along with the scribes, were mocking among themselves and saying, He saved others; He cannot save Himself!
15:32 Let Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe! Those who were crucified with Him were also insulting Him.
15:33 When the sixth hour came, darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour.
15:34 At the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, which is translated,
15:35 And when some of the bystanders heard , they saying, Look! He is calling for Elijah!
15:36 And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave Him a drink, saying, Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.
15:37 But Jesus let out a loud cry, and died.
15:38 And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
15:39 And when the centurion, who was standing right in front of Him, saw that He died in this way, he said, Truly this Man was the Son of God!
15:40 Now there were also women watching from a distance, among whom Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Less and Joses, and Salome.
15:41 When He was in Galilee, they used to follow Him and serve Him; and many other women who came up with Him to Jerusalem.
15:42 When evening had already come, since it was the preparation day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
15:43 Joseph of Arimathea came, a prominent member of the Council, who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God; and he gathered up courage and went in before Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.
15:44 Now Pilate wondered if He was dead by this time, and summoning the centurion, he questioned him as to whether He was already dead.
15:45 And after learning this from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
15:46 Joseph bought a linen cloth, took Him down, wrapped Him in the linen cloth, and laid Him in a tomb which had been cut out in the rock; and he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
15:47 Mary Magdalene and Mary the of Joses were watching where He was laid.

LUKE
1:1 Since many have undertaken to compile an account of the things accomplished among us,
1:2 just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word,
1:3 it seemed fitting to me as well, having investigated everything carefully from the beginning, to write for you in an orderly sequence, most excellent Theophilus;
1:4 so that you may know the exact truth about the things you have been taught.
1:5 In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah; and he had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
1:6 They were both righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and requirements of the Lord.
1:7 And they had no child, because Elizabeth was infertile, and they were both advanced in years.
1:8 Now it happened while he was performing his priestly service before God in the appointed order of his division,
1:9 according to the custom of the priestly office, he was chosen by lot to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
1:10 And the whole multitude of the people were in prayer outside at the hour of the incense offering.
1:11 Now an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.
1:12 Zechariah was troubled when he saw , and fear gripped him.
1:13 But the angel said to him, Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.
1:14 You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice over his birth.
1:15 For he will be great in the sight of the Lord; and he will drink no wine or liquor, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit while still in his mothers womb.
1:16 And he will turn many of the sons of Israel back to the Lord their God.
1:17 And he will go before Him in the spirit and power of Elijah, , and the disobedient to the attitude of the righteous, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
1:18 Zechariah said to the angel, How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in her years.
1:19 The angel answered and said to him, I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
1:20 And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day when these things take place, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.
1:21 And the people were waiting for Zechariah, and were wondering at his delay in the temple.
1:22 But when he came out, he was unable to speak to them; and they realized that he had seen a vision in the temple, and he made signs to them, and remained speechless.
1:23 When the days of his priestly service were concluded, he went back home.
1:24 Now after these days his wife Elizabeth became pregnant, and she kept herself in seclusion for five months, saying,
1:25 This is the way the Lord has dealt with me in the days when He looked upon , to take away my disgrace among people.
1:26 Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city in Galilee named Nazareth,
1:27 to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the descendants of David; and the virgins name was Mary.
1:28 And coming in, he said to her, Greetings, favored one! The Lord with you.
1:29 But she was very perplexed at statement, and was pondering what kind of greeting this was.
1:30 And the angel said to her, Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
1:31 And behold, you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and you shall name Him Jesus.
1:32 He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High; and the Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David;
1:33 and He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and His kingdom will have no end.
1:34 But Mary said to the angel, How will this be, since I am a virgin?
1:35 The angel answered and said to her, The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; for that reason also the holy Child will be called the Son of God.
1:36 And behold, even your relative Elizabeth herself has conceived a son in her old age, and she who was called infertile is now in her sixth month.
1:37 For nothing will be impossible with God.
1:38 And Mary said, Behold, the Lords bond-servant; may it be done to me according to your word. And the angel departed from her.
1:39 Now at this time Mary set out and went in a hurry to the hill country, to a city of Judah,
1:40 and she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
1:41 When Elizabeth heard Marys greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
1:42 And she cried out with a loud voice and said, Blessed you among women, and blessed the fruit of your womb!
1:43 And how has it happened to me that the mother of my Lord would come to me?
1:44 For behold, when the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby leaped in my womb for joy.
1:45 And blessed she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what had been spoken to her by the Lord.
1:46 And Mary said: My soul exalts the Lord,
1:47 And my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.
1:48 For He has had regard for the humble state of His bond-servant; For behold, from now all generations will call me blessed.
1:49 For the Mighty One has done great things for me; And holy is His name.
1:50 And His mercy is to generation after generation Toward those who fear Him.
1:51 He has done mighty deeds with His arm; He has scattered proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
1:52 He has brought down rulers from thrones, And has exalted those who were humble.
1:53 He has filled the hungry with good things, And sent the rich away empty-handed.
1:54 He has given help to His servant Israel, In remembrance of His mercy,
1:55 Just as He spoke to our fathers, To Abraham and his descendants forever.
1:56 Mary stayed with her about three months, and returned to her home.
1:57 Now the time had come for Elizabeth to give birth, and she gave birth to a son.
1:58 Her neighbors and her relatives heard that the Lord had displayed His great mercy toward her; and they were rejoicing with her.
1:59 And it happened that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to call him Zechariah, after his father.
1:60 And his mother responded and said, No indeed; but he shall be called John.
1:61 And they said to her, There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.
1:62 And they made signs to his father, as to what he wanted him called.
1:63 And he asked for a tablet and wrote as follows, His name is John. And they were all amazed.
1:64 And at once his mouth was opened and his tongue , and he speaking in praise of God.
1:65 And fear came on all those who lived around them; and all these matters were being talked about in the entire hill country of Judea.
1:66 All who heard kept in mind, saying, What then will this child be? For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him.
1:67 And his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
1:68 Blessed the Lord God of Israel, For He has visited and accomplished redemption for His people,
1:69 And has raised up a horn of salvation for us In the house of His servant David—
1:70 Just as He spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets from ancient times—
1:71 Salvation from our enemies, And from the hand of all who hate us;
1:72 To show mercy to our fathers, And to remember His holy covenant,
1:73 oath which He swore to our father Abraham,
1:74 To grant us that we, being rescued from the hand of enemies, Would serve Him without fear,
1:75 In holiness and righteousness before Him all our days.
1:76 And you, child, also will be called the prophet of the Most High; For you will go on before the Lord to prepare His ways;
1:77 To give His people knowledge of salvation By the forgiveness of their sins,
1:78 Because of the tender mercy of our God, With which the Sunrise from on high will visit us,
1:79 To shine on those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, To guide our feet into the way of peace.
1:80 Now the child grew and was becoming strong in spirit, and he lived in the deserts until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
2:1 Now in those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus, that a census be taken of all the inhabited earth.
2:2 This was the first census taken while Quirinius was governor of Syria.
2:3 And all were on their way to register for the census, each to his own city.
2:4 Now Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
2:5 in order to register along with Mary, who was betrothed to him, and was pregnant.
2:6 While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
2:7 And she gave birth to her firstborn son; and she wrapped Him in cloths, and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
2:8 In the same region there were shepherds staying out in the fields and keeping watch over their flock at night.
2:9 And an angel of the Lord stood near them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them; and they were terribly frightened.
2:10 And the angel said to them, Do not be afraid; for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be for all the people;
2:11 for today in the city of David there has been born for you a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
2:12 And this a sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.
2:13 And suddenly there appeared with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God and saying,
2:14 Glory to God in the highest, And on earth peace among people with whom He is pleased.
2:15 When the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds saying to one another, Lets go straight to Bethlehem, then, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.
2:16 And they came in a hurry and found their way to Mary and Joseph, and the baby as He lay in the manger.
2:17 When they had seen , they made known the statement which had been told them about this Child.
2:18 And all who heard it were amazed about the things which were told them by the shepherds.
2:19 But Mary treasured all these things, pondering them in her heart.
2:20 And the shepherds went back, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as had been told them.
2:21 And when eight days were completed so that it was time for His circumcision, He was also named Jesus, the given by the angel before He was conceived in the womb.
2:22 And when the days for their purification according to the Law of Moses were completed, they brought Him up to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord
2:23 (as it is written in the Law of the Lord: ),
2:24 and to offer a sacrifice according to what has been stated in the Law of the Lord: A .
2:25 And there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon; and this man was righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
2:26 And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lords Christ.
2:27 And he came by the Spirit into the temple; and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to carry out for Him the custom of the Law,
2:28 then he took Him in his arms, and blessed God, and said,
2:29 Now, Lord, You are letting Your bond-servant depart in peace, According to Your word;
2:30 For my eyes have seen Your salvation,
2:31 Which You have prepared in the presence of all the peoples:
2:32 A light for revelation for the Gentiles, And the glory of Your people Israel.
2:33 And His father and mother were amazed at the things which were being said about Him.
2:34 And Simeon blessed them and said to His mother Mary, Behold, this is appointed for the fall and rise of many in Israel, and as a sign to be opposed—
2:35 and a sword will pierce your own soul—to the end that thoughts from many hearts may be revealed.
2:36 And there was a prophetess, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in years and had lived with husband for seven years after her marriage,
2:37 and as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She did not leave the temple , serving night and day with fasts and prayers.
2:38 And at that very moment she came up and giving thanks to God, and continued to speak about Him to all those who were looking forward to the redemption of Jerusalem.
2:39 And when had completed everything in accordance with the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own city of Nazareth.
2:40 Now the Child continued to grow and to become strong, increasing in wisdom; and the favor of God was upon Him.
2:41 His parents went to Jerusalem every year at the Feast of the Passover.
2:42 And when He was twelve years old, they went up according to the custom of the feast;
2:43 and as they were returning, after spending the full number of days , the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware .
2:44 Instead, they thought that He was in the caravan, and they went a days journey; and they looking for Him among their relatives and acquaintances.
2:45 And when they did not find Him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for Him.
2:46 Then, after three days they found Him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
2:47 And all who heard Him were amazed at His understanding and His answers.
2:48 When saw Him, they were bewildered; and His mother said to Him, Son, why have You treated us this way? Behold, Your father and I have been anxiously looking for You!
2:49 And He said to them,
2:50 And they on their part did not understand the statement which He had made to them.
2:51 And He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and He continued to be subject to them; and His mother treasured all things in her heart.
2:52 And Jesus kept increasing in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and people.
3:1 Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee and his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
3:2 in the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
3:3 And he came into all the region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins;
3:4 as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: , , !
3:5 , ; , ;
3:6 !
3:7 So he was saying to the crowds who were going out to be baptized by him, You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
3:8 Therefore produce fruits that are consistent with repentance, and do not start saying to yourselves, We have Abraham father, for I say to you that from these stones God is able to raise up children for Abraham.
3:9 But indeed the axe is already being laid at the root of the trees; so every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
3:10 And the crowds were questioning him, saying, Then what are we to do?
3:11 And he would answer and say to them, The one who has two tunics is to share with the one who has none; and the one who has food is to do likewise.
3:12 Now even tax collectors came to be baptized, and they said to him, Teacher, what are we to do?
3:13 And he said to them, Collect no more than what you have been ordered to.
3:14 And soldiers also were questioning him, saying, What are we to do, we as well? And he said to them, Do not extort money from anyone, nor harass , and be content with your wages.
3:15 Now while the people were in a state of expectation and they all were thinking carefully in their hearts about John, whether he himself perhaps was the Christ,
3:16 John responded to them all, saying, As for me, I baptize you with water; but He is coming who is mightier than I, and I am not fit to untie the straps of His sandals; He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
3:17 His winnowing fork is in His hand to thoroughly clear His threshing floor, and to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
3:18 So with many other exhortations he preached the gospel to the people.
3:19 But when Herod the tetrarch was reprimanded by him regarding Herodias, his brothers wife, and regarding all the evil things which Herod had done,
3:20 also added this to them all: he locked John up in prison.
3:21 Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also was baptized, and while He was praying, heaven was opened,
3:22 and the Holy Spirit descended upon Him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: You are My beloved Son, in You I am well pleased.

1:2 He was in the beginning with God.
1:3 All things came into being through Him, and apart from Him not even one thing came into being that has come into being.
